Results Of 429 studies screened, 10 were included (5 RCTs, 5 comparative), yielding 50 dichotomous (e.g., progression to arthroplasty or adverse events) and 83 continuous (e.g., Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score subscales, International Knee Documentation committee scores, pain visual analog scale scores, etc.) outcomes. The median fragility index was 6 (interquartile range [IQR] 4-12.75) with median FQ of 0.031 (IQR 0.014-0.049). The median continuous fragility index was 18 (IQR 6.8-41.5) with median continuous FQ of 0.13 (IQR 0.084-0.16). Dichotomous outcomes from RCTs were significantly more fragile than those from comparative studies (RCT FQ = 0.021 vs 0.049; P = .010), whereas continuous outcome fragility did not differ significantly. Conclusions Studies comparing meniscal debridement with nonoperative management are statistically fragile, meaning that statistical significance could be reversed with only a small number of outcome changes, particularly for dichotomous outcomes. Continuous outcomes showed greater robustness but remained limited by loss to follow-up and study design. Level of evidence Level III, systematic review of Level I to III studies.

title: Prospective Polynomial Characterization of Tibial Plateau Geometry Shows No Association With Contralateral ACL Injury in Female Athletes.
authors: Dees A, Gardner-Morse M, Vacek P, Krug M, Pechstein A, Imhauser CW, Beynnon B.
abstract: Background Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries are common in athletic people, with young female athletes at particularly high risk. After ACL injury, reconstruction, and return to sport, many sustain contralateral ACL (CACL) injuries. While tibial plateau cartilage surface geometry has been associated with first-time ACL injury risk, its role in subsequent CACL injury remains unclear. Hypothesis The normal knee of female athletes who suffered a first-time ACL injury, underwent reconstruction, returned to preinjury activities and subsequently suffered a CACL injury will have tibial plateau cartilage surface geometry that is different compared with an equivalent population who did not sustain a subsequent CACL injury. Study design Prospective cohort study. Level of evidence Level 2. Methods A total of 199 subjects who suffered a first-time ACL injury, had reconstruction, returned to preinjury activities and had a contralateral knee that was normal underwent bilateral magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan acquisitions. Tibial plateau cartilage geometry was assessed on the uninjured, normal knees using T1-weighted Fast Field Echo MRI. Parasagittal slices at maximum cartilage concavity in medial and lateral compartments of the tibia were characterized by fitting fifth-order polynomials. Female athletes who sustained a CACL injury within 4 years of reconstruction and return to sport (n = 12) were matched and compared with a group of female athletes who did not sustain CACL injury (n = 24). Random coefficient mixed-effects regression was used to assess group differences in polynomial functions. Results No significant differences in tibial cartilage surface geometry were found between the first-time ACL and first-time ACL + CACL injury groups in the medial ( P = 0.23) and lateral ( P = 0.18) compartments. Conclusion These findings suggest that characterization of tibial plateau cartilage geometry in the normal knee of subjects who underwent reconstruction after a first-time ACL injury is insufficient to predict who will on go on to suffer a subsequent CACL injury. Clinical relevance More comprehensive predictive models incorporating anatomic, biomechanical, and psychological factors are likely needed to identify those at increased risk for CACL injury after a first-time ACL injury and reconstruction.

title: Perioperative neurocognitive outcomes after robot-assisted pelvic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of reported proportions, comparative risk and prognostic factors.
authors: Drobot RB, Skorupka JJ, Lipa M.
abstract: Delirium and cognitive decline may complicate recovery after robot-assisted pelvic surgery, but their frequency and relationship to positioning remain uncertain. We assessed reported proportions, comparative surgical risk and prognostic factors. PubMed, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched through 4 August 2026. Eligible adult robotic pelvic studies reported objective cognitive testing or delirium. Two reviewers performed original screening, extraction and question-specific bias appraisal. Post hoc logit random-effects meta-analyses summarized prospective cohorts using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals in R. Twenty-six reports represented 25 studies. Five cognitive cohorts (356 participants) yielded 29.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 20.2-39.8%); excluding Beck yielded 31.8% (20.7-45.4%). Three delirium cohorts (245 participants) yielded a descriptive model summary of 10.3% (2.2-37.0%). Individual delirium proportions were 8/82 (9.8%; exact 95% CI 4.3-18.3%), 4/80 (5.0%; 1.4-12.3%) and 14/83 (16.9%; 9.5-26.7%). The approximate 95% prediction interval from the delirium meta-analysis was very wide (<0.1-99.8%). The same-procedure prostatectomy comparison yielded an unadjusted risk ratio of 1.06 (0.73-1.55) for early cognitive decline. Comparative evidence was of low or very low certainty. Definitions, surveillance and selection limited interpretation; Trendelenburg-duration findings were inconsistent. These proportions describe selected study-defined outcomes. They do not establish attributable robotic or positioning risk, a safe exposure threshold, or benefit from horizontal breaks. Standardized prospective measurement is needed.

title: Long-term periprosthetic femoral bone loss after cementless total hip arthroplasty: natural history and response to late osteoporosis treatment.
authors: Ando W, Takao M, Hamada H, Uemura K, Takashima K, Sugano N.
abstract: Purpose The long-term course of periprosthetic bone mineral density (BMD) after cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) and BMD changes during late osteoporosis treatment remain unclear. Methods Fifty-eight hips in 44 patients underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) > 15 years after cementless THA using a proximally coated tapered stem. Longitudinal changes were assessed in 18 hips (12 patients) with serial DXA obtained within three months, at one year, and at a mean of 17.2 years postoperatively. For therapeutic analysis, ten hips (7 patients) with osteoporosis received zoledronic acid annually, together with daily eldecalcitol and calcium, for two years with serial DXA before treatment and during follow-up. Results At a mean of 17.2 years, lumbar spine BMD declined to 74.9% of baseline (P 0.05, vs lumbar spine). In contrast, proximal zones 1, 2, 6, and 7 showed significantly greater reductions (60.0%, 61.8%, 54.0%, and 30.8%, respectively; all P Conclusions Proximal periprosthetic bone loss was evident beyond 15 years after cementless THA, with the greatest reduction in Zone 7. Late osteoporosis treatment was associated with no significant further decline in periprosthetic BMD but did not reverse severe proximal bone loss.

title: Krackow Stitch Augmentation for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: Surgical Technique.
authors: Nakamura H, Mitsui Y, Abe R, Sakai S, Higuchi K, Yoshida T, Gotoh M.
abstract: Despite the advances in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair, postoperative structural failure remains a persistent problem. Retear patterns are commonly classified as type 1 failure, which is associated with the poor quality of the torn tendon edge, and type 2 failure, which occurs at the medial suture site owing to stress concentration within the repaired tendon. Consequently, we propose an arthroscopic medial augmentation technique using a suture tape-based Krackow construct placed medial to the footprint as an adjunct to conventional rotator cuff repair. By obtaining additional fixation in more medial tendon tissue, this technique may reduce dependence on a compromised tendon stump and may also help distribute the load away from the medial suture site. This Technical Note describes the surgical details of this augmentation method that is intended to provide additional tendon reinforcement and load sharing without altering the surgeon's preferred primary repair configuration.

title: Intrawound Vancomycin Powder in Posterior Lumbar Fusion: In Vitro Osteoblast Effects and Clinical Outcomes in a Historical-Control Cohort.
authors: Truumees H, Friedman LIN, Schmirler J, Sinclair S, Funk Z, Geerling DM, Spina NT, Spiker WR, Brodke DS, Lawrence BD, Karamian BA.
abstract: Study DesignRetrospective analysis.ObjectivesTo analyze the immediate post-operative effects on osteoblast activity, and long-term impact on bone healing, of intrawound vancomycin powder following posterior lumbar fusion (PLF).MethodsThis study had two phases: (1) an in vitro analysis of vancomycin effects on osteoblasts and (2) a retrospective chart review-spanning over a decade-analyzing outcomes of vancomycin use in PLF patients. Cellular metabolic and osteogenic activities were evaluated using well-established in vitro assays. The retrospective chart review included patients ages 18+ who underwent PLF (four levels or fewer) between January 2007-December 2015. Patients were divided into two groups: the pre-vancomycin group (PVG) and the vancomycin group (VG). Statistical analyses included descriptive and comparative analyses across groups.ResultsPhase One included 56 patients. Drain vancomycin concentrations peaked at POD 0, averaging 1253.67 ng/µL. Osteoblasts exposed to vancomycin concentrations of 1,250 ng/µL had significantly lower ALP activity compared to those exposed to 0, 245, 285, and 500 ng/µL (ps<0.05). Phase Two included 425 patients: 232 in the PVG and 193 in the VG. SSIs requiring debridement were observed in 3.02% of PVG patients compared to 2.07% of VG patients (p=0.761). There were no differences in pseudoarthrosis across cohorts (p=0.886), but lucency was more common in the VG (25.39%) than the PVG (11.64%; p<0.001).ConclusionsLocal drain concentrations of vancomycin decreased significantly across the postoperative period, suggesting its effects on osteoblasts are limited to the early inflammatory phase. In the long-term, intrawound vancomycin may not impact risk of SSI or pseudoarthrosis.

title: Favorable Short-Term Outcomes for Minced Cartilage Implantation in Cartilage Defects of the Knee: A Systematic Review.
authors: Tham A, Alzobi O, Rubin J, AlSaadi A, Al-Shammari F, Emanuel KS, Kekhoffs GMMJ, Kennedy JG.
abstract: Purpose To systematically review available data on clinical, structural, and safety outcomes after minced cartilage implantation (MCI) in knee cartilage defects and to descriptively compare outcomes with microfracture and other treatment modalities. Methods A systematic search following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines was performed in 3 databases evaluating MCI for knee cartilage defects. Extracted variables included patient characteristics, patient-reported outcomes, structural outcomes, and complications at 12 and ≥24 months. Outcomes were summarized descriptively using study-level data without pooled estimates. Results Seventeen studies comprising 493 patients treated with MCI were included, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months and a maximum of 60 months and mean defect sizes ranging from 2.53 to 4.5 cm 2 (International Cartilage Repair Society grade III-IV). Improvement in International Knee Documentation Committee scores ranged from 21.6 to 40.8 points at 12 months and 19.7 to 43.9 points at ≥24 months. Visual analog scale pain scores improved from a range of 3.5 to 7.2 preoperatively to a range of 0.6 to 2.5 points at both timepoints. Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score total and subscale scores showed improvement across all reporting studies. Magnetic Resonance Observation of Cartilage Repair Tissue scores ranged from the low 50s to mid-80s at both timepoints. Comparative studies with microfracture displayed mixed findings of functional scores at 12 months and numerically higher International Knee Documentation Committee scores at ≥24 months. Complication rates ranged from 0% to 14% at 12 months and 0% to 8% at 24 months. Conclusions In this study, MCI is associated with improvements in pain and knee function, favorable structural repair, and low reported complication rates at short- to midterm follow-up. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level I to IV studies.

title: Explainable radiomics and clinical models for prediction of total knee arthroplasty in knee osteoarthritis: data from Osteoarthritis Initiative.
authors: Pooyan A, Alipour E, Eshraghi N, Mirghaderi P, Pishgar F, Nyflot MJ, Park C, Kim HS, Thurlow PC, Link TM, Chalian M.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate MRI radiomics models, with and without clinical variables, for predicting total knee arthroplasty (TKA) within 9 years in patients with knee osteoarthritis. Materials and methods This retrospective exploratory study included 507 participants from the Osteoarthritis Initiative-Zuse Institute Berlin dataset with manually segmented knee MRIs; 66 underwent TKA. Four hundred radiomics features from bone and cartilage were combined with 13 clinical variables. Logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated using radiomics-only, clinical-only, and combined feature sets in an 80/20 development-holdout analysis and stratified nested cross-validation. Preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning were restricted to training folds. Results On the held-out test set, radiomics-only LASSO had the highest observed AUC-ROC of 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.88), followed closely by combined LASSO at 0.75 (0.61-0.87). Combined logistic regression and XGBoost achieved AUC-ROC values of 0.73 (0.60-0.86) and 0.72 (0.57-0.84), respectively. Differences among the leading models were modest. In nested cross-validation, combined LASSO showed the highest discrimination (AUC-ROC, 0.786 [0.722-0.841]; AUC-PR, 0.343 [0.239-0.451]; F1 score, 0.405 [0.321-0.481]), with modest improvement over radiomics-only LASSO (AUC-ROC, 0.781 [0.717-0.834]). Consistently retained predictors included femoral bone sphericity, femoral cartilage first-order skewness, and WOMAC disability. Conclusion MRI radiomics features, alone or combined with clinical variables, showed potential for predicting TKA risk. Performance differences among leading models were modest, and these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical application.

title: Effects of hyponatremia on bone repair in mice.
authors: Yamao H, Mizukami Y, Kishigami R, Kawao N, Okumoto K, Kaji H.
abstract: Hyponatremia, a common electrolyte abnormality in older patients, is associated with osteopenia and an increased risk of fracture. However, the effects of hyponatremia on bone repair remain unclear. In the present study, we investigated the effects of 1-desamino-8-D-arginine vasopressin (dDAVP)-induced chronic hyponatremia on bone repair after creation of a femoral bone defect. A total of 54 nine-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to the control group (n = 24) or the dDAVP-treated group (n = 30), and dDAVP was administered for 6 weeks before bone defect creation. Serum sodium levels were 120.2 ± 1.2 mEq/L in dDAVP-treated mice. dDAVP administration significantly suppressed bone volume fraction (BV/TV) in the bone defect region 10 days after femoral bone injury creation in mice, compared to control (23.7 ± 3.4 vs. 39.0 ± 4.1%, p = 0.021). Histological analyses showed that dDAVP significantly reduced the numbers of alkaline phosphatase (ALP)-positive osteoblastic cells and both CD31- and endomucin-positive blood vessels in the bone injury region 10 days after femoral bone defect creation (ALP: 24.7 ± 2.0 vs. 30.0 ± 2.0 cells/mm, p = 0.043; CD31/endomucin: 107 ± 15 vs. 151 ± 9 vessels/mm 2 , p = 0.016). Moreover, dDAVP significantly suppressed the mRNA expression of osteogenic genes, such as Runx2, Osterix, ALP, osteocalcin, and type 1 collagen in the bone injury region. In in vitro studies, low sodium concentrations (125 mEq/L), but not dDAVP treatment, significantly suppressed ALP activity as well as the mRNA levels of Osterix and ALP enhanced by bone morphogenetic protein-2 in ST-2 cells (p = 0.029). Moreover, low sodium concentrations, but not dDAVP treatment, significantly suppressed mineralization in mouse primary osteoblasts (p = 0.007). In conclusion, we demonstrated for the first time that dDAVP-induced chronic hyponatremia delays bone repair after a femoral bone defect in mice, at least partly through impaired osteoblast differentiation and angiogenesis.

title: Differences in Imaging and Surgical Management of Patellar Instability in Children and Adolescents Between Asia-Pacific and North America: A Systematic Review.
authors: Heng WT, Zhang S, Tan SHS, Hui JHP.
abstract: Purpose To compare diagnostic imaging practices and surgical interventions for patellofemoral instability in children and adolescents between Asia-Pacific and North America. Methods A systematic review was conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guideline. Inclusion criteria were original surgical studies of patellofemoral instability in children or adolescent patients, with a sample size of more than 5, from either Asia-Pacific or North America. Exclusion criteria included nonoriginal research, cadaveric/biomechanical studies, imaging-only reports, unrelated diagnoses, and adult-only cohorts. Data were synthesized descriptively by region. Results Sixty-eight studies were included, with 15 from Asia-Pacific and 53 from North America. The total sample size was 397 patients in Asia-Pacific and 10,376 in North America. Magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and radiographs were reported more consistently in Asia-Pacific studies, whereas North American studies more frequently reported medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction and tibial tubercle osteotomy. Asia-Pacific studies more commonly reported medial soft-tissue tightening, lateral retinacular release, trochleoplasty, and medial hemiepiphysiodesis. The included literature was predominantly Level III to IV evidence, with marked heterogeneity in study design, populations, and procedures. Conclusions This systematic review identified reported regional variation in the imaging and surgical management of patellofemoral instability in children and adolescents between Asia-Pacific and North America. Asia-Pacific studies more frequently described computed tomography use and soft-tissue procedures, whereas North American studies more frequently reported medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction and tibial tubercle osteotomy. These findings should be interpreted with caution because of heterogeneity in study design and a marked imbalance in sample size between regions. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level I to IV studies.

title: Comparison of Wiltse Approach-Based Invasion-Controlled Surgery With Traditional Open Surgery for Thoracolumbar Spinal Metastases Within the NOMS Framework.
authors: Wang P, Shen Z, Zhou J, Xu G, Yuan H, Xu M, Xiao J, Xu W.
abstract: Objectives To compare Wiltse approach-based invasion-controlled surgery (ICS) with traditional open surgery (TOS) for symptomatic thoracolumbar spinal metastases within the Neurologic, Oncologic, Mechanical, and Systemic (NOMS) framework, focusing on perioperative burden, postoperative recovery, neurological outcomes, pain, and QLQ-BM22 domains. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 30 patients undergoing ICS and 60 patients undergoing TOS from January 25, 2019, to January 25, 2022. Perioperative, neurological, and patient-reported outcomes were compared, including operative burden, postoperative recovery, complications, ASIA grade, VAS score, and QLQ-BM22 domains. Continuous variables were assessed with Shapiro-Wilk tests and compared using two-sided Welch independent-samples t-tests; categorical variables were analyzed using Pearson's χ 2 or exact tests, and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for sensitivity analyses when patient-level data were available. Results The groups differed in preoperative ASIA distribution (p = 0.036). Compared with TOS, ICS was associated with shorter operative time (p Conclusions Wiltse approach-based ICS was associated with reduced operative burden and faster postoperative recovery, without evidence of a worse postoperative neurological distribution in the unadjusted comparison. ICS may be considered a complementary muscle-sparing option within NOMS-guided management for appropriately selected patients who require posterior stabilization with decompression or separation. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: ChiCTR1800016921.

title: Bullous Pemphigoid Following Total Hip Arthroplasty With Subsequent Prosthetic Joint Infection: Literature Review.
authors: Naim Rodriguez N, Saudan M, Bartolone P.
abstract: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is an autoimmune blistering disorder potentially triggered by surgery or perioperative medications. An 88-year-old man underwent uncomplicated anterior total hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture. Five weeks later, pruritic tense bullae appeared around the operative site. Histology demonstrated subepidermal blistering with eosinophils; direct immunofluorescence revealed linear basement-membrane IgG and C3, confirming BP. Immunosuppression was initiated. Five weeks thereafter, fever, erythema, tenderness, and effusion developed. Purulent aspirate grew Staphylococcus aureus, confirming prosthetic joint infection. Despite urgent debridement and intravenous antibiotics, persistent infection required explantation and antibiotic spacer placement three weeks later. After clinical improvement over three months, planned second-stage reimplantation was completed without BP recurrence. To our knowledge, this first reported complication highlights prompt dermatologic diagnosis, judicious immunosuppression, and multidisciplinary management following arthroplasty.

title: BoneNet: a framework for predicting MSK-FE-estimated femoral neck strain patterns from exercise IMU data.
authors: Altai Z, Hollinger D, Phillips ATM, Moran J, Zhai X, Mei Q, Liew BXW.
abstract: Femoral neck fractures pose serious risks, particularly in osteoporosis, highlighting the need for effective bone-strengthening exercises and practical, non-invasive assessment of femoral loading. This study quantifies exercise-induced strains and presents BoneNet, an explainable convolutional neural network that predicts femoral neck strains from inertial measurement unit (IMU) data, offering a potential approach for estimating musculoskeletal-finite element (MSK-FE)-derived femoral neck strain patterns. Data were collected from 40 healthy participants (40.3 ± 13.1 years), with 37 included in the FE and BoneNet analyses. MSK-FE models estimated femoral neck strains during walking, running, jumping and hopping at varying intensities. BoneNet used IMU accelerometer and gyroscope signals from seven- and three-sensor configurations with participant-grouped cross-validation. Fast running yielded 3731 ± 1472 µε (tensile) and - 9541 ± 3610 µε (compressive), with walking strain magnitudes 47% lower for both tensile and compressive strains. Unilateral hopping with longer ground contact yielded 3003 ± 1189 µε and - 7755 ± 3040 µε, with walking strain magnitudes 34% and 35% lower, respectively. Walking generally produced higher strains than all other exercises. Using seven IMUs, BoneNet achieved correlations of r = 0.75-0.94 for five exercises, while squat jumps showed weak correlations (r = 0.27-0.36) and high relative RMSE (54.9-59.4%). Three IMUs showed comparable correlations, but squat-jump errors remained high (relative RMSE 56.0-61.2%). Running at all intensities and unilateral hopping with longer ground contact may have implications for bone adaptation, while BoneNet shows potential for estimating strain patterns rather than validated absolute values.

title: Barriers to Radiation Protection Among Female Orthopedic Trainees: A Survey of Current Residents.
authors: Orringer M, Ramos V, Blumenthal S.
abstract: Objective Higher rates of breast cancer have been linked previously to occupational radiation hazards in the orthopaedic operating room. However, increased awareness regarding the elevated risk of cancer among female orthopaedic surgeons has not necessarily resulted in improved access to appropriately fitting protective lead garments. The primary objective of this study was to survey female residents on their access to one-piece versus two-piece lead garments. Secondary objectives included identifying descriptive barriers and regional differences in access. Design An anonymous survey was distributed via email, word of mouth, and orthopaedic surgery social media groups to trainees around the United States. Statistical analysis was performed using SAS Enterprise 8.3, with descriptive analysis conducted for reported barriers to access. Setting Electronic RedCap-based survey study. Participants Eighty-nine female resident trainees completed the survey, including 58 junior (PGY1-3) and 31 senior residents (PGY4-5). Results 98% of surveyed residents endorsed awareness of the increased breast cancer risk among female orthopaedic surgeons, and 63% of residents reported concerns regarding elevated risk due to inadequate radiation protection. 39% of participants reported anxiety related to lead accessibility. Only 46% of surveyed residents were provided custom garments from their institution, and 51% of respondents reported financial barriers to obtaining appropriately fitting lead. Common barriers included inadequate financial resources, storage or ability to transport between sites, and lack of awareness among program leadership. Conclusions Access to lead protective garments varies between institutions, inducing significant financial and psychological stress among female trainees. Provision of protective garments ranges widely, with less than half of surveyed residents receiving appropriately fitted lead. Cost remains the most frequently cited barrier to adequate radiation protection.

title: Arthroscopic Flipped Coracoid Transfer (Laterjet Procedure) With Endobutton Fixation for Anterior Shoulder Instability.
authors: Patzer T, Zolle M, Hofmaier A.
abstract: Glenoid bone loss is one of the most important risk factors for recurrent anterior shoulder instability. Transfer of the coracoid process is a well-established procedure for this. In the classic Latarjet procedure, the subscapularis tendon is split and the graft is fixed with screws. The subscapularis split may weaken the tendon, and screws may contact the humeral head after partial graft osteolysis, leading to cartilage damage. To avoid splitting the subscapularis, the "flipped" coracoid transfer technique has been described, in which the coracoid process is passed above the subscapularis and the superior instead of the inferior surface of the graft is fixed to the anterior glenoid. The origin of the conjoint tendon is located superiorly. The "flipped" technique uses a U-tape cerclage with 2 glenoid tunnels drilled posteriorly, thereby reducing the risk of axillary nerve injury anteroinferiorly. The tape obtains the risk of suture cutout with insufficient primary stability. Therefore, the present "flipped" technique uses 2 double Endobuttons with a sliding, self-locking Nice knot posteriorly. This fixation has been shown to provide sufficient stability. The technique is performed fully arthroscopically except for coracoid osteotomy which is performed through a 4-cm miniopen incision.

title: An exploratory study on the influence of CT slice spacing on the positioning accuracy of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments designed for a distal radius osteotomy.
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
authors: Gryska E, Axelsson P, Libberecht K, Stor Swinkels C, Björkman A.
abstract: Background Computed tomography (CT) images with slice spacing up to 3 mm are generally sufficient for accurate 3D reconstructions of patient anatomy. For designing patient-specific instruments, particularly for forearm and wrist osteotomies, higher-resolution imaging (slice spacing of 0.4-1.25 mm) is commonly used. However, it remains unclear whether CT slice spacing meaningfully affects the surface fit of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments. This in-vitro study quantified the impact of CT slice spacing on the positional accuracy of instruments for the distal radius. Methods Data from 12 patients were analysed. Each had a high-resolution CT image (0.625 mm slice spacing), from which a reference 3D radius model and a patient-specific instrument were designed. The original images were downsampled to slice spacings of 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.875, and 2.5 mm to generate corresponding radius models and instrument bases. An experienced hand surgeon, blinded to slice spacing, fixated each 3D-printed instrument base onto its reference 3D-printed radius model in a simulated surgery. The assembled constructs were scanned, and the translation and rotation deviations of each lower-resolution instrument position were measured relative to the gold-standard instrument from the original scan. Results Mean rotational deviations across all slice spacings remained consistently low ( Conclusion CT slice spacing had a generally small effect on the positional accuracy of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments for the distal radius in vitro. These results indicate that clinically acceptable instrument accuracy may be achieved across a broad range of CT slice spacing commonly used in musculoskeletal imaging, potentially reducing the need for high-resolution protocols in selected clinical scenarios.

title: Age as an Independent Predictor of MCID Achievement and Patient Satisfaction Following Elective Cervical Spine Surgery.
authors: Joaquin TA, McDevitt JW, Ferreira AC, Bennett CF, Compton TM, Herrera DE, Staub JR, Hrvojevic L, Hoyt AK, Colman MW, Hsu WK, Divi SN, Patel AA.
abstract: Study DesignRetrospective Cohort Study.ObjectivesTo determine whether age independently predicts minimal clinically important difference (MCID) achievement in physical function (PF) and pain interference (PI) following elective cervical spine surgery, and to examine how age-related expectation-achievement discordance influences postoperative satisfaction.MethodsAdult patients undergoing elective cervical spine surgery at a single academic center (2022-2025) were included if they completed preoperative and 12-month Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) PF and PI computerized adaptive tests (CATs) and a preoperative expected outcome assessment. MCID was defined as an 8-point PROMIS T-score change. Patients were stratified into five age groups (<45, 45-54, 55-64, 65-74, ≥75). Multivariable logistic regression modeled age continuously, adjusting for BMI, levels fused, sex, smoking, revision status, and pathology.ResultsAmong 129 patients, MCID achievement declined significantly with age for both domains (trend p<0.001). Each additional year of age independently reduced odds of achieving MCID (PF: OR 0.95, p=0.007; PI: OR 0.96, p=0.02). Adjusted MCID probability fell below 50% at 45.9 years for PF and 49.1 years for PI. The expectation-achievement gap was widest in middle-aged patients (45-64), who held expectations comparable to younger patients yet achieved outcomes consistent with older cohorts. Among non-achievers, satisfaction increased with advancing age (trend p=0.05 for PF).ConclusionsAfter adjusting for the covariates assessed, age continuously and independently predicts failure to achieve MCID after cervical spine surgery, with probability falling to 50% by the late forties. Despite this, older non-achievers report high satisfaction, suggesting MCID is not a universal prerequisite for surgical success and underscoring the need for age-specific preoperative counseling.

title: Ultrasonographic assessment of transversus abdominis activation during core training tasks and its association with trunk stability in young adults with post-stroke hemiplegia.
authors: Hu N, Huang F, Gu S, Zhang T, Zhang Q, Wang Y, Miao P.
abstract: Objective This study used ultrasound to investigate the acute transversus abdominis (TrA) activation characteristics during core muscle task performance and explore its relationship with trunk stability in young adults with post-stroke hemiplegia. Method 15 young adults with post-stroke hemiplegia and 22 healthy controls were recruited. Ultrasonography was used to assess TrA thickness and contraction during core muscle training tasks, including quiet and deep exhalation in supine (quiet 0, deep 0) with hips and knees flexed at 90° (quiet 90, deep 90), crunch (crunch 90), and ball-squeezing crunch (ball crunch 90). Correlations between TrA thickness or contraction and trunk stability (Modified Trunk Impairment Scale, mTIS) and activities of daily living (MBI) were examined in patients. Results 1. Bilateral asymmetry: Healthy controls had a thicker right TrA (p 0.05). 2. Comparison between healthy and patients: Healthy controls had a thicker TrA across all tasks (all p ≤ 0.05) and a higher TrA contraction ratio during deep 0 (left, p = 0.000, right, p Conclusion Young adults with post-stroke hemiplegia exhibited right-sided TrA dominance, particularly during the ball crunch 90° task. Among all tested movements, both crunch 90° and ball-crunch 90° elicited the greatest acute TrA activation. Ambulation capacity showed exploratory positive trends in relation to TrA contractility, trunk stability, and activities of daily living. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Ultra-early perioperative Guillain-Barré syndrome following traumatic fracture surgery: a case report and literature review.
authors: Zhao Y, Wang Z, Dong J, Chang M, Liu D, Wang Z, Zhou N.
abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy most commonly associated with preceding infection. Perioperative GBS is rare, particularly when neurological symptoms develop within 24 h after surgery. We report a 46-year-old man who developed rapidly progressive symmetrical limb weakness and sensory symptoms approximately 15 h after surgical fixation of traumatic fractures, including a right intertrochanteric femur fracture and a right calcaneal fracture. His neurological condition rapidly progressed to bulbar dysfunction, respiratory failure, and cardiac arrest. Electrophysiological examination revealed motor and sensory peripheral nerve abnormalities with mixed demyelinating and axonal features, supporting a clinical diagnosis of GBS, although definitive electrophysiological subtype classification was not possible. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was not performed because the family declined lumbar puncture due to concerns about bleeding risk during postoperative anticoagulation, limiting diagnostic certainty. Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy was initiated following clinical suspicion of GBS, alongside respiratory support and comprehensive rehabilitation. At transfer to a higher-level hospital, the patient remained severely neurologically impaired. According to information provided by the patient during a telephone follow-up approximately six months later, outpatient assessment at the receiving hospital indicated substantial neurological recovery, including independent ambulation and recovery of swallowing and bowel and bladder function; these findings were not independently verified by the authors. Although GBS developed shortly after trauma and surgery, a causal relationship between these events and the syndrome could not be established. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of very early postoperative GBS and underscores the importance of prompt recognition, appropriate electrophysiological evaluation, and timely consideration of immunotherapy in patients with unexplained progressive postoperative weakness.

title: Systemic Physiological Impact on Cervical Bone Quality Measurements: A Comparative Analysis of Cervical Vertebral Bone Quality Scores and Hounsfield Units.
authors: Qi F, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Feng T, Wang L, Liu X.
abstract: Objectives Cervical vertebral bone quality (C-VBQ) scores and cervical Hounsfield units (C-HU) demonstrate significant potential for bone quality assessment. However, research on the influence of physiological factors on these metrics remains limited. This study aims to: quantify segment- and gender-specific associations between various physiological factors and both measures. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 512 patients with cervical spondylotic myelopathy from January 2023 to January 2024, with a mean age of 63.04 ± 8.86 years. Differences between male and female groups were compared using independent sample t-tests, Welch's corrected t-test, Mann-Whitney U tests, and chi-square tests, as appropriate for variable type and distribution. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses, as well as multiple linear regression, were performed to clarify the associations between physiological factors and these two measurement methods across different cervical segments and genders. Results At the C4/5 segment, the C-VBQ score showed the strongest correlations with age, fasting blood glucose (FBG), glycated albumin (GA), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), conjugated bilirubin (CB), unconjugated bilirubin, total bilirubin, and serum calcium, while C-HU correlated most strongly with age, serum phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), CB, GA, and APTT (all p Conclusions The associations of bilirubin metabolism and glucose metabolism indicators with both methods were more pronounced at the C4/5 segment and among female populations, and the C-VBQ score appeared to be more sensitive.

title: Survival and functional outcomes in surgically treated pelvic chondrosarcoma: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
authors: Deventer N, Theil JC, Gosheger G, Deventer N, de Vaal M, Rachbauer A, Schulze M, Budny T.
abstract: Background Pelvic chondrosarcoma is a rare malignant bone tumor associated with challenging surgical management, high morbidity, and variable oncological outcomes. Because of its rarity, prognostic factors and functional outcomes remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated survival, prognostic factors, complications, and functional outcomes following surgical treatment of primary and locally recurrent pelvic chondrosarcoma. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 54 consecutive patients who underwent surgery for primary pelvic chondrosarcoma (n = 37) or locally recurrent disease (n = 17) at a single tertiary musculoskeletal oncology center between 2007 and 2020. Patients undergoing surgery for metastatic pelvic lesions were excluded. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Univariable Cox regression analyses and an exploratory multivariable model including age and tumor grade were performed. Functional outcome was assessed using the Musculoskeletal Tumor Society (MSTS) score. Results The mean clinical follow-up was 31.7 months. During follow-up, 22 patients died. Estimated overall survival was 80.3% at 1 year (95% CI 65.4-89.3%), 65.1% at 3 years (95% CI 48.6-77.4%), and 48.8% at 5 years (95% CI 30.6-64.8%). Increasing age was independently associated with a higher hazard of death (adjusted HR per year, 1.048; 95% CI, 1.014-1.083; p = 0.0052); tumor grade also showed an association (adjusted HR per grade, 1.802; 95% CI, 1.006-3.228; p = 0.0476). Functional outcome was available for 27 patients, with a mean MSTS score of 11.6 ± 5.8. Revision surgery was required in 38 patients (70.4%). Conclusions Surgical treatment of pelvic chondrosarcoma is associated with considerable morbidity and impaired functional outcome. In this cohort, age and tumor grade were associated with overall survival in an exploratory model. These findings should be interpreted in light of the retrospective design, limited cohort size, and relatively short follow-up. Clinical trial number not applicable.

title: Successful limb salvage and favorable functional outcome after subtotal scapulectomy and custom 3D-printed reconstruction in a 14-year-old with high-grade osteosarcoma.
authors: Blecha O, Belzarena AC, Lesensky J.
abstract: Scapular reconstruction following tumor resection remains a surgical challenge because of the scapula's essential role in upper extremity biomechanics. Although patient-specific implants have expanded reconstructive options, achieving durable fixation and functional restoration remains difficult. A 14-year-old male with high-grade osteosarcoma of the scapular wing underwent limb-salvage surgery using a custom 3D-printed endoprosthesis. Preoperative planning incorporated dedicated software and patient-specific cutting guides. Wide resection preserved a small portion of the glenoid and the native glenohumeral joint to maximize postoperative function. At 3 months, radiographs demonstrated early osseointegration. The patient achieved 100° of active shoulder abduction without scapular winging or instability. At 2 years, he maintained near-full motion, demonstrated stable implant integration without loosening or recurrence, and returned to sports and daily activities with minimal limitations. Patient-specific scapular endoprosthetic reconstruction can achieve excellent oncologic and functional outcomes after subtotal scapulectomy, even in very young patients with high-grade malignancy.

title: Stabilization of canine ilial body fractures using an anatomically contoured locking iliac plate: A short retrospective case series.
authors: Ferrigno CRA, de Magalhaes Ferraz VC, Chiaramonte A, Woo G, Boone A, Bevelock T, Weaver C, Kasmark L, Ferreira MP.
abstract: Objective To report the clinical outcomes of canine ilial body fractures stabilized with a newly designed, anatomically 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate. Study design Retrospective case series. Animals Ten client-owned dogs treated between 2023 and 2024. Methods Medical records and orthogonal pelvic radiographs were reviewed for signalment, fracture configuration, surgical findings, time to radiographic union, postoperative sacral index (SI), complications, and limb function. Continuous variables were summarized as median (interquartile range, IQR), mean ± standard deviation (SD), and range; categorical variables as counts and proportions with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Median age was 3.5 years (IQR 2.25-5.75; range 0.75-10) and median body weight 32.0 kg (IQR 28.3-38.5; range 21-52). Median time to radiographic union was 60 days (IQR 60-62.5; range 60-97). Six of ten dogs (60%; 95% CI 31.3-83.2%) achieved union by 60 days. One dog (10%; 95% CI 1.8-40.4%) developed a cutaneous fistula that resolved within seven days of plate removal after fracture healing. The SI was within normal limits in all dogs at final follow-up, and limb function was normal in 10/10 dogs. Conclusions In this small case series, stabilization of canine ilial body fractures with the dedicated 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate was associated with reliable bone healing, a low complication rate, and preserved pelvic canal dimensions. Clinical significance: A dedicated, anatomically contoured locking plate is a feasible option for fixation of canine ilial body fractures, conforming to the iliac surface with no or minimal intraoperative contouring and allowing straightforward application. Larger comparative studies are warranted.

title: Robotics in endoscopic spine surgery: a scoping review of clinical applications, workflow integration, and patient outcomes.
authors: Serdoura F, Gonçalves Dos Santos D, Correia MC, Silva JD, Nunes B.
abstract: Robotic and endoscopic technologies are increasingly being combined in spine surgery, yet the clinical literature remains fragmented across procedures, platforms, and robotic functions. We conducted a scoping review to map clinical applications of robot-assisted endoscopic spine surgery, describe how robotic systems are incorporated into endoscopic workflows, and summarize the technical, perioperative, and patient-centered outcomes reported to date. PubMed and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Human clinical reports were eligible when endoscopy constituted part of the operative visualization or working approach and a robotic system directly assisted the same spinal procedure. Study selection was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Of 374 records identified, 122 duplicates were removed and 252 records were screened. Sixty-six reports were sought, 13 were not retrieved, 53 full texts were assessed, and 24 studies were included. The evidence comprised 11 comparative studies, four uncontrolled clinical series, and nine case-based or technical clinical reports. Applications ranged from discectomy and decompression to interbody fusion, pars repair, infection, trauma, and thoracic or craniovertebral procedures. Robots were used for trajectory planning, localization, percutaneous access, guidewire or pedicle screw placement, drilling, endoscope stabilization, and interbody instrumentation. Comparative studies most often showed gains in fluoroscopy use, access efficiency, or instrumentation accuracy; patient-reported outcomes were usually similar between groups. Robotic-endoscopic integration is clinically feasible across an expanding range of spinal procedures, but its patient-level value remains incompletely defined.

title: Osteogenesis imperfecta caused by ultra-rare variants in IFITM5: New cases and molecular studies on missense variants.
authors: Ordaz-Robles T, Tiranardi M, Ríos-Ruíz JG, Bardai G, Rauch F, Moffatt P.
abstract: Variants in IFITM5 are a unique cause of osteogenesis imperfecta (OI). The recurrent c.-14C > T leads to classical OI type V, whereas missense variants are considerably rarer and associated with a distinct phenotype. Here we present 3 Mexican boys with IFITM5 missense variants and investigated their cellular and molecular consequences in vitro. Individual 1 (p.Ser40Trp) had a history of 30 fractures, primarily involving both femurs, leading to bone deformities and short stature (height z-score - 3.1). Individual 2 (p.Ser40Leu) had bilateral lower extremity deformities at birth and sustained 15 fractures postnatally. Individual 3 (p.Asn48Ser) experienced 6 fractures, all involving the left femur. None exhibited the hallmark features of OI type V, including hyperplastic callus formation or interosseous membrane calcification. Transient transfection in MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts showed that all 3 IFITM5 variants were aberrantly retained intracellularly, although total protein levels remained normal. In a surrogate MEF2-based luciferase assay in MLO-A5 osteocytic cells, the variants failed to elicit a signaling response and appear to exert a dominant negative effects on wild type IFITM5 when co-expressed. Consistently, plasma membrane localization of the wild type protein was reduced in the presence of the mutants. Additional variants identified in ClinVar and gnomAD (p.Ser40Pro, p.Asn48Asp, and p.Asn48His) showed similar intracellular retention and loss of activity. Biochemical analyses indicated loss of palmitoylation of the adjacent cysteine residues. These findings expand the clinical spectrum of IFITM5 missense variants and support a dominant negative-like disease mechanism distinct from the classical IFITM5 c.-14C > T variant.

title: Opportunistic abdominal aortic calcification assessment on spine radiographs in women with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis: linking cardiovascular burden and femoral neck bone loss.
authors: Pinheiro MMC, Ramos FP, Silva LVA, Szejnfeld VL, Castro CHM.
abstract: Introduction/objectives Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and osteoporosis are major comorbidities in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We assessed abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) opportunistically on spine radiographs and examined its associations with CVD, estimated cardiovascular risk, bone mineral density (BMD), and fragility fractures in women with longstanding RA. Method This cross-sectional study included 196 consecutive women with longstanding RA followed at a tertiary hospital. All underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and conventional spine radiography. AAC was graded using the Kauppila score (KS) and categorized as absent, mild-to-moderate (KS 1-6), or extended (KS > 6). Multivariable models evaluated factors associated with AAC and overt CVD. Results Participants had a mean age of 62.8 ± 9.6 years and median RA duration of 21 years. AAC was present in 48 women (24.5%), including extended AAC in 25 (12.7%). Overt CVD was documented in 32 participants (16.3%). Extended AAC was independently associated with hypertension (OR 8.57, 95% CI 1.10-67.02), longer RA duration (OR 1.05 per year, 95% CI 1.004-1.09), and lower femoral neck T-score (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.95). AAC of any severity was associated with overt CVD (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.26-6.63). Conclusions AAC detected on routine spine radiographs was common among women with longstanding RA and was associated with cardiovascular burden and lower femoral neck BMD. Opportunistic AAC assessment may complement cardiovascular and skeletal risk evaluation in RA. Larger cohorts are needed to confirm these exploratory associations, and prospective studies are needed to establish predictive value.

title: No Differences in Patient-reported Outcomes Between the Direct Anterior and Posterolateral Approach for THA: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Rykov K, de Vries AJ, Reininga IHF, Sietsma MS, Ten Have BLEF.
abstract: Background The direct anterior approach (DAA) for THA is seeing wider use because it is purported to deliver a faster postoperative recovery. However, most previous studies comparing the DAA with the posterolateral approach (PLA) were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous patient populations, and the use of outcome measures with ceiling effects. Questions/purposes (1) Does the DAA result in a higher proportion of patients achieving the patient acceptable symptom state (PASS) on the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS) after THA compared with the PLA? (2) Are there differences in symptoms, physical function, life activities and participation, health-related quality of life (QoL), or complications between the DAA and PLA in the first postoperative year? Methods A prospective, parallel-group, nonblinded, randomized controlled trial comparing the DAA and PLA for THA was conducted. Patients with primary or secondary osteoarthritis with an indication for THA with an uncemented femoral stem and cemented acetabular component were eligible. Of the 241 patients assessed for eligibility, 53% (128) were included in the study. Fifty-one percent (65 of 128) were randomized to the DAA group, and 49% (63 of 128) were randomized to the PLA group. One patient in each group was lost to follow-up, leaving 98% (64 of 65) and 98% (62 of 63) of patients available for analysis, respectively. There were no between-group differences in baseline or perioperative measurements. The primary outcome was achievement of the PASS on the HOOS at 3 months postoperatively. An a priori sample-size calculation indicated that 60 patients per group were required to detect a 20% difference in PASS achievement between groups (80% power; α = 0.05). With an expected loss to follow-up of 10%, the sample size was set to 65 patients per group. Secondary outcomes included symptoms, physical functioning, participation, and health-related QoL, assessed using patient-reported outcome measures and physical performance tests. Complications were assessed using the Clavien-Dindo classification. Outcomes were assessed preoperatively as well as at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Results At 3 months, the proportion of patients achieving the PASS did not differ between the DAA and PLA for any HOOS subscales, including symptoms (65% [41 of 63] versus 63% [39 of 62], OR 1.03 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.80 to 1.35]; p = 0.80), pain (48% [30 of 63] versus 53% [33 of 62], OR 0.90 [95% CI 0.63 to 1.27]; p = 0.53), activities of daily living (68% [43 of 63] versus 65% [40 of 62], OR 1.06 [95% CI 0.82 to 1.36]; p = 0.66), sports and recreation (55% [34 of 62] versus 58% [36 of 62], OR 0.94 [95% CI 0.69 to 1.29]; p = 0.72), and QoL (73% [46 of 63] versus 71% [44 of 62], OR 1.03 [95% CI 0.83 to 1.28]; p = 0.80). There were no between-group differences in symptoms, physical function, life activities and participation, and health-related QoL at any time point. Complications occurred in 8% (5 of 65) of patients in the DAA group and 2% (1 of 63) of patients in the PLA group (OR 3.05 [95% CI 0.51 to 18.40]; p = 0.21). Conclusion In this randomized controlled trial, the DAA did not improve patient-reported or functional outcomes compared with the PLA during the first postoperative year. In the absence of demonstrated patient-reported or functional benefits of the DAA, surgeons should not represent to patients that the DAA provides advantages in terms of the pace or magnitude of recovery. Future studies powered to detect differences in the risk of complications should be performed to see whether harms are more likely with the DAA than with other surgical approaches. Level of evidence Level I, therapeutic study.

title: No Difference in Revision Risk for Uncemented Humeral Stems Compared to Cemented Humeral Stems in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty for Proximal Humerus Fracture: A Registry-Based Cohort Study.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Chauhan A, Chang RN, Prentice HA, Cruz JR, McQueen PD, Paxton EW, Navarro RA, Koyonos LD.
abstract: Background Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) is an effective treatment option for complex proximal humerus fractures (PHF). Humeral stems are commonly cemented in patients with poor bone quality, increased comminution and/or older age to provide rotational stability for stem fixation. Recently, the use of uncemented stems has gained popularity due to newer, more stable designs. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to evaluate whether there were any differences in uncemented versus cemented stems with respect to revision risk. Methods Data from a US-based integrated healthcare system's Shoulder Arthroplasty Registry was utilized to conduct a cohort study. Adult patients with primary rTSA for PHF from 2011-2024 were included. The exposure of interest was humeral stem fixation, classified as uncemented versus cemented. Crude cumulative revision incidence was calculated as one minus the Kaplan-Meier estimate at 5-years follow-up. Propensity score-weighted Cox proportional hazard regression was used to evaluate the risk for all-cause revision. Propensity score weights were calculated prior to outcome evaluation using multivariable logistic regression and included age, sex, body mass index, race/ethnicity, diabetes status, smoking status, American Society of Anesthesiologist's classification, operative year, and operative time. Results The cohort comprised 1,415 rTSA; 450 with uncemented stems and 965 with cemented stems. At 5-years follow-up, the crude revision probability was 3.9% for uncemented stems and 3.2% for cemented stems. After propensity score weighting, no difference was observed in all-cause revision for uncemented versus cemented stems (hazard ratio [HR]=1.20, 95% confidence interval [CI]=0.61-2.37, p=0.60). Further, no differences were observed in risk for revision for dislocation (HR=1.06, 95% CI=0.38-2.98, p=0.91) or infection (HR=1.52, 95% CI=0.48-4.82, p=0.48). Conclusions Overall, our observational registry-based cohort study found no difference in revision risk when comparing uncemented to cemented stems for the use of rTSA in PHF. However, we still recommend surgeons consider cemented stem fixation on a case-by-case basis in patients with complex fractures, poor bone quality, and metabolic conditions affecting bone density. Level of evidence Level III, Retrospective Cohort Comparison using Large Database, Treatment Study.

title: Newer Generation DePuy INHANCE™ Modular Anatomic Convertible Polyethylene Glenoid and Platform Baseplate have Improved Resistance to Micromotion and Dissociation at the Polyethylene-Metal Junction.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Kane LT, Myers C, Smith M, Cuff D, Jawa A, Wiater JM, Austin L.
abstract: Introduction Metal-backed glenoid (MBG) designs in anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (aTSA) were introduced in the 1980s to address concerns with the high rate of loosening of all-polyethylene glenoid components, offering potential advantages of durable glenoid fixation and easy revisability, but have historically demonstrated concerning rates of mechanical failure including polyethylene (PE) liner dissociation. Recently, platform baseplates have been introduced which can be used in anatomic or reverse TSA configurations. Platform baseplates may improve clinical performance, but more biomechanical analysis is needed to support their implant design improvements over the failed MBG designs of the past. The purpose of this study was to biomechanically evaluate a newer generation DePuy INHANCE™ modular anatomic convertible glenoid PE liner and platform baseplate and its ability to withstand mechanical forces and resist polyethylene dissociation when subjected to worst-case loading conditions. Methods The DePuy INHANCE™ convertible glenoid + platform baseplate were tested for resistance to micromotion from repetitive loading and compared to an all-polyethylene glenoid component. The study implant was also evaluated for its ability to withstand tensile displacement and polyethylene dissociation from shear and axial forces and compared against another commonly used modular anatomic glenoid PE liner and platform baseplate implant. Micromotion testing was performed in accordance with the standardized modular dissociation test method (ASTM F028-17) that was developed specifically for modular anatomic glenoid systems. Results The average tensile displacement of the INHANCE™ study implant after cyclic rocking was significantly less than the all-polyethylene glenoid component (0.1 mm vs. 0.4 mm; p=0.03). The INHANCE™ polyethylene-metal junction had a significantly greater resistance to modular dissociation under shear loading (1104N, 95% CI [1068, 1140] vs. 713N, 95% CI [687, 739]; p Conclusion Our investigation shows that the DePuy INHANCE™ modular anatomic convertible glenoid PE liner and platform baseplate demonstrates favorable biomechanical performance against micromotion and polyethylene dissociation. These results should be considered when evaluating the current and future role of platform baseplates in aTSA.

title: Network meta-analysis of the efficacy of different exercise therapies in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
authors: Diao K, Zhang T, Wang H, Wang Y, Pan Y.
abstract: Background Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a leading cause of disability in the elderly and a growing social burden due to aging and increasing obesity rates. This study aims to investigate the effects of different exercise modalities on pain, physical function, stiffness, and muscle strength in patients with KOA. Methods A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and EBSCO databases for randomized controlled trials evaluating the efficacy of exercise therapy for KOA from January 2000 to 16 August 2025, followed by an updated search through 28 March 2026. No additional eligible studies were identified in the updated search. In total, 51 studies involving 3,045 participants (71.7% female; study-group mean ages ranged from 50.3 to 74.4 years) were included. The studies were conducted in 14 countries across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and Oceania. A network meta-analysis was performed using Stata 16.0. This systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251177632). Results The results showed that mind-body exercise was the most effective in reducing pain (standardized mean differences (SMD) = -1.13, 95% confidence interval (CI) [-1.47 to -0.79], P P P P P Conclusion Mind-body exercise appeared to be the most favorable option for reducing pain and stiffness in patients with knee osteoarthritis, whereas strength training appeared to be the most beneficial for improving muscle strength. These findings may help inform individualized exercise prescription, but should be interpreted cautiously given the uncertainty and limitations of the available evidence.

title: Multifocal isolated bone involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis in a 6-week-old infant.
authors: Ploeger C, Firouzabadi FD, Frank M, Chorney M, Contractor S, Ohene-Baah NY.
abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare clonal disorder of dendritic cells with a wide spectrum of clinical and radiologic manifestations. LCH occurs most frequently in infants often manifesting in multisystem or cutaneous disease. Consequently, the isolated multifocal bone involvement seen in this case is an unusual presentation for early infancy. We report a case of a 6-week-old female infant presenting with feeding intolerance and decreased use of the right upper extremity, found to have multifocal lytic skeletal lesions involving the humerus, ribs, calvarium, spine, pelvis, and long bones without clinical or imaging evidence of skin, hepatic, splenic, pulmonary, thymic, gastrointestinal, or central nervous system involvement. Diagnosis was established via CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of a proximal humeral lesion, which confirmed Langerhans cell histiocytosis. This case highlights the imaging features of multifocal osseous LCH in early infancy and demonstrates the safety and diagnostic utility of image-guided long bone biopsy in this vulnerable population. Early recognition and tissue confirmation are essential to avoid misdiagnosis and guide appropriate patient management.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals new mechanistic insights underlying the osteoanabolic effects of short chain fructooligosaccharide.
authors: Adedigba P, Grez-Capdeville M, Knotts TA, Peng G, Cooper B, O'Connell TM, Prideaux M, Lucas EA, Smith BJ.
abstract: Despite evidence that short chain fructooligosaccharide (FOS) improves bone mass and intestinal mineral absorption, the mechanism driving these effects remains uncertain. This study investigated how FOS modulates molecular and cellular pathways in bone through alterations in the gut microbiota and metabolome. Eight-week-old C57BL/6 female mice were fed a control or FOS-supplemented diet (10%) for 4 weeks. Bone histomorphometry, femur and bone marrow transcriptomics, cecal content 16S rRNA sequencing, and serum untargeted metabolomics were performed. Mice fed the FOS diet exhibited greater femoral trabecular bone volume and cortical bone thickness and area. FOS increased trabecular and cortical bone formation (i.e., periosteal and endocortical surface), and enhanced mineralization on the trabecular and endocortical surfaces. These changes coincided with increased osteoblasts and osteocytes, while osteoclasts were unchanged. Transcriptomics on the flushed femur revealed enrichment of pathways involving calcium ion homeostasis, PPAR signaling and adipogenesis, while in the bone marrow pathways associated with T-cell modulation and extracellular matrix organization were enriched. FOS altered the gut microbiota, increasing the abundance of taxa associated with fermentation and aromatic compound degradation, and increased serum metabolites (e.g., indole, mevalonate, polyphenol, and fatty acid intermediates). These findings reveal new insights into gut microbial and serum metabolite shifts induced with short-term FOS supplementation accompanying a rapid increase in osteocytes as well as bone formation and mineralization.

title: Match Exposure and Estimated Travel Before ACL Injury in Professional Women's Football: An Exploratory Within-Player Case-Crossover Study.
authors: Hampstead W, Pappas E, Whalan M, Wakefield B, Crespin V, Lovell R.
abstract: Background Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries are a substantial concern in professional women's football and involve a complex interplay of intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Pre-injury match exposure and match-related travel may represent relevant contextual factors; however, their relationship with ACL injury occurrence remains unclear. Objective To quantify and compare pre-injury match exposure and estimated travel distance between ACL injury seasons and matched preceding-season periods using a within-player design. Methods This retrospective, within-player case-crossover study included professional women's football players (Tier 3-5) with publicly reported ACL injuries between 2022 and 2024. For each player, match exposure and estimated travel distance before injury were compared with the corresponding calendar window 365 days earlier. Match minutes, appearances, and matches started were assessed across 30-, 60- and 90-day pre-injury windows, whilst estimated travel distance was assessed over 30 days. Paired tests and Cohen's d quantified the differences. Mixed-effects logistic regression models examined whether exposure variables differentiated injury-season from control-season observations, and Spearman's correlations assessed associations between the corresponding between-season differences in match exposure and estimated travel distance. Results Data from 375 players were analysed. Match minutes, appearances and matches started were greater during injury seasons across all observation windows, with small effect sizes (d = 0.21-0.37). Estimated travel distance during the 30 days preceding injury was significantly greater in injury seasons (2724 ± 4821 km vs 2194 ± 4625 km, p Conclusion Injury season periods were characterised by slightly greater match exposure and estimated travel distance than matched control periods from the preceding year. However, effect sizes were small and between-player variability was substantial. These exploratory findings do not establish causality but identify contextual exposure patterns that warrant further prospective investigation.

title: Long-term outcome of acromioclavicular joint injuries in an urban population.
authors: Skjaker SA, Enger M, Torgalsen A, Pripp AH, Nordsletten L, Bøe B.
abstract: Objective To assess long-term outcomes following acromioclavicular (AC) joint injuries and associations between injury severity and patient-reported shoulder function. Methods This prospectively registered cohort included all patients diagnosed with an AC joint injury at Oslo University Hospital in 2013-2014. Participants were invited to follow-up in 2021. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) included the Oxford Shoulder Score (OSS), Quick Disabilities of Arm, Shoulder and Hand, and Numeric Rating Scale for shoulder pain. A subset underwent clinical examination using the Constant-Murley Score, shoulder tests and anteroposterior radiographs. Radiographs were evaluated for Rockwood classification and degenerative changes. Results A total of 240/287 (84%) participants responded at a mean follow-up of 7.6 years (SD 0.3). Among respondents, 72% had Rockwood type I or II injuries, 24% had type III injuries and 4% had type V injuries. The mean OSS was 41.8 (SD 8.6) of 48, without significant differences comparing Rockwood type I with types II, III or V injuries (p>0.05). Younger females aged 20-30 and males aged 20-40 recorded lower OSS scores than normative data (p Conclusion In this unselected urban cohort, most respondents reported favourable long-term shoulder function, although some experienced ongoing symptoms. OSS did not differ significantly between Rockwood categories, although comparisons involving Rockwood type V were limited by small sample size. Radiographic degeneration was common but unrelated to PROMs.

title: Implant-Preserving Guided Bone Regeneration for Peri-Implant Bone Loss Associated With Early Peri-Implantitis: A Case Report.
authors: Samantaray RK, Sinha P, Agarwal SK, Sharan J, Devi LB, Basynat SK.
abstract: A 60-year-old man developed localized peri-implant bone loss 2.5 months after implant placement. Surgical debridement was followed by guided bone regeneration using autogenous retromolar bone and a resorbable collagen membrane. At follow-up, satisfactory hard-tissue healing and implant stability were observed, permitting successful prosthetic rehabilitation and maintenance of function.

title: Impact of early versus delayed mobilization after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair in small and medium-sized tears: a prospective randomized study.
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
authors: Abdallah MR, Hassan AS, Abdelal M.
abstract: Purpose To compare early versus delayed mobilization following arthroscopic single-row knotless rotator cuff repair for small and medium-sized tears, performed in the beach-chair position without the use of an abduction sling. Methods A prospective randomized study was conducted on 70 patients aged 20-70 years with small and medium-sized full-thickness supraspinatus tears repaired using single-row knotless suture anchors (one or two depending on tear size). Patients were assigned to early mobilization (EPM, n = 35) or delayed mobilization (DPM, n = 35). Outcomes were assessed using range of motion (ROM), pain (VAS), Constant-Murley and UCLA scores, and MRI tendon integrity at 12 months. Results EPM patients showed faster ROM recovery at 3 months (mean 130° vs. 115°; p = 0.02), but one re-tear (2.8%) occurred in this group compared to DPM, where no re-tears occurred. At 12 months, both groups achieved comparable functional and pain outcomes. Conclusion Early mobilization accelerates short-term ROM recovery, whereas both early and delayed protocols result in comparable functional and pain outcomes by 12 months. Given the limited number of retear events and the absence of a prespecified tear size subgroup analysis, no definitive recommendation can be made regarding a differential mobilization strategy according to tear size.

title: HIF-1α expression is associated to cell proliferation and ECM production in temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis.
authors: Liu L, Shi X, Li X, Lin Y, Yang H, Zhang J, Yang C.
abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJOA) is a complex joint disorder characterized by progressive degradation of the cartilage matrix and apoptosis of chondrocytes; however, hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) serves a positive role in maintaining the stability of the articular cartilage matrix. Therefore, the present study aimed to determine the expression levels of HIF-1α in the cartilage tissue of rats with TMJOA, and to explore its association with the proliferation of chondrocytes and the formation of cartilage matrix. Experimental animals were subjected to occlusal interference treatment for periods ranging from 2 to 10 weeks to induce osteoarthritis (OA)-like pathological changes. Subsequently, various histochemical methods were employed to systematically evaluate the degree of articular cartilage damage in the TMJOA rat model. The expression levels of HIF-1α, proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), collagen type II (COLII) and aggrecan in cartilage tissues of rats with OA were analyzed using immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence techniques. Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to quantify the expression levels of HIF-1α, PCNA, Aggrecan and COLII in primary chondrocytes under hypoxic conditions (1% O2). EdU was used to assess the chondrocyte proliferation. From week 4 onward, a reduction in HIF-1α expression levels were detected in the lesioned cartilage of the TMJOA rats. Furthermore, the percentage of HIF-1α-positive chondrocytes was found to be significantly negatively associated with the OA score. This study demonstrated that the expression pattern of HIF-1α was consistent with cell proliferation and extracellular matrix production, and was negatively correlated with the severity of condylar cartilage degeneration.

title: Glenohumeral radial mismatch and revision for aseptic loosening after anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty: a Dutch Arthroplasty Register study.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Boulidam D, Macken AA, Buijze GA, Spekenbrink-Spooren A, Sierevelt IS, Eygendaal D, van Noort A, van den Bekerom MPJ.
abstract: Background Aseptic glenoid loosening remains a leading cause of revision after anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (aTSA). Glenohumeral radial mismatch is considered an important biomechanical factor influencing glenoid component survival, with smaller mismatches associated with radiolucent lines, an early sign of implant loosening. However, its effect on implant survival remains unclear. Therefore, the aim of this study is to evaluate the association between glenohumeral radial mismatch and revision for aseptic glenoid loosening in patients undergoing aTSA. Methods All primary aTSAs performed between 2014 and 2024 and registered in the Dutch Arthroplasty Register were included. Patients were eligible if they had a Walch A glenoid (A1 or A2) and received a fully cemented all-polyethylene glenoid component. Cases with components for which the radius could not be identified were excluded. Patients were divided into a low radial mismatch group ( Results A total of 1,683 shoulders were included (909 low mismatch, 774 high mismatch). Median follow-up was 5.3 years (IQR 2.8-7.7), and median radial mismatch was 4.8 mm (IQR 3.0-6.2). Overall, 88 (5%) revisions were recorded, including 26 (1.5%) for aseptic glenoid loosening and 17 (1%) for instability. At 6 years, estimated revision-free survival in the low and high radial mismatch groups was 98.5% and 98.2% for aseptic loosening. Univariable Cox regression showed no statistically significant association between radial mismatch and aseptic loosening or overall revision, whereas high mismatch was associated with a higher hazard of revision for instability (HR 3.86, 95% CI 1.26- 11.83; p = 0.037). Conclusion In this registry-based cohort of patients with Walch A glenoids treated with fully cemented all-polyethylene glenoid components, glenohumeral radial mismatch was not associated with revision for aseptic glenoid loosening or overall revision. An association between higher radial mismatch and revision for instability was observed; however, given the low number of events, this finding should be interpreted with caution. Future studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Functional outcomes over 24 months after arthroscopic repair of isolated subscapularis tendon tears in a multicentre study.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Audigé L, Croci E, Trong MLD, Flury M, Jost B, Cunningham G, Benninger E, Baum C, Müller AM.
abstract: Background Isolated subscapularis tears are rare, and it is currently unclear how the tear size relates to the postoperative outcomes after arthroscopic repair. This study aimed to evaluate clinical- and patient-reported outcomes, as well as adverse events of arthroscopically treated isolated subscapularis tears based on the tear extent over 24 months. Methods Across 19 orthopaedic centres, 69 patients undergoing primary arthroscopic repair for isolated subscapularis tears were prospectively recruited between June 2020 and November 2021. Medical imaging examinations were conducted at baseline and at 12 months. Clinical- and patient-reported outcomes were obtained at baseline, 6, 12, and 24 months. Adverse events within 24 months were documented. Patients were grouped into partial tears (n = 14), full-thickness tears of the superior half (n = 35) or complete full-thickness tears (n = 20) of the subscapularis. All outcomes were compared using generalised linear mixed models adjusted for baseline values, age, sex, American Society of Anaesthesiologists classification, tear aetiology, and steroid infiltrations. Results Improvements in all outcome scores were observed after surgery. No group differences were observed in the ranges of motion in flexion, abduction and external rotation (P≥0.634). The partial tear group had a higher pain level than both full-thickness groups at 12 months (P≤0.005). Abduction strength, Constant Score, Oxford Shoulder Score, Subjective Shoulder Value and EQ-5D-5L showed positive changes within 12- or 24-month follow-ups, with no group differences (P≥0.089). The risk of at least a symptomatic adverse event of any severity level affecting the operated shoulder and arm was highest for patients with partial tears (50%) and lowest for patients with complete full-thickness tears (25%). The most frequent occurrences were persistent or worsening pain, stiffness, and recurrent defects. Overall, 62% of patients with partial tears, 97% of patients with superior full-thickness tears and 77% of patients with complete full-thickness tears were satisfied at 24 months. Conclusion Arthroscopic repair of isolated subscapularis tears leads to significant and sustained improvements in clinical and patient-reported outcomes over 24 months, regardless of tear extent. However, patients with partial tears demonstrated greater residual pain and fewer patients reported satisfaction compared with those with full-thickness tears. These findings may reflect differences in patient characteristics and surgical treatment choices. Further studies are needed to determine the suitability and efficacy of surgical treatments for isolated subscapularis partial tears. Level of evidence Level III, Retrospective Cohort Comparison, Prognosis Study.

title: Finger Lacerations Are Highly Prevalent Among Shoulder Surgeons, and No Widely Effective Preventive Measures Are Available.
authors: Do A, Lazaridou A, Scheibel M.
abstract: Purpose To explore factors associated with the occurrence of finger lacerations during arthroscopic and open knot-tying techniques in shoulder surgery. Methods This cross-sectional survey was conducted at an international shoulder surgery course in March 2024. Attending shoulder surgeons performing arthroscopic and open shoulder surgeries were asked to participate in a survey on site using a structured questionnaire to explore factors associated with the occurrence and anatomical distribution of skin lacerations during arthroscopic and open knot-tying techniques. Demographic, procedural, and intraoperative variables were collected and compared between techniques. Linear and logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of laceration occurrence and severity. Results A total of 100 surgeons were invited to participate, all of whom completed the survey (response rate: 100%). Eighty-nine percent of respondents reported having experienced finger lacerations either currently or in the past, with 79% still affected at the time of the survey. The remaining 10% had adopted effective preventive measures: 3% modified their knot-tying technique, 2% wrapped tape around the affected fingers, and 5% developed hyperkeratosis as a protective adaptation. Among those affected, lacerations were reported to occur always in 20%, often in 42%, sometimes in 22%, and rarely in 16% of arthroscopic cases.
