Conclusions This meta-analysis supports expandable endoprostheses as an effective limb-salvage option for skeletally immature patients with bone sarcoma, providing good functional outcomes and acceptable 5-year survival despite a high complication burden.

title: CORR Insights®: Disruption of Intrinsic Healing Elements Does Not Alter Early Functional or Mechanical Outcomes After Zone II Flexor Tendon Repair in a Large-animal Model.
authors: Beredjiklian PK.

title: A Review of Platelet-Rich Plasma as Treatment for Partial Elbow Ulnar Collateral Ligament Tears.
authors: Fogel AJ, Goli P, Yaeger LH, Baker M, Hartman JA, Smith MV, Hollabaugh WL.
abstract: Platelet-rich plasma injections are increasingly utilized for partial-thickness ulnar collateral ligament tears in throwing athletes. This narrative review evaluates platelet-rich plasma's efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness for partial ulnar collateral ligament tears using literature from 2020 to 2026. A systematic search identified four studies, including cohorts and an economic simulation model. The largest cohort demonstrated that 60% of athletes with partial tears returned to play when platelet-rich plasma was combined with rehabilitation. Smaller case series reported successful return to play with similar treatment, though limited by a lack of comparison groups and small sample sizes. Complications included ulnar nerve dysfunction, particularly in athletes with preexisting nerve instability. Early surgery was often more cost-effective for long-term career durability. Current evidence suggests platelet-rich plasma alongside rehabilitation may benefit select athletes with partial ulnar collateral ligament injuries but is limited by retrospective designs, heterogeneous protocols, and inconsistent outcome measures. Future research is needed regarding patient selection and standardized treatment protocols.

title: Tibial Condylar Valgus Osteotomy Combined With Inverted V-Shaped High Tibial Osteotomy.
authors: Nakayama H, Yasuda K, Kondo E, Yonekura A, Tachibana T, Yoshiya S, Iseki T.
abstract: In constructing surgical strategies for correction of varus deformity in osteoarthritic knees, both bony and intra-articular deformities should be taken into consideration. Bony deformity is corrected by high tibial osteotomy (HTO), whereas intra-articular deformity associated with increased joint line convergence angle can be addressed by tibial condylar valgus osteotomy (TCVO). In the TCVO procedure, the medial tibial joint line is elevated by an L-shaped osteotomy. A surgical procedure combining open-wedge HTO and TCVO has been reported before. Although this combined procedure can address both bony and articular deformities, correction of severe bony deformity by open-wedge HTO with large wedge opening may induce problems of unacceptable joint line obliquity and increase in leg length. In this situation, inverted V-shaped HTO reported by Aoki and Kondo can be an alternative option. The inverted V-shaped HTO procedure is designed to combine hemiclosed and hemiopen osteotomies. However, the correction is made near the center of rotation of tibial angulation, and wedge width can be reduced compared with other HTO procedures; potential problems associated with conventional HTO can be avoided. In this paper, the surgical rationale and sequence of combined TCVO and inverted V-shaped HTO for correction of severe varus deformity are described.

title: The Impact of Rurality on the Standard of Care for Hip Fracture Patients: An ANZHFR Study.
authors: Hurst KP, Fielding K, Hoque S, Wall C, Maguire R, Seal A.
abstract: Background Hip fracture care requires timely, multi-disciplinary management. This study examined whether rural hospital location was associated with adherence to the Australian Hip Fracture Clinical Care Standard (HFCCS). Methods Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry data from 2018 to 2023 were analysed for patients aged ≥ 50 years. Hospitals were classified using the Modified Monash Model as metropolitan (MM1-2) or rural (MM3-7). Patients transferred before surgery were excluded from the primary analysis and examined separately. Missing data were addressed using multiple imputation. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex and ASA classification. Results The primary analysis included 58 757 patients (50 727 metropolitan; 8030 rural). Metropolitan hospitals had higher adherence to cognitive assessment (72.8% vs. 68.1%), nerve block administration (94.0% vs. 91.2%), delirium assessment (76.2% vs. 70.1%), surgery within 48 h (80.3% vs. 78.7%), mobilisation within 24 h (92.9% vs. 90.9%) and secondary fracture prevention (81.3% vs. 69.8%) (all p Conclusion Rural hospital location was associated with lower adherence to several HFCCS indicators, particularly cognitive and delirium assessment, early mobilisation and secondary fracture prevention, while timely analgesia was more frequent in rural hospitals. Geographical variation in guideline-based hip fracture care persists in Australia and warrants further investigation.

title: Menopausal Hormone Therapy Decreases the Odds of Developing Soft-Tissue Disorders of the Shoulder in Perimenopausal Women.
authors: Shah IK, Shah AK, Burkhart RJ, Dannacher CA, Desai NN, Calcei JG, Campbell AL.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether perimenopausal women receiving menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) have decreased odds of developing soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with women without an active MHT prescription, specifically adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, bicipital tendinitis, calcific tendinitis, atraumatic rotator cuff tear/rupture, and shoulder impingement syndrome and to quantify the impact of differing formulations and administration route. Methods The TriNetX US Collaborative Research Network, a deidentified database of over 180 million patients, was queried on June 11, 2026. Women aged 40 to 60 years in a menopausal state were identified by International Classification of Diseases code N95.1 and primary ovarian insufficiency by International Classification of Diseases code E28.3. Patients were grouped by MHT prescription status. Patients were one-to-one propensity-matched on age, race, ethnicity, and metabolic disease status, with standardized mean difference less than 0.1. The odds of developing soft-tissue shoulder disorders were studied, with P values less than .05 considered statistically significant. Results A total of 296,992 patients were included. The index the mean age was 49.1 years, 74.5% to 74.6% were White, 6% were Hispanic/Latino, 9% were African American, and 4.1% were Asian. Women prescribed any form of systemic MHT showed significantly lower odds of developing adhesive capsulitis (odds ratio [OR] 0.875, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.786-0.973; P = .014), bicipital tendinitis (OR 0.775, 95% CI 0.669-0.898; P = .001), calcific tendinitis (OR 0.829, 95% CI 0.706-0.974; P = .023), shoulder impingement syndrome (OR 0.873, 95% CI 0.792-0.962; P = .006), and rotator cuff tear/rupture (OR 0.892, 95% CI 0.804-0.991; P = .032). Topical estrogen specifically was associated with decreased odds of developing adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, bicipital tendinitis, shoulder impingement syndrome, and rotator cuff tear/rupture. Conclusions In peri- and postmenopausal women, MHT use was associated with decreased odds of soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with individuals not using MHT. Topical estrogen was more closely associated with reduced odds of soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with oral estrogen and oral combined formulations. Level of evidence Level III, therapeutic retrospective comparative study.

title: Diamond-Unit Crisscross Mattress Suture for Double-Row Rotator Cuff Repair: An All-Arthroscopic Technique.
authors: Wang XH, Fang C, Yu G, Wang YM, Zhao QC.
abstract: This article describes the diamond-unit crisscross mattress suture technique for double-row rotator cuff repair using an all-arthroscopic approach. This method combines knotted fixation at the medial row and knotless fixation, offering uniform tendon footprint coverage while reducing anchor usage. The technique is straightforward to perform and does not require additional sutures. By using a single lateral-row anchor, it improves the contact and stability between the tendon and bone. This technique is intended for selected small- to medium-sized tears, particularly those with irregular or degenerative margins.

title: Association of Subscapularis Tear Severity With Posterosuperior Cuff Tear Morphology in a Combined‐Tear Surgical Cohort: A Retrospective Cross‐Sectional Study
authors: Bircan R, Kaya İ, Yaş S, Çalta M, Eren T, Kanatlı U.

title: Association of Subscapularis Tear Severity With Posterosuperior Cuff Tear Morphology in a Combined-Tear Surgical Cohort: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Bircan R, Kaya İ, Yaş S, Çalta MŞ, Eren TK, Kanatlı U.
abstract: Objectives In combined tears, the relationship between posterosuperior cuff tear (PSCT) morphology and subscapularis (SSC) tear severity is unknown. This study aimed to determine whether PSCT morphology is associated with SSC tear severity, which morphologies are associated with complete SSC rupture, and whether any association is confined to a particular severity threshold and persists after accounting for classification uncertainty and overall cuff extent. Methods A retrospective review of 368 patients who underwent arthroscopic surgery for combined, chronic, full-thickness PSCTs with concomitant SSC tears between 2016 and 2023 was conducted. High-resolution preoperative MRI and high-definition intraoperative video recordings were used to classify PSCT morphology (crescent, U-shaped, anterior L-shaped, posterior L-shaped, massive-retracted) and SSC tears (Lafosse Types I-V). Interobserver agreement was almost perfect for both classifications. Binary logistic regression (adjusted for age, sex, side, and BMI) was used to evaluate associations with complete subscapularis rupture (Lafosse IV/V). Results The mean patient age was 60.3 ± 9.2 years. PSCT morphology was significantly associated with SSC tear severity (Monte Carlo P less than 0.001; Cramer's V 0.234). The proportion with complete SSC rupture rose from 23.8% in posterior L-shaped and 25.6% in crescent tears to 39.6% in U-shaped, 60.9% in anterior L-shaped, and 71.4% in massive-retracted tears. Complete subscapularis rupture was significantly more likely in anterior L-shaped (adjusted OR 4.50, 95% CI 1.86 to 11.41) and massive-retracted morphologies (adjusted OR 7.12, 95% CI 2.24 to 27.17), both surviving correction (adjusted p = 0.003). Posterior L-shaped and U-shaped morphologies showed no significant difference from crescent tears. Conclusion In surgically treated combined tears, PSCT morphology shows a graded association with SSC tear severity that is concentrated in the anterior L-shaped and massive-retracted morphology patterns. However, because most complete ruptures overall occurred within crescent tears due to their high prevalence, morphology alone cannot serve as a definitive diagnostic rule-out tool. Nevertheless, anterior L-shaped or massive-retracted PSCT patterns warrant systematic inspection of the SSC.

title: Arthroscopic Supraspinatus Repair With Bioinductive and Mechanical Reinforcement Using a Biocomposite Scaffold.
authors: Gomez G, Capasso M, Gomez GM, Bourlot D, Colombo P, Aguirre Trujillo KF.
abstract: Rotator cuff repair failure remains a major challenge, particularly in large, chronic, and revision supraspinatus tears. Structural failure is multifactorial and involves both mechanical insufficiency and compromised biologic healing capacity. Retear rates in large and massive tears have been reported between 20% and 70%. Biocomposite-reinforced scaffolds have been introduced to address both mechanical and biologic limitations. BioBrace (CONMED, Largo, FL) consists of a porous type I collagen matrix reinforced with resorbable poly-L-lactic acid microfilaments, designed to provide load-sharing support while promoting tissue ingrowth. This technical note describes a stepwise arthroscopic double-row supraspinatus repair incorporating a bioinductive and mechanically reinforced scaffold.

title: Arthroscopic Bone Xenograft Augmentation for Glenoid Bone Deficiency and Recurrent Anterior Shoulder Instability Improves Functional Outcomes Despite Graft Nonunion.
authors: Russo R, Fedele A, Rossi V, Russo F, Russo C, Francesco DP, Gigante AP, Guastafierro A.
abstract: Purpose To analyze the healing of equine-derived xenograft bone blocks with the native glenoid using computed tomography (CT) and to evaluate clinical outcomes in patients undergoing arthroscopic bone block stabilization with xenograft, Bankart repair, and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis for recurrent anterior shoulder instability with glenoid bone loss. Methods Patients with recurrent anterior shoulder instability and glenoid bone loss between 12.5% and 25% who underwent arthroscopic equine-derived xenograft bone block augmentation combined with Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis between 2019 and 2023 were identified. Minimum clinical and radiological follow-up was 24 months. Xenograft healing was evaluated on serial CT scans, and clinical outcomes were assessed using Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index, Rowe, quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand, and visual analog scale scores. Results A total of 76 patients (72 men, 4 women) met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed, with a mean clinical follow-up of 50.7 months (range, 24-75 months). Radiological follow-up on CT averaged 46.1 months (range, 24-72 months). All patients underwent CT imaging according to the study protocol. Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index improved from 1335.7 ± 136.8 to 134.6 ± 138.2 ( P P P P Conclusions Despite the lack of radiographic union, most patients treated with arthroscopic bone xenograft plus Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis showed functional improvements surpassing the MCID threshold at a minimum 2-year follow-up. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective therapeutic case series.

title: Arthroscopic Anatomic Glenoid Reconstruction With Distal Tibial Allograft and Remplissage Suture Staple Procedure in the Beach-Chair Position.
authors: Wagala NN, Lurie B, Sliepka JM, Zhang AL.
abstract: Critical bone loss in patients with recurrent shoulder instability is often addressed with bone block procedures such as glenoid reconstruction. Various bone block procedures and techniques currently exist to address glenoid bone loss; however, the addition of remplissage may be frequently overlooked despite concomitant engaging or off-track Hill-Sachs defects. Recent biomechanical studies suggest that the addition of remplissage may improve shoulder stability after glenoid reconstruction. This technique highlights an efficient method for addressing glenoid bone loss with arthroscopic anatomic glenoid reconstruction using distal tibia allograft as well as Hill-Sachs lesions with knotless remplissage suture staple procedure in the beach-chair position.

title: Anatomic Triple-Bundle Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Technique With Three Femoral Tunnels and Three Tibial Tunnels Using Hamstring Tendon.
authors: Shammas BM, Jasim A M.
abstract: Reconstruction of the anterior cruciate ligament is a common procedure for athletes with the aim of returning to sports activities. Despite improved surgical techniques and rehabilitation, the return-to-sport rate and retear rates remain unsatisfactory. Some centers in Japan and India nowadays have resorted to triple-bundle anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction to solve these issues. We described a technique for triple-bundle anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with three femur tunnels and three tibial tunnels using hamstring tendon.

title: An Adaptive Knee Brace Is Associated With Improved Dynamic Stabilization Compared With a Standard Passive Brace in Anterior Cruciate Ligament-Deficient Men During a Functional Hop Task.
authors: Greenberg S, Gottlieb R.
abstract: Purpose To compare the dynamic knee stabilization effects of an adaptive dynamic brace (ADB) with those of a standard passive brace in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)-deficient men. Methods ACL-deficient participants were included. The subjects performed 3 single-leg functional hop tests: drop jump, crossover hop, and 90° rotational hop. Each task was performed once while wearing the ADB and once while wearing a traditional passive brace. Three-dimensional kinematic data were collected using an 8-camera optoelectronic motion-capture system. Repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to evaluate the effects of brace condition and time. An a priori power analysis indicated that a minimum of 12 participants were required. Results Twelve ACL-deficient participants were included (age: 30.2 ± 3.4 years; time since injury: 32 ± 6 months; ACL-Return to Sport after Injury score: 70 ± 3). No significant differences in knee flexion angles were observed between braces. Knee flexion during landing was significantly lower in the crossover hop compared with the drop jump and rotational hop tasks ( P P P P P Conclusions The ADB showed improved dynamic stabilization particularly during high-risk landing and rotational movement compared with a standard passive brace. Clinical relevance The ADB may enhance the effectiveness of rehabilitation strategies in ACL-deficient individuals by improving dynamic knee stability during functional activities.

title: Understanding acceptance before intervention: patient perspectives on robotic-assisted femoral neck fracture fixation.
authors: Al-Smadi F, Abudourusuli X, Yang H, Al-Smadi S, Liao J, Ouyang L, Zhang Z, Zeng R, Mi B, Xie X, Liu M, Liu G.
abstract: Patient acceptance is important for surgical robotics implementation, but evidence in acute orthopaedic trauma is limited. We examined preoperative acceptance of robotic-assisted femoral neck fracture fixation and factors associated with behavioral intention. This prospective multicenter observational study included 378 adults with femoral neck fractures assessed before definitive fixation technique selection. A Chinese-adapted questionnaire assessed six acceptance constructs and behavioral intention. Multivariable linear regression with heteroskedasticity-consistent type 3 (HC3) robust standard errors examined associations with intention, while logistic regression assessed factors associated with post-introduction self-reported understanding of the robot's role. Performance expectancy (B = 0.524; 95% CI, 0.391-0.657; P < 0.001), social influence (B = 0.262; 95% CI, 0.151-0.373; P < 0.001), and pleasure (B = 0.159; 95% CI, 0.038-0.281; P = 0.010) were associated with greater intention. In a separate contextual model, prior knowledge of femoral neck fracture surgical techniques (B = 0.905), self-reported understanding (B = 0.540), and robotic-option offering (B = 0.545) were positively associated with intention, whereas additional-cost concern was inversely associated (B = - 0.242). The association with robotic-option offering was not significant in a restricted-center analysis (B = 0.447; P = 0.125). Prior knowledge (aOR = 7.46; 95% CI, 4.01-13.89) and robotic-option offering (aOR = 2.54; 95% CI, 1.15-5.61) were associated with self-reported understanding. Acceptance of robotic-assisted femoral neck fixation reflects perceived technological value and the clinical decision context. Implementation should emphasize realistic expectations, clear explanations of the robot's role, cost transparency, and informed patient choice.

title: The impact of arthroscopic repair of the tibionavicular bundle of the deltoid ligament on ankle fractures.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Kürüm H, Akcan A, Çakır M, İpekten F.
abstract: Background Notwithstanding well-established ligament repair with ankle arthroscopy and a thorough understanding of deltoid ligament anatomy, evidence supporting early arthroscopic repair of the deltoid ligament (EAR-DL) remains limited. The purpose of this study was to compare EAR-DL with conservative treatment following ankle fracture. Methods This retrospective study evaluated 45 patients with deltoid ligament tears among 1165 ankle fractures. Patients were grouped based on the EAR-DL decision or conservative treatment. The EAR-DL decision is based on evidence gathered from clinical, radiological, and surgical findings. Patients with imaging-confirmed deltoid ligament injury and ≥ 12 months of follow-up were included; those with major concomitant injuries were excluded. Clinical and radiological outcomes, including instability, functional scores, return to sport, and medial clear space (MCS), were compared. The concomitant injury count (CIC) was developed to measure injury complexity; yet this exploratory score has not yet been validated or assessed for reliability. Final outcomes were evaluated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for baseline values. MCS ≤ 4 mm was considered normal, and ankle stability was assessed using anteromedial drawer and valgus stress tests. Results C3 was the most common fracture pattern in 14 patients (31.1%), followed by B3 in 9 patients (20.0%). The most common CIC level was 3, observed in 28 patients (62.2%). No recurrent instability occurred following EAR-DL, compared with 4 (15.4%) cases in the conservative group (p = 0.126). The return to sports was observed at an average of 33.04 ± 3.18 weeks in the conservative group and at 29.32 ± 1.60 weeks in the EAR-DL group (p Conclusions In this retrospective cohort study, no statistically significant difference was found between the groups in recurrent instability. EAR-DL was associated with a smaller MCS and exploratory, unadjusted clinical outcomes compared with conservative management. Prospective, adequately powered studies are required to determine whether EAR-DL provides clinically meaningful benefits. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Sex-Equitable Machine Learning Prediction of Ankle Reinjury in Individuals with Chronic Ankle Instability: A 2-Year Prospective Cohort Study with Fairness Audit.
authors: Hwang UJ, Son SJ, Fu SN, Wong AYL, Bruening D, Feland B, Seeley M, Hopkins JT.
abstract: Background Patients with chronic ankle instability (CAI) face a 2-year reinjury rate approaching 50%, but individualized prediction models that quantify which baseline impairments predict subsequent reinjury within an established CAI cohort remain scarce, and existing prediction models for ankle injury have not assessed sex-related fairness. The aim was to develop and internally validate sex-equitable machine learning (ML) models predicting 2-year ankle reinjury in individuals with CAI, identify the most influential baseline prognostic markers, and audit sex-stratified model performance. Methods One hundred physically active individuals (50 male, 50 female) with CAI (mean age 21.8 ± 2.3 years) were recruited from a university population between February 2017 and February 2018 and prospectively followed for 2 years; 96 (49 male, 47 female) with at least one follow-up response were retained for analysis (41 reinjury events, 43% reinjury rate). Fourteen baseline predictors spanning demographic, anthropometric, injury-history, patient-reported, biomechanical, postural-control, and functional-performance domains were collected. Six algorithms were trained with nested cross-validation: an unpenalized logistic regression baseline and five ML algorithms (Elastic Net, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM). Predictive contribution of each feature was quantified using Shapley additive explanations and partial-dependence plots. A pre-specified fairness audit compared single global and sex-specific Youden thresholds derived out-of-fold using the equalized-odds gap and disproportionate-impact ratio. Results All algorithms achieved area under the curve (AUC) values above 0.70; Elastic Net was selected as the primary model (AUC = 0.807, 95% CI 0.714-0.893; calibration slope = 1.015). Sex, arch height index, previous sprains, dorsiflexion range of motion, and Biodex Overall Stability Index consistently emerged as the most influential prognostic markers. Within-sex discrimination was comparable between males and females, but a single global threshold produced an equalized-odds gap of 0.384 that was reduced by 57% (to 0.164) through sex-specific thresholding without retraining the model. Conclusions ML models with a fairness-audited threshold strategy predicted 2-year ankle reinjury in individuals with CAI, reducing the equalized-odds gap by 57%, though the disproportionate-impact ratio (0.683) remained below the 0.80 benchmark. External validation is required before clinical deployment.

title: Preoperative CT-derived psoas attenuation and correction loss after traumatic thoracolumbar fracture fixation: A construct-dependent association.
authors: Özdemir M, Latifoğlu F, Uğur OT, Peksoy F, Kamaşak K.
abstract: Background Postoperative correction loss remains a concern after posterior fixation of traumatic thoracolumbar fractures. Although bone quality and construct characteristics influence mechanical stability, the role of preoperative muscle quality remains poorly defined. We examined whether CT-derived psoas attenuation was associated with correction loss and whether fracture-level screw placement modified this association. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort included 78 adults who underwent posterior pedicle screw fixation for traumatic AO Spine A3 thoracolumbar fractures. Preoperative psoas and paravertebral attenuation and cross-sectional area were measured at L3. Correction loss was defined as the difference between final-follow-up and immediate postoperative Cobb angles measured on supine sagittal CT reconstructions. Multivariable linear regression tested the interaction between centered psoas attenuation and fracture-level screw placement, adjusting for age, sex, vertebral attenuation, instrumented levels, and follow-up duration. An extended model added vertebral height loss and canal compromise. HC3 robust variance estimation and sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Mean correction loss was 4.1 ± 5.4°, and 23 patients (29.5%) experienced loss greater than 5°. The psoas attenuation-by-fracture-level screw interaction was significant (B=0.311°/HU; 95% CI, 0.091-0.530; p = .006; HC3 p = .037). Without fracture-level screws, each 10-HU increase in psoas attenuation corresponded to approximately 2.6° less correction loss (B=-0.255°/HU; 95% CI, -0.440 to -0.071; p = .007), although HC3 inference crossed the null (p = .068). No clear association was observed with fracture-level screws. The interaction persisted after adjustment for vertebral height loss and canal compromise (B=0.342°/HU; 95% CI, 0.127-0.556; p = .002; HC3 p = .016), when short- versus long-segment fixation replaced instrumented-level count, and in patients with at least 12 months of follow-up. Paravertebral attenuation showed a similar pattern, whereas muscle cross-sectional area did not. Conclusions Preoperative psoas attenuation showed a construct-dependent association with correction loss after fixation of traumatic AO Spine A3 fractures. Lower attenuation may identify mechanical vulnerability when the fractured vertebra is not incorporated into the construct. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before CT-based muscle assessment can guide construct selection.

title: Patellofemoral joint cartilage status was not deteriorated after inverted V-shaped high tibial osteotomy.
authors: Hayashi S, Kato K.
abstract: Background Inverted V-shaped high tibial osteotomy (iVHTO), combining hemi-open-wedge (OW) and hemi-closed-wedge (CW) techniques, was developed to overcome the limitations of conventional high tibial osteotomy. This study aimed to evaluate postoperative changes in patellofemoral (PF) joint alignment, cartilage status, and clinical outcomes following iVHTO. Methods Thirty-seven knees in 27 patients underwent iVHTO for medial compartment osteoarthritis requiring a correction angle of >15°, or Results The mean follow up period was 25.1 months. PTA and LSR decreased significantly postoperatively (both P Conclusion iVHTO achieved satisfactory correction of lower limb alignment while preserving PF joint alignment and cartilage status. Significant improvements in patient-reported outcomes were observed, and preoperative AKP resolved in all affected patients.

title: Outside-In Inverted L-Shaped Capsulotomy in Hip Arthroscopy.
authors: Feng Y, Ni J, Tian Z, Chen Z, Wei W, Wang D, Shi Z.
abstract: Hip arthroscopy has become the mainstream surgical treatment for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, with approximately 88.75% of patients returning to sports postoperatively. Capsulotomy is a critical step in arthroscopic labral repair; however, various reported techniques possess inherent limitations. This technique employs an outside-in longitudinal capsulotomy along the femoral neck, followed by a transverse capsular release from its acetabular attachment along the path of the labral tear, creating an inverted "L"-shaped opening. On completion of the repair, the hip capsule is closed and retensioned using the remaining sutures from the labral repair anchors. This article summarizes the advantages, disadvantages, pearls, and pitfalls of this technique.

title: Outcomes associated with suprapectoral versus subpectoral biceps tenodesis site after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a retrospective comparative cohort analysis.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Rosso C, Loske S, Audigé L, Dao Trong ML, Weiss I, Mueller A, Selman F, Cunningham G.
abstract: Objectives To investigate functional outcomes, groove pain, presence of Popeye sign and complications associated with suprapectoral and subpectoral biceps tenodesis site in rotator cuff (RC) surgery. Methods Within the ARCR_Pred multicenter cohort study, patients from 19 centers undergoing primary arthroscopic RC repair between June 2020 and November 2021 were prospectively enrolled. Patients undergoing biceps tenodesis without preoperative Popeye sign were allocated to suprapectoral or subpectoral groups, respectively. Outcomes (range of motion, pain, strength, Subjective Shoulder Value, Constant-Murley Score, Oxford Shoulder Score, quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), groove pain, Popeye sign, Speed's test, and postoperative adverse events) were compared using adjusted mixed models. Propensity-score matching was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Results Among 445 eligible patients (242 suprapectoral, 203 subpectoral), biceps-specific outcomes were not significantly different for all parameters except for postoperative Popeye sign, being more frequent in the suprapectoral group (36 (15%) vs. 10 (5%); Odds ratio [OR] 0.20; P = 0.009). Shoulder abduction strength at 90° was higher in the suprapectoral cohort at 12 months postoperatively (7.1 vs. 6.3 kg; adjusted difference 0.8; P = 0.024), not reaching minimal clinical important difference. All other functional outcome parameters demonstrated no clinically significant differences. Biceps specific complications were not significantly different between groups. The propensity-score matching sensitivity analysis supported these findings except for the shoulder abduction strength. Conclusion Suprapectoral tenodesis was associated with a higher prevalence of postoperative Popeye sign. No significant differences were detected in postoperative groove pain. The observed strength advantage after suprapectoral tenodesis was not clinically meaningful. Procedure-specific complication rates were low in both groups.

title: Injury labels and patient-problem codes in FDA adverse event reports for robotic arthroplasty platforms: a cross-sectional analysis of 12,175 MAUDE reports.
authors: Abushal MH.
abstract: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) device reports carry two structured fields used to describe patient harm: the event-type label and patient-problem codes. I quantified how often prespecified contrasting categories of these fields co-occur in reports for robotic arthroplasty platforms. Cross-sectional analysis of reports in the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database, accessed through openFDA (product code OLO, received to 30 September 2026) matching search definitions for Mako and NAVIO/CORI (manufacturer field) and VELYS and ROSA Knee/Recon (brand field); procedures were not confirmed. The primary outcome was co-occurrence of an injury label with a no-consequence code, or of a non-injury label with a harm-related code, counted exactly from archived report-level records. Sensitivity analyses included harmonised definitions and duplicate screening. Of 12,175 reports, 2,106 (17.3%) were labelled injury, from 0.6% (VELYS) to 44.2% (ROSA). A no-consequence code appeared in 46.0% (Mako), 71.3% (NAVIO/CORI) and 59.5% (ROSA) of injury-labelled reports; a harm-related code appeared in 12.8% of non-injury VELYS reports. Overall, 1,785 reports (14.7%; 95% confidence interval 14.0-15.3) showed co-occurrence. The injury-label share exceeded the harm-related code share for Mako, NAVIO/CORI and ROSA; for VELYS, the reverse held. These directions persisted with clinical code categories, harmonised definitions and duplicate removal. Contrasting label and patient-code categories frequently co-occurred, in platform-specific directions. This reflects the fields' different purposes, not demonstrated coding disagreement, patient harm or device safety. Because reporting practices and search-field composition may contribute, harm proportions from either field alone should not be used to rank platforms.

title: Hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement in American football athletes: examining factors associated with outcomes at a mean follow-up time of 6.3 years.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Atkinson A, Crick M, Froom R, Westbrooks B, King E, Mussell E, Crawford A, Aiken C, Ithurburn M, Ryan M, Emblom B.
abstract: Introduction Femoroacetabular impingement (FAIS) is a common cause of hip pain and performance limitation in athletes. Hip arthroscopy is the gold standard of treatment in professional American football athletes, with numerous studies demonstrating favorable outcomes and high return-to-sport (RTS) rates. However, limited outcomes data exists in collegiate athletes and fewer still in high school athletes. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term patient-reported outcomes (PROs), RTS rates, and predictors of outcomes following hip arthroscopy for symptomatic FAIS in high school and collegiate football athletes. Materials and methods A retrospective cohort study was performed which included high-school and collegiate football athletes who underwent hip arthroscopy for symptomatic FAIS. Outcomes were assessed using the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), International Hip Outcome Tool-12 (IHOT-12), and Hip Outcomes Score-Sport Specific Subscale (HOS-Sport). Data regarding return to preinjury sport were also collected. Pre-operative radiographic data, including alpha angle, lateral center edge angle, and Tönnis grade, were collected. Results This cohort had a mean post-operative follow up of 6.3 years, with mean PRO scores of 82.2 on the mHHS, 84.6 on the iHOT-12, and 88.3 on the HOS-Sport. PASS thresholds were achieved by 69%, 77% and 80% of athletes for the same outcomes, respectively. 60% of the cohort attempted to return to sport, and 91% of the athletes who attempted to return to preinjury level of sport were successful. Increased age at time of surgery and larger pre-operative alpha angles were associated with worse PRO scores at follow-up. Conclusions Hip arthroscopy for FAIS in high school and collegiate football players yielded favorable long-term outcomes and RTS rates. This is similar to current outcomes data in professional athletes. Increased alpha angle and age at surgery were associated with worse outcomes, emphasizing the importance of early recognition and appropriate surgical treatment. Comparisons of outcomes between blocking and nonblocking positions may warrant further investigation in larger cohorts.

title: Defining the musculoskeletal ultrasound phenotype of ochronotic arthropathy: a systematic study of 34 patients with alkaptonuria.
authors: Bianchi E, Conticini E, Bardelli M, Baldi C, Selvi E, Mazzon A, Peruzzi L, Santucci A, Cantarini L, Frediani B, Falsetti P.
abstract: Objectives Ochronotic arthropathy is the leading cause of disability in patients with alkaptonuria (AKU), yet its musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSUS) phenotype has not been systematically characterized. This study aimed to define the ultrasound features of ochronotic arthropathy and identify recurring imaging patterns that may facilitate its recognition in clinical practice. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study including consecutive patients with genetically confirmed AKU evaluated at a tertiary referral centre between 2017 and 2025. Patients receiving nitisinone therapy and prosthetic joints were excluded from the ultrasound assessment. Bilateral standardized MSUS examinations of the shoulders, hips, knees and Achilles tendons were performed by experienced rheumatologists according to OMERACT definitions. The frequency and distribution of structural and inflammatory abnormalities were recorded, and their associations with clinical variables were explored. Results Thirty-four patients (17 females; mean age 52.1 ± 18.9 years) were included. Diagnostic delay positively correlated with the cumulative number of joint prostheses (ρ = 0.46, p = 0.006). The shoulder was the most frequently involved site (85.3%), showing bilateral hyperechoic rotator cuff deposits (66.7%), tendon tears (29.0%) and long head of the biceps tenosynovitis (30.0%). Knee abnormalities were identified in 61.8% of patients and included extensor tendon hyperechoic deposits (65.4%), meniscal involvement (50.0%), osteoarthritic changes (44.4%) and synovitis (29.4%). Achilles tendon involvement was observed in 48.4% of patients and was characterized by insertional and mid-portion linear hyperechoic deposits associated with tendinosis, entheseal thickening, erosive changes and only limited Power Doppler activity. Hip involvement was less common (20.0%). Significant associations were found between knee involvement and extensor mechanism abnormalities (p = 0.005) and between hip involvement and Achilles tendon enthesopathy (p = 0.038). Conclusions Ochronotic arthropathy demonstrates a distinctive musculoskeletal ultrasound phenotype characterized by bilateral tendon and entheseal involvement, linear hyperechoic deposits, advanced tendinosis and limited inflammatory activity. These findings provide the first systematic description of the ultrasound phenotype of AKU and suggest that MSUS may represent a valuable adjunctive tool for raising clinical suspicion of ochronotic arthropathy in patients with otherwise unexplained early degenerative musculoskeletal disease. Key Points • Ochronotic arthropathy shows a distinctive musculoskeletal ultrasound pattern. • Bilateral tendon and entheseal abnormalities are highly prevalent in AKU. • Linear hyperchoic deposits frequently accompany advanced tendinosis.

title: Deep learning-derived functional MRI connectivity maps of cervical spinal cord segments during hand grasping.
authors: Khan D, Rehman HZU, Jadoon K.
abstract: Task-based fMRI of the cervical spinal cord is limited by physiological noise and small sample sizes. The primary objective of this study was to examine whether a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based denoising framework can improve the detection of task-dependent functional connectivity between cervical spinal segments using generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) analysis. An open dataset of 26 healthy adults performing a hand-grasp task with alternating right- and left-hand blocks during 3 T fMRI was analyzed. A CNN with Inception V3 transfer learning (91.0% slice-level and 89.2% block-level accuracy) was trained to classify grasp versus rest, and the trained model was then utilized to derive denoised time series from masks of the spinal segments C5-C8. A gPPI model with a C6 ventral horn seed was evaluated using FDR correction and permutation testing (n = 1000). C6 showed positive task-dependent connectivity with C7 (β = 0.72, p = 0.003) and C8 (β = 0.58, p = 0.018), and negative connectivity with C5 (β = -0.31, p = 0.041), which is broadly consistent with the organization of the cervical myotomes. The C6-C5 effect was marginal and was not detected when conventional time series were used (p = 0.21), and therefore it requires replication. Grad-CAM maps aligned with ventral horn motor pools (Dice = 0.89 at C7). These results suggest that deep learning-based denoising may increase the sensitivity of spinal cord fMRI to segmental connectivity, although validation in larger cohorts is needed.

title: Trochleoplasty combined with MPFL reconstruction is associated with a postoperative reduction in the measured Caton-Deschamps index.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Coppola C, Nardelli P, Liebensteiner M, Lindtner RA, Khosravi I, Mayr R.
abstract: Introduction To investigate changes in MRI-measured Caton-Deschamps index (CDI) at mid- to long-term follow-up following groove-deepening trochleoplasty (TP) combined with medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction (MPFLR) and to compare these changes between single-bundle quadriceps tendon graft (QTG) and double-bundle hamstring tendon graft (HTG) reconstruction. Materials and methods Seventeen patients who had undergone TP with concomitant MPFLR were analyzed retrospectively. Patellar height was assessed preoperatively and postoperatively on sagittal magnetic resonance images by three independent observers using the CDI. Preoperative and postoperative CDI values were compared using a paired t-test. CDI changes were compared between single-bundle QTG (n = 9) and double-bundle HTG (n = 8) reconstruction using an independent-samples t-test. Interobserver reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results The mean CDI decreased significantly from 1.06 ± 0.13 preoperatively to 0.95 ± 0.15 postoperatively (Δ = -0.10 ± 0.07; P Conclusions Combined trochleoplasty and MPFL reconstruction was associated with a significant postoperative reduction in MRI-measured CDI at mid- to long-term follow-up, with an average decrease of - 0.10. Whether this finding reflects true anatomical patellar distalization cannot be determined from the present study.

title: The MIS-Diamond fixation: A minimally invasive diamond-shaped construct for spinopelvic dissociation in polytrauma patients.
authors: Giorgi PD, Ramponi A, Legrenzi S, Bove F, Mezzadri U, Addevico F, Prina A, Schirò GR.
abstract: Introduction Sacral fracture with spinopelvic dissociation (SPD) is a rare, high-energy injury associated with substantial mortality and morbidity. Surgical stabilization is technically challenging and has historically been associated with relatively high rates of construct failure. The present study describes and evaluates a novel minimally invasive spinopelvic diamond-shaped construct (The MIS-Diamond fixation), designed to improve rigid triangular stabilization while minimizing soft-tissue morbidity and facilitate the fracture reduction. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted including patients who underwent MIS-Diamond fixation for AO Type C3 sacral fractures at a single Level-I Trauma Center between January 2014 and December 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Neurological status, operative parameters, perioperative complications, and radiological outcomes were systematically assessed. Fractures were classified according to the AO Spine Sacral Injury Classification System. Results Thirty-two patients (mean age 39 years) were included. Surgery was performed at a median of 5 days post-injury, with a mean operative time of 115.8 min and mean estimated blood loss of 82.7 mL. No intraoperative complications occurred. One patient developed a postoperative S1 motor impairment attributed to indirect radicular injury during reduction. Implant-related complications were recorded in 4 patients (12.5%), including one late-onset surgical site infection and three cases of asymptomatic iliac screw loosening. No soft tissue or wound healing complications were observed. Implant removal was successfully completed in 28 patients (87.5%) at 12 months postoperatively. Discussion MIS-Diamond fixation demonstrated a favourable safety profile while enabling early postoperative mobilization. The incorporation of a 5.5 mm transverse iliac rod converts the classical triangular construct into a rigid box-like configuration, enhancing rotational stability and preventing coronal diastasis during vertical distraction. Limiting instrumentation to L4-L5 reduces the number of immobilized motion segments compared to previously described longer constructs, potentially mitigating long-term degenerative sequelae. Conclusions The MIS-Diamond fixation represents a safe and effective minimally invasive surgical option for SPD, providing reliable multiplanar stabilization with a low complication profile. Routine implant removal at 12 months is feasible and recommended to preserve motion segment function. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to further validate these findings.

title: The Influence of Height-Adjusted Nutritional Status Assessment on Complications Following Growing-Rod Surgery for Early-Onset Scoliosis.
authors: Zhang Y, Geng H, Wang J, Hai Y.
abstract: Objectives Accurate nutritional assessment in children with early-onset scoliosis (EOS) is challenging because spinal deformity reduces measured standing height and may distort BMI-for-age classification. This study aimed to evaluate, using a longitudinal design, height-adjusted nutritional status before each growing-rod procedure throughout the treatment course and to investigate its association with postoperative complications in patients with EOS. Methods A retrospective cohort study included 53 patients with EOS who underwent 86 growing-rod procedures between January 2016 and January 2023, with each procedure serving as the unit of analysis. Nutritional status was reassessed before each analyzed procedure using BMI calculated from height corrected by the Ylikoski formula and was linked to the postoperative outcome of the corresponding procedure. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to evaluate factors associated with postoperative complications while accounting for within-patient clustering. Results A total of 14 procedures resulted in postoperative complications, yielding an overall complication rate of 16.3% (14/86), with 15 specific complication events recorded. After height-adjusted BMI correction, 46 procedures were classified into the malnourished group and 40 into the normal nutrition group. The complication rate was significantly higher in the postadjusted malnourished group than in the normal nutrition group (23.9% vs. 7.5%, p = 0.042). Multivariable analysis using GEE revealed that undergoing ≥ 3 surgeries (OR = 4.614, 95% CI: 1.133-18.786, p = 0.033), and postadjusted malnutrition (OR = 3.701, 95% CI: 1.006-13.613, p = 0.049) were associated with increased risk of postoperative complications. However, after the Mancl-DeRouen small-sample correction, the association between height-adjusted malnutrition and complications was no longer statistically significant (OR = 4.21, 95% CI: 0.38-46.12, p = 0.239). Conclusions Height-adjusted malnutrition and repeated surgeries (≥ 3) were associated with increased postoperative complications after growing-rod surgery in EOS patients. However, larger cohorts are needed to confirm these findings. The procedure-specific application of height-adjusted BMI provides an alternative approach to longitudinal nutritional assessment during repeated growing-rod treatment. Timely intervention should be implemented for patients with poorer nutritional status.

title: The Effect of Cementless Stem Design on Late Periprosthetic Fractures After Total Hip Arthroplasty. Does the Design of Cementless Stems Affects the Rate of Periprosthetic Femoral Fractures?
authors: Koutalos AA, Akrivos V, Gkekas N, Karachalios T.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) are a leading cause of revision after total hip arthroplasty (THA). Cementless stems have been associated with higher rates of early and late PFFs than cemented fixation. This study evaluated whether cementless stem design is associated with the risk of late PFF following primary THA. Methods We performed a retrospective review of all primary cementless THAs implanted at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2000 and December 2023 (n = 3772). Early fractures ( Results At a mean follow-up of 14.5 years, the incidence of late PFF was 1.4% (53 of 3772). No difference in overall survival was observed among stem designs ( P = .108). Exploratory pairwise comparisons showed higher PFF-free survival for 1 type 2 stem design than for two other type 2 designs ( P = .002 and P = .003, respectively). No differences were found between type 2 (double wedge) and type 3 (tapered) stems ( P = .510). Increased age was independently associated with PFF ( P = .02). Conclusions Late PFF after cementless THA was uncommon. Although survivorship did not differ between broad stem categories, variability among individual designs warrants further evaluation in larger multicenter or registry-based studies.

title: Robotic arthroplasty and the gap between technical precision and clinical benefit.
authors: Xu Z, Fan W, Kong K, Jin M, Li Z, Li D, He C, Mamuladze T, Korytkin AA, Li H, Zhai Z.
abstract: Robotic-assisted arthroplasty improves resection accuracy, component positioning, and reproducibility. Whether these technical gains produce clinically meaningful benefits remains uncertain. This expert narrative review drew on PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science searches performed on April 28, 2026. Systematic reviews and randomized trials were prioritized, supplemented by observational, registry, economic, and technical studies. Evidence was appraised qualitatively by design, follow-up, bias, and platform differences; technical endpoints were assessed separately from patient-important outcomes. Evidence most consistently supports fewer alignment and component-positioning outliers. Functional and perioperative benefits vary by procedure, platform, outcome, and follow-up; evidence for generalizable long-term benefit remains inconsistent. The precision-target gap is proposed as one explanation: more accurate execution may yield limited benefit when the surgical target is insufficiently validated for the patient. Small differences from conventional care, confounding, and outcome measurement provide alternative explanations. Clinical value requires evidence that a surgical target improves outcomes and that robotic delivery adds benefit. Patient-specific models, intraoperative sensing, and decision support require external validation and prospective comparison with optimized conventional care. Adoption should reflect patient-important outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and local practice.

title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Prevention of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Namdari S, Zmistowski B, Fiandeiro M, Gupta S, Nicholson T, ICM Shoulder Group.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is an uncommon but serious complication of shoulder arthroplasty. Many preventive practices are also extrapolated from hip and knee arthroplasty despite important differences in microbiology and surgical procedures. Furthermore, prevention is complicated by the importance of Cutibacterium acnes, which resides within the dermis and sebaceous structures and may not be reliably eliminated by conventional skin preparation. This International Consensus Meeting (ICM) aimed to develop evidence-based consensus recommendations for prevention of shoulder PJI. Methods The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts. More than 100 proposed questions were refined to 86, of which 25 addressed prevention. For each question, delegates performed a systematic literature review and developed a proposed recommendation. Evidence and recommendations were presented to the full group, discussed, revised, and voted upon using a modified Delphi process. Delegates voted agree, disagree, or abstain. Degree of consensus and strength of recommendation were assessed separately. Results Consensus was achieved for all 25 questions, with 65%-100% agreement. Male sex and clinical or physical evidence of malnutrition were identified as PJI risk factors. Moderate-strength evidence supported avoiding corticosteroid injection within 3 months of shoulder arthroplasty, while evidence regarding hemoglobin A1c >8% was conflicting. Consensus supported individualized perioperative management of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis, alcohol-based skin preparation, and avoidance of razor shaving. Evidence was insufficient to determine the effects of testosterone supplementation, diagnostic indication, continuation of antiplatelet therapy before revision, extended oral antibiotic prophylaxis, or antibiotic prophylaxis for dental and other invasive procedures. Evidence was also insufficient to support specific intraoperative interventions for reducing PJI, including intrawound antibiotics, antiseptic irrigation, iodine-impregnated drapes, electrocautery, tranexamic acid, or selection of a particular arthroplasty type. Conclusion The 2025 ICM identified several strategies applicable to current practice while highlighting substantial gaps in shoulder-specific evidence. Many recommendations remain based on limited or extrapolated evidence. Prospective shoulder-specific studies using clinical PJI as the primary outcome are needed to determine which prevention strategies provide meaningful benefit.

title: Post-Treatment Follow-up, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport: Proceedings of the International Consensus Meetings on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
authors: Rubin J, Tham A, Butler JJ, Gauthier P, Hedbany D, Kennedy JG, Smyth NA, Murawski CD, Adams SB, Berlet GC, Buda R, Labib SA, Nunley JA, Raikin SM, Andrews CL, Angthong C, Batista JP, Bayer S, Becher C, Boakye LAT, Brown AJ, Calder JDF, Canata GL, Carreira DS, Clanton TO, Dahmen J, D'Hooghe P, DiGiovanni CW, Dombrowski ME, Ferkel RD, Ferrao PNF, Glazebrook M, Giza E, Gomaa M, Görtz S, Haleem AM, Hamid KS, Hangody L, Hannon CP, Haverkamp D, Hertel J, Hintermann B, Hogan MV, Hunt KJ, Hurley ET, Karlsson J, Kerkhoffs GMMJ, Kim HJ, Kong SW, Lambers KTA, Woo Lee J, Lee KB, Ling JS, Longo UG, Marangon A, McCollum G, Mitchell AW, Mittwede PN, Nehrer S, Niemeyer P, O'Malley MJ, Osei-Hwedieh D, Paul J, Pearce CJ, Pereira H, Popchak A, Prado MP, Reilingh ML, Rothrauff BB, Schon LC, Simpson H, Sofka CM, Spennacchio P, Stone JW, Sullivan M, Takao M, Tanaka Y, Thordarson DB, Tuan R, Valderrabano V, van Bergen CJA, van Dijk CN, van Dijk PAD, Vannini F, Vaseenon T, Walther M, Wiewiorski M, Xu X, Yasui Y, Hua Y, Yoshimura I, Younger ASE, Zhang Z.
abstract: BackgroundPostoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and return to sport (RTS) are key components of recovery following surgical management of osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT). However, substantial variability exists in postoperative protocols, with limited high-quality evidence guiding clinical practicesMethodsInternational experts convened during the International Congress on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle (ICCRA) in Pittsburgh, USA (2017), with subsequent ratification of recommendations in New York, USA (2025). The original consensus statements were developed using a modified Delphi process involving electronic surveys, structured questionnaires, and expert discussion. Consensus strength was defined as consensus (51%-74%), strong consensus (75%-99%), or unanimous (100%). The recommendations addressed postoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and RTS following OLT management.ResultsA total of 16 consensus statements were developed and subsequently ratified, comprising 7 statements addressing post-treatment follow-up and 9 addressing rehabilitation and RTS. All statements achieved strong consensus, with agreement ranging from 75% to 98%. Follow-up recommendations emphasized standardized clinical assessment and patient-reported outcomes, with extended monitoring in select patients. Rehabilitation recommendations supported early controlled motion and progressive weightbearing, with individualized progression according to procedure and clinical performance. Return to sport recommendations emphasized functional recovery and individualized decision-making. Ten statements (63%) were classified exclusively as Grade E, highlighting the limited evidence supporting several recommendations.ConclusionThe ICCRA consensus statements establish a structured framework for postoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and RTS following surgical management of OLT. Despite strong expert agreement, several recommendations remain supported by limited evidence, underlining the need for prospective studies to establish validated, procedure-specific rehabilitation protocols and objective RTS criteria.Level of Evidence: V, expert consensus .

title: Pin-related complications in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 15,874 knees.
authors: Ade-Conde M, Dhanoa D, Wolfstadt JI, Lanting BA, Abdel Khalik H.
abstract: This review evaluated the incidence, characteristics, and management of pin-related complications following robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA). MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from January 1, 2010, to April 15, 2026 for studies evaluating pin-related complications following primary RA-TKA. Pooled complication rates were estimated using a random-effects generalized linear mixed model, and a random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analysis compared complication rates between intra-incisional and extra-incisional tracker pin placement. Descriptive analyses summarized pin techniques, complications, and management. Thirty-seven studies comprising 15,874 RA-TKAs were included with a mean age of 65.5 years, body mass index of 30.5 kg/m², and follow-up of 10.7 months. Femoral pins were most commonly placed intra-incisionally (54.9%), whereas tibial pins were most commonly placed extra-incisionally (52.5%). The random-effects pooled pin-related complication rate was 0.47% (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.90%), compared with a crude rate of 0.89% (142/15,874). Wound complications (n = 93, 0.59%) and fractures (n = 24, 0.15%) were most common. Of the 93 wound complications, 69 (74.2%) occurred at extra-incisional tibial sites. Of 40 pin-related complications with reported management, 70% were managed nonoperatively. Meta-analysis of four studies (5,635 knees) found no significant difference between intra-incisional pin placement (risk ratio [RR] 0.25, 95% CI 0.03-2.06; P = 0.20; I² = 70%). Among RA-TKA pin-related complications with reported management, most were managed nonoperatively. Wound complications were most frequently reported at extra-incisional tibial sites, but comparative evidence did not demonstrate a significant difference between placement strategies. Further comparative studies and standardized reporting are needed to optimize pin safety. PROSPERO ID: CRD420261371245. LOE: IV.

title: Minor Deviations in Cup Center of Rotation Can Reduce Impingement-Free Range of Motion in Total Hip Arthroplasty.
authors: Sullivan M, Clark GW, Chartier L, Esposito CI.
abstract: Background Precise restoration of the acetabular center of rotation (COR) is important for hip biomechanics, particularly in patients with stiff spinopelvic mobility. This study quantified the effect of small COR shifts on impingement-free virtual range of motion (ROM). Methods We retrospectively reviewed the final acetabular component position achieved during robotically assisted total hip arthroplasty in 100 patients. Impingement-free ROM was measured for the final plan, then reassessed after translating the COR 2 mm anteriorly, superiorly, or medially. Patients were stratified by spinopelvic flexibility. Results A 2 mm COR shift altered virtual ROM in 93% of patients. Medial translation increased failure to meet any functional ROM threshold from 16% to 30% ( P P Conclusions Small deviations from planned COR meaningfully reduce virtual ROM and have the greatest impact in patients with stiff spinopelvic mechanics.

title: MRI-based virtual radiographs of the pelvis for assessment of acetabular morphology.
authors: Roshardt JA, Hirt J, Meier MK, Lerch TD, Heimann AF, Tannast M, Hoch A, Sommer S, Sutter R, Steppacher SD, Schmaranzer F.
abstract: Objectives We generated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based virtual radiographs (VRs) from hips with/without intra-articular contrast and compared them with conventional anteroposterior pelvic radiographs (CR) regarding measurement bias, interobserver and intraobserver agreement, and diagnosis of acetabular deformities; we also assessed hip deformity prevalence on VR in asymptomatic participants. Materials and methods Retrospective study of 50 patients (100 hips; mean age 34 years) with femoroacetabular impingement or hip dysplasia undergoing CR and unilateral magnetic resonance arthrography. Additionally, 53 asymptomatic participants underwent noncontrast MRI. Segmentation of the osseous pelvis was performed on T1-weighted volume interpolated breathhold examination (VIBE) Dixon MRI using 3D nnU-Net, pseudo-computed tomography generation, and cone-beam projection to generate VR. Acetabular coverage (lateral center edge angle (LCE), acetabular index (AI), anterior/posterior coverage, extrusion index (EI)), and acetabular version were compared between CR and VR. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and κ statistics; bias with Bland-Altman analysis. Results Interobserver agreement for VR ranged from moderate to almost perfect (ICC/κ 0.60-0.94), except for the AI. LCE showed no significant bias with ( - 0.2° ± 2.5, p = 0.663) or without contrast ( - 0.2° ± 2.2, p = 0.530). Systematic differences occurred for AI, EI, anterior/posterior coverage, and ischial spine sign; 57-75% of discrepancies were within CR interobserver variation. Diagnostic classification showed substantial agreement between CR and VR (κ = 0.62), comparable to CR interobserver agreement (κ = 0.70). In asymptomatic participants, 13% had acetabular dysplasia, 68% normal coverage, and 19% overcoverage. Conclusion MRI-based VR provides acetabular morphology assessment comparable to CR and enables radiation-free evaluation in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations. Key points Question Can MRI-based virtual radiographs reproduce conventional radiographic measurements of acetabular morphology, enabling radiation-free two-dimensional assessment in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations? Findings The lateral center-edge angle showed no significant bias between virtual and conventional radiographs; diagnostic classification of acetabular deformities agreed substantially (κ = 0.62), comparable to conventional radiograph interobserver agreement. Relevance Statement MRI-derived virtual radiographs can provide acetabular measurements comparable to conventional radiographs without ionizing radiation, supporting integration into three-dimensional surgical planning and enabling assessment in young patients and population-based cohorts where repeated radiographs are undesirable.

title: Leuprorelin Acetate for Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy: A Systematic Review of Clinical Efficacy, Long-Term Outcomes, and Safety Considerations.
authors: Wang B, Wang I, Park C, Barkhaus PE, Shirilla D.
abstract: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA; Kennedy disease) is a rare X-linked neuromuscular disorder caused by a CAG repeat expansion in the androgen receptor gene. Leuprorelin acetate, a luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone agonist, suppresses androgen signaling and is approved for SBMA-associated dysphagia in Japan; however, evidence regarding efficacy remains heterogeneous. PubMed and Embase were searched from inception through June 18, 2026, for studies evaluating leuprorelin in genetically confirmed SBMA. Randomized trials, observational cohorts, natural history-controlled studies, extension studies, and safety case reports were included, and findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity. Eleven studies met inclusion criteria, including eight efficacy studies (460 patients) and three safety-focused case reports. Leuprorelin reduced pathogenic androgen receptor accumulation and improved biochemical markers, including serum creatine kinase and creatinine decline. Although neither pivotal randomized trial demonstrated significant short-term functional improvement at 48 weeks, longer-term studies showed slower decline in Revised Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R), Limb Norris, and Norris Bulbar scores and improved event-free survival from pneumonia and death. Benefits were greatest with earlier treatment, particularly disease duration < 10 years. Leuprorelin was generally well tolerated; common adverse effects included hot flushes, sexual dysfunction, and decreased bone mineral density. Leuprorelin may slow long-term functional deterioration in SBMA, with greater benefit following early initiation and prolonged treatment.

title: Injury mechanisms and imaging findings in mixed martial arts.
authors: Thompson G, McCarthy CL.
abstract: Mixed martial arts (MMA) is a rapidly growing combat sport that combines striking and grappling disciplines including boxing, Muay Thai, karate, judo, and Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ). As participation and professional competition increase, musculoskeletal radiologists become increasingly likely to encounter characteristic MMA-related injuries. Although craniofacial trauma, lacerations, and concussion remain the most common injuries in competition, several distinctive musculoskeletal injury patterns arise from grappling, takedowns, and submission techniques. Understanding the biomechanical forces generated by these manoeuvres contributes to accurate image interpretation and appropriate management. Injuries arising from submission techniques are particularly associated with recognisable imaging patterns. The arm bar most commonly results in ulnar collateral ligament injury at the elbow, whereas the Americana and Kimura shoulder locks may produce anterior and posterior capsulolabral injuries respectively. Heel hooks are associated with rotational knee trauma involving the anterior cruciate ligament and collateral ligaments, with injury patterns varying according to whether valgus-external rotation or varus-internal rotation forces are applied. Less common but highly characteristic injuries include combined lateral collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament injury with intact cruciate ligaments as a result of grappling guard positions and choke manoeuvres. This review summarises the major MMA techniques, associated mechanisms of injury, and key imaging findings relevant to musculoskeletal radiologists.

title: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in patients with rheumatic diseases: clinical characteristics, associated factors, and fragility fractures.
authors: Ok NF, Duruöz MT, Gezer HH.
abstract: Background Glucocorticoids (GCs) are widely used in the treatment of rheumatic diseases because of their potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. However, prolonged GC exposure is associated with glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) and an increased risk of fragility fractures. Objectives To determine the prevalence of reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and densitometric osteoporosis and to investigate factors associated with BMD and fragility fractures in patients with rheumatic diseases receiving GC therapy. Methods This cross-sectional medical records review study included 223 patients with rheumatic diseases receiving GC therapy who underwent osteoporosis screening. Clinical characteristics, GC exposure, fragility fractures, laboratory parameters and femoral neck and lumbar spine dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) results were recorded. Patients were classified by the lowest T-score using World Health Organization criteria as normal (T-score > - 1.0), osteopenia (- 2.5 Results Mean age was 59.9 ± 10.9 years; 93.3% were female. Rheumatoid arthritis was the most common diagnosis (54.3%). Among 214 patients with available DXA classification, 16.4% had normal BMD, 55.6% osteopenia and 28.0% osteoporosis; thus, 83.6% had reduced BMD. Patients with reduced BMD were older, had longer disease duration, longer GC treatment duration and higher cumulative GC exposure than those with normal BMD (p Conclusion Reduced BMD was common among patients with rheumatic diseases receiving long-term GC therapy and was associated with older age, longer disease duration and greater GC exposure. Most fragility fractures occurred in patients without densitometric osteoporosis, suggesting that BMD alone may not fully reflect fracture risk in this population. Key points • Reduced BMD (T-score ≤ - 1.0) was present in 83.6% of patients with rheumatic diseases receiving long-term GC therapy, whereas densitometric osteoporosis (T-score ≤ - 2.5) was present in 28.0%. • Fragility fractures were frequent, and approximately two-thirds of patients with fractures did not have densitometric osteoporosis. • Older age, female sex and longer disease duration were independently associated with fragility fractures, highlighting the need for fracture risk assessment beyond BMD alone.

title: Enhanced Diagnosis and Management of Far-Out Syndrome Using 3D Visualization and Uni-Portal Non-Coaxial Spinal Endoscopic Surgery: A Case Report With Literature Review.
authors: Wu H, Chen Z, Cheng X, Dong R, Li T, Qu Y, Song E.
abstract: Background Far-out syndrome (FOS) is an uncommon cause of L5 radiculopathy that may be missed when extraforaminal compression lies beyond routine imaging planes. This report describes the added value of three-dimensional (3D) CT/magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) fusion for diagnosing persistent symptoms after lumbar endoscopic surgery and planning revision decompression. Case presentation A 55-year-old woman had persistent right L5 radiculopathy after unilateral biportal endoscopic discectomy (UBED). CT/MRI suggested L5-S1 extraforaminal stenosis. Patient-specific 3D CT/MRN fusion showed the exiting L5 root compressed by the L5 transverse process, sacral ala, posterior osteophyte, disc protrusion, and ligaments, redirecting revision planning to the extraforaminal zone. Uni-portal non-coaxial spinal endoscopic surgery (UNSES) achieved targeted bony, ligamentous, and disc decompression without vascular, neural, or dural injury. From pre-revision values of VAS 7/10 for back pain and 7/10 for leg pain, ODI 54%, and JOA 5, scores improved at postoperative Day 1 to 3/10, 2/10, 22%, and 23, respectively. At 1, 3, and 6 months, back/leg VAS was 2/1, 1/0, and 1/0; ODI was 24%, 16%, and 8%; and JOA was 23, 25, and 27, respectively. Conclusions In this patient, 3D CT/MRN fusion complemented conventional imaging by integrating bone, disc, and nerve anatomy and directly informing revision decompression. UNSES was feasible, with improvement maintained through 6 months. As a single case, these findings support clinical feasibility and educational value rather than general efficacy or safety.

title: Efficacy of diadynamic currents versus transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation in subjects with overactive bladder syndrome: A double-blind randomized controlled trial.
authors: Tedla JS, Lalaji SL, Midde AK, Papalkar NA, Bindhu Priya N, Sangadala DR, Reddy RS, Mukherjee D, Alamri AM, Alzahrani AS, Alhadi NA.
abstract: Background In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment. Methodology A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18-80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269. Results The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant. Conclusion Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of 3D MRI rendering techniques for evaluation of hourglass-like constrictions in Parsonage-Turner syndrome.
authors: Shakoor D, McKinney EJ, Queler SC, Davis-Hayes C, Hao M, Baker A, Wang SH, Tan ET, Sneag DB.
abstract: Objective To evaluate inter-reader agreement and diagnostic accuracy of curved multiplanar reformatting (cMPR) and maximum intensity projection (MIP) techniques for detecting hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs). Materials and methods Thirty brachial plexus 3-Tesla, 3D, 1-mm isotropic MR neurography (MRN) datasets (10 patients without and 20 patients with Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS) affecting the suprascapular nerve (SSN)) were retrospectively analyzed by four musculoskeletal radiology fellows for the number and severity of HGCs using both post-processing views in a randomized, blinded fashion. An experienced, attending radiologist served as the reference standard. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's AC1 and intraclass correlation (ICC). Image interpretation time was compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results Inter-reader agreement for HGC presence was substantial to almost perfect among fellows (cMPR AC1 = 0.7, MIP AC1 = 0.67) and when compared to the attending (cMPR AC1 = 0.67-0.83, MIP AC1 = 0.63-0.83). Agreement for severe HGC count was substantial to almost perfect (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.65, MIP ICC = 0.79; vs. attending: ICC = 0.62-0.83, MIP ICC = 0.69-0.88), but poor to fair for mild HGCs (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.23, MIP ICC = 0.26; vs. attending: ICC = 0-0.21, MIP ICC = 0-0.09). Sensitivity to HGC presence was excellent (cMPR, 85-100%; MIP, 90-100%), though specificity (cMPR, 50-100%; MIP, 40-90%) and diagnostic accuracy (cMPR, 80-90%; MIP, 76-90%) varied. The MIP method required significantly less interpretation time than cMPR (median: 33 vs. 104 s, p Conclusion High inter-reader agreement and sensitivity but variable specificity for HGC detection suggest both techniques are viable tools for MRN, with cMPR better suited for detailed HGC evaluation and MIP for initial screening.

title: Cone-Beam CT-Guided SpineJack® vertebral augmentation: A reproducible technique for accurate pedicular access and implant deployment.
authors: Dien E, Grange S, Mondon P, Peraldi L, Lavigne J, Chalamet B, Ben-Rejeb MI, Bouchet M, Gleyzolle A, Ahoury N Guessan J, Barrey C, Amoretti N, Pialat JB, Stacoffe N.
abstract: Background SpineJack® vertebral augmentation requires precise bilateral transpedicular access and accurate implant deployment. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and technical performance of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-guided SpineJack augmentation. Methods This retrospective single-institution, two-site study included consecutive CBCT-guided procedures performed between May 2021 and April 2026. Technical success required planned bilateral implantation, expansion, and cement augmentation without pedicle breach or implant malposition on final CBCT. Secondary outcomes included immediate vertebral height restoration, complications, procedure duration, radiation exposure, and treatment setting. Results The analysis included 178 procedures; median age was 45 years (interquartile range [IQR], 27-59), and 158 procedures (88.8%) involved traumatic fractures. Technical success was 100% (178/178), including 64 procedures (36.0%) with pedicle-implant clearance Conclusions CBCT-guided SpineJack augmentation achieved accurate bilateral implant deployment and substantial immediate vertebral height restoration without major procedure-related complications. These findings support CBCT as a reliable guidance strategy for vertebral augmentation, with demonstrated feasibility in outpatient practice.

title: Computational biomechanics of capsulolabral stress and elongation in Hill-Sachs bone defect: a finite element method aimed at patient-specific prediction of glenohumeral instability.
authors: Suarez-Hernandez ML, Urriolagoitia-Sosa G, Romero-Ángeles B, Carrasco-Hernández F, Martines-Reyes J, Ramirez-Sanchez G, Mar-Luna FJ, Lopez-Zumaran IA, Rocha-Martinez MN.
abstract: Hill-Sachs is a compression fracture of the posterolateral humeral head that occurs in up to 93% of patients with recurrent anterior glenohumeral instability. Although previous research has primarily focused on the osseous defect, joint stability depends on a complex interaction between the soft tissue biomechanics (bone, cartilage, labrum, capsule, and ligaments). The mechanical interaction between the Hill-Sachs defect and joint soft tissues remains insufficiently characterized. This study used finite-element method analysis to evaluate the biomechanical response of the capsulolabral complex to humeral head defects of different sizes in the abduction and external rotation position. A patient-specific computational model of the glenohumeral joint was reconstructed from computed tomography; based on data from a female volunteer. Five defect sizes were simulated: 0% (healthy for reference), 6%, 9%, 31%, and 44% of the humeral head.
