This study sought to compare STS ability and gait symmetry between older adults with sarcopenia alone (SP group) and the SO group, and to analyze the biomechanical and neuromuscular differences associated with varying levels of body fat. A cohort of 60 elderly individuals diagnosed with sarcopenia was stratified into SP and SO groups according to the Chinese diagnostic criteria for sarcopenia and obesity. Functional performance was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS), the Five Times Sit-to-Stand Test, the Timed Up and Go Test, and phase-specific STS timing. Gait and plantar pressure symmetry indices were evaluated utilizing motion capture and pedobarographic systems. The SO group demonstrated significantly lower BBS scores, extended durations for the Five Times Sit-to-Stand Test and Timed Up and Go Test, and prolonged STS phase times (P < .05). Additionally, this group exhibited reduced knee joint angular velocities and increased asymmetry in the stance phase, swing phase, single-limb support, and foot rotation (P < .05). No significant differences were observed in the symmetry indices for step length and step time. Sarcopenic obesity was associated with poorer sit-to-stand performance and greater gait asymmetry in older adults compared with sarcopenia alone. Body composition assessment and gait analysis may provide complementary information for functional evaluation.

title: Single Antibiotic Use With Ceftriaxone for Prophylaxis of All Open Fractures.
authors: Koulopoulos MW, Buseck A, Lynch CP, Lutz K, Brand O, Sommers E, Pompo I, Laychur A, Vaughn J, Mann K, Sullivan MP.
abstract: Objectives To compare outcomes for open fractures treated with a prophylactic antibiotic protocol using ceftriaxone (CTX) for all open fractures, referred to as group "CTX," versus a previous protocol using cefazolin for Gustilo I/II fractures and cefazolin plus gentamicin or CTX monotherapy for Gustilo type III fractures only, referred to as group "Classic." Methods . Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria This study included adult patients undergoing surgery for an open fracture from December 2016 to December 2022 with a minimum follow-up of 3 months. Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome of deep infection and secondary outcomes of superficial infection rates, nonunion rate, and time to antibiotic administration were compared between overall groups and subgroups based on Gustilo type. Results A total of 521 patients were included. Baseline characteristics were similar between groups, with no differences in age (CTX 41.1 ± 19.7 vs. classic 39.5 ± 19.3), sex (68.5% vs. 72.0% male), or comorbidities ( P > 0.05). There were no differences in deep infection (7.8% vs. 12.7%, P = 0.095), superficial infection (7.0% vs. 4.7%, P = 0.427), or nonunion (10.3% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.500) between CTX and Classic groups for all Gustilo types. Similarly for only type I/II fractures, rates of deep infection (3.5% vs. 8.9%, P = 0.145), superficial infection (2.9% vs. 3.6%, P = 0.683), and nonunion (3.6% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.340) did not differ. Noninferiority of CTX for deep infection was demonstrated for all Gustilo types (intergroup difference -0.048, P = 0.027) and type I/II fractures (-0.054, P = 0.035). The CTX protocol was associated with shorter time to antibiotic administration (63.9 ± 116.9 vs. 114.1 ± 199.0 minutes, P = 0.002). Conclusions The use of CTX for prophylaxis of all open fractures, regardless of Gustilo type, was associated with noninferior outcomes in deep infection as well as shorter time to antibiotic administration, compared with a regimen where type I/II fractures received cefazolin. No significant differences in rates of superficial infection or nonunion were noted after transition to CTX protocol. The study was notably underpowered to detect a difference in the primary outcome of deep infection. Prophylaxis of all open fractures with CTX may be a safe and effective method of standardizing and expediting care for orthopaedic trauma patients. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Risk factors and morbidity characteristics of surgical site infection following ankle fracture ORIF: A comprehensive analysis.
authors: Zhao C, Fan X, Pang C.
abstract: This study aimed to describe the incidence and microbiological characteristics of surgical site infection (SSI) after open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of ankle fractures and identify clinical factors associated with SSI. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 248 patients who underwent ankle fracture ORIF between January and December 2023. SSI occurring within 30 postoperative days was identified from available inpatient and postoperative medical records. Demographic, injury-related, laboratory, and perioperative variables were compared between patients with and without SSI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations with SSI. SSI occurred in 32 of 248 patients (12.9%), including 25 superficial and 7 deep infections. Cultured organisms included Escherichia coli (n = 10), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 7), Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 6), Enterobacter cloacae (n = 5), and Staphylococcus epidermidis (n = 4). In multivariable analysis, open fracture, wound class II-III, and neutrophil percentage > 75% were associated with SSI. Age and body mass index (BMI) also showed positive associations, although the precise unit-specific effect sizes could not be reliably reconstructed from the archived statistical analysis; these comparatively large per-unit estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of SSI events and potential residual confounding. SSI occurred in 12.9% of this single-center ankle fracture cohort. Older age and higher BMI showed associations with SSI, together with open fracture, less-clean operative wounds, and neutrophilia. The magnitude of the age- and BMI-related effects should be interpreted cautiously because their original regression scaling could not be independently reconstructed.

title: Risk Factors for Failure of Internal Fixation in Postmenopausal Patients With Osteoporotic Intertrochanteric Fractures.
authors: Yu Y, Zhao S, Li H, Jiang Z, Liang Y, Wang S.
abstract: Aim To identify independent risk factors for internal fixation failure after intramedullary nail fixation in postmenopausal patients with osteoporotic intertrochanteric fractures, and to develop and internally validate a predictive model for risk assessment. Methods The clinical data of 360 postmenopausal patients with osteoporotic intertrochanteric fractures admitted to The Second Affiliated Hospital of Liaoning University of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2021 to May 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. The patients were divided into the failure group ( n = 65) and the success group ( n = 295) according to whether internal fixation failure occurred within 6 months after the operation. General data, bone metabolism indices, imaging parameters, and surgery-related factors were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to screen the independent risk factors of internal fixation failure. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to evaluate the model's discriminative ability, while the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and bootstrap resampling calibration curve were used to evaluate calibration. Decision curve analysis was used to assess the clinical utility of the model. Results The failure rate of internal fixation was 18.06% (65/360). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that the quality of fracture reduction was poor (odds ratio (OR) = 3.07, 95% CI: 1.60-5.87, p p = 0.02) was identified as an independent risk factor for internal fixation failure, whereas bone mineral density (BMD) T-score (OR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.06-0.47, p p p p = 0.28), and the calibration curve closely aligned with the ideal line. Decision curve analysis showed that the model had significant net clinical benefit within a wide threshold probability range. Conclusions Poor quality of fracture reduction, the position of the intramedullary nail deviated from the center of the medullary cavity, lower bone mineral density, lower femoral cortical thickness index, and smaller lateral wall thickness are independent risk factors for the failure of internal fixation after intramedullary nail fixation in postmenopausal women with osteoporotic intertrochanteric fractures. The predictive model based on these factors demonstrates good discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. Clinicians should pay close attention to the identified risk factors, thoroughly evaluate preoperative bone quality, achieve anatomical reduction, and ensure optimal positioning of the main nail during operation to reduce the risk of internal fixation failure and improve patient outcomes.

title: Risk Factors for Bone Cement Leakage and Re-fracture Following PKP in Patients With Thoracolumbar Spine Fractures.
authors: Li X, Fu M, Liu X, E Z, Wang C.
abstract: Aim Thoracolumbar spine fractures are commonly treated with percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP), but bone cement leakage and re-fracture remain major concerns. Identifying their risk factors is essential for improving prognosis but remains insufficiently characterized. This study was designed to explore the risk factors for bone cement leakage and re-fracture following PKP in patients with thoracolumbar spine fractures. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 115 patients with thoracolumbar spine fractures who underwent PKP at Heilongjiang Provincial Hospital between April 2022 and February 2025 (leakage group: 18 patients with bone cement leakage; non-leakage group: 97 patients without leakage). Risk factors for bone cement leakage were analyzed. Patients were divided into re-fracture (29 cases with re-fractures) and non-re-fracture (86 cases without re-fractures) groups to identify risk factors for postoperative re-fracture. Results Logistic multivariate regression analysis identified age and vertebral wall destruction as independent risk factors for postoperative bone cement leakage ( p p Conclusions Age and vertebral wall destruction are independent predictors of cement leakage, and together with compression severity, also predict re-fracture. These findings support routine preoperative assessment of vertebral wall integrity using high-resolution computed tomography (CT), particularly in elderly patients, as vertebral wall destruction was independently associated with bone cement leakage.

title: Risk Assessment for Reoperation After Surgery for Lumbar Degenerative Disease Based on Preoperative Clinical Characteristics and Imaging Parameters: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Jiang J, Xu L, Zhou L, Xiong J, Tao Z.
abstract: Aim To explore the relevant clinical and radiological risk factors for reoperation in patients with lumbar degenerative diseases, and to inform preoperative risk stratification. Methods This was a single-center retrospective cohort study. A total of 653 patients with lumbar degenerative diseases who underwent initial surgical treatment at Nanchang Hongdu Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine Affiliated to Jiangxi University of Chinese Medicine between June 2018 and June 2022 were included. All patients completed a 36-month follow-up. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, perioperative parameters, and preoperative imaging parameters were collected, including the degree of intervertebral disc degeneration (Pfirrmann classification), the degree of paraspinal muscle fat infiltration (Goutallier classification), facet joint effusion distribution, and facet joint angles. Patients were divided into a reoperation group (n = 41) and a non-reoperation group (n = 612) based on whether they underwent reoperation for complications related to the index surgical segment during the follow-up period. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent factors associated with postoperative reoperation, and their discriminative ability was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results The reoperation rate within 36 months postoperatively was 6.28% (41/653). Final multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that age (Odds Ratio [OR] = 1.11, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] 1.06~1.15, p p p = 0.004) were independent risk factors for reoperation. Compared with patients with bilateral effusion or synovial cysts, patients with unilateral effusion had a significantly lower risk of reoperation (OR = 0.03, 95% CI 0.00~0.23, p Conclusions Age, preoperative pain level, intervertebral disc degeneration grade, and facet joint effusion status (bilateral effusion or synovial cyst vs. unilateral effusion) may be closely related to the risk of reoperation after lumbar degenerative disease surgery. Patients with these characteristics should be thoroughly evaluated preoperatively to inform the development of individualized treatment strategies.

title: Reproducibility of Two Novel Bone Defect Classification Systems.
authors: Campbell ST, Campbell ST, Agel J, Levack AE, Bernstein M, Wallace SJ, Meinberg E, Quinnan S, Hernandez-Irizarry R, Saiz AM, Crist BD, Marmor M, Shymon SJ, Lee P, Githens MF, Marecek GS, Orthopaedic Trauma Association.
abstract: Objectives To determine the reproducibility of 2 novel bone defect classification systems, the Tetsworth classification system and the universal long bone defect (ULBD) classification system. Methods Two independent reproducibility studies were undertaken. A series of cases with bone defects was collected and sent to a panel of orthopaedic surgeons who were members of the OTA or Limb Lengthening and Reconstruction Society who routinely manage bone defects. The surgeons were provided with a measurement calibration scale for defect length assessment. Analysis of reproducibility was performed using a Fleiss multirater kappa model, where a Fleiss kappa of 0 indicated agreement no better than random chance, and 1 indicated perfect agreement. Surgeons also rated their confidence in their rating from 1 to 3, with 3 as "very confident." Results For the Tetsworth classification, the Fleiss kappa was 0.264 for the overall classification system (fair agreement) (95% CI, 0.224-0.305). The kappa for the D1, D2, D3 part of the code related to defect completeness (incomplete, subcritical, or critical) was 0.557 (moderate agreement) (95% CI, 0.446-0.648). The kappa for the A, B, C part of the code related to defect shape was 0.402 (moderate agreement) (95% CI, 0.323-0.480). The mean confidence for all cases was 2.46 (range, 1.86-3). For the ULBD classification, the Fleiss kappa for the entire classification was 0.133 (slight agreement) (95% CI, 0.123-0.144). The kappa for the location and segment was 0.568 (moderate agreement) (95% CI, 0.526-0.610). The kappa for the morphology component was 0.124 (slight agreement) (95% CI, 0.114-0.135). The mean confidence for all cases was 2.0 (range, 1.0-3.0). Conclusions The bone defect classification system proposed by Tetsworth et al was reproducible by surgeons familiar with bone defects. The system can be considered for future research use. The ULBD classification system had low overall reproducibility. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Preoperative High-Sensitivity Troponin and Risk of In-Hospital Mortality and Cardiac Events After Hip Fracture Surgery.
authors: Touré A, Okafor K, Medilien B, Mather R, Parry J, Hernandez-Irizarry RC, Bradley CA, Ahn J, Schenker ML.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether preoperative high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) elevation predicted in-hospital cardiac events and mortality after hip fracture surgery, and whether surgical delay modified this relationship. Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single Level 1 trauma center in the United States. Patient selection criteria Adult patients who underwent hip fracture surgery between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2024, and had a preoperative hs-cTn measurement as part of routine perioperative assessment were included. Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital cardiac event or mortality. Secondary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and in-hospital cardiac events analyzed separately. Outcomes were compared across preoperative troponin categories defined as normal ( 100 ng/L), and across surgical delay categories defined as 48 hours. Results A total of 510 patients were included. The mean age was 76.3 ± 14.1 years, and 291 patients (57.1%) were female. Preoperative troponin was normal in 424 patients (83.1%), elevated in 58 patients (11.4%), and significantly elevated in 28 patients (5.5%). Thirty-five patients (6.9%) experienced the composite outcome. The composite outcome occurred in 19 of 424 patients (4.5%) with normal troponin, 6 of 58 patients (10.3%) with elevated troponin, and 10 of 28 patients (35.7%) with significantly elevated troponin ( P Conclusions Preoperative hs-cTn elevation was independently associated with in-hospital cardiac events and mortality after hip fracture surgery. Troponin levels greater than 100 ng/L identified patients at highest risk, independent of surgical delay. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Photon-counting CT of Spinal Canal Stenosis Induced by Gouty Tophi.
authors: Wei X, Zhou Z.

title: Periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary hip arthroplasty : should the choice of femoral component design and fixation method vary according to the sex and age of the patient?
authors: Børsheim S, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, Gjertsen JE, Furnes O, Dybvik E, Lie SA, Dale H.
abstract: Aims Periprosthetic femoral fracture is a severe complication following hip arthroplasty, influenced by the design of the femoral component and the method of fixation. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of sex and age on the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture. Methods We analyzed 204,041 primary hip arthroplasties from the Norwegian Arthroplasty Register and the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register (1 January 2005 to 31 December 2025). Femoral components were categorized as cemented composite beam (CB), cemented polished taper-slip (PTS), uncemented collarless (UCC-), and uncemented collared (UCC+). Cox regression analysis was used to compare the risk (adjusted hazard rate ratio (aHRR)) of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture stratified by sex and age. Results In males, PTS and UCC- had a nine-times higher risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture than CB. For UCC+, the risk was four times higher than CB. The risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in males aged > 65 years for UCC-; for UCC+ the risk was increased in males aged > 75 years, whereas PTS had higher risk for periprosthetic femoral fracture at all ages, compared with CB. In females, the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in those aged > 70 years for PTS and UCC+ compared with CB, whereas for UCC- the risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture was higher in those aged > 60 years, compared with CB. Conclusion Our findings suggest that CB should be the preferred choice of femoral component, at least for males aged > 75 years and females aged > 70 years. UCC+ components were the best uncemented option, while the use of PTS components was associated with a high risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture among males of all ages.

title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
authors: Zaed I, Ricciardi L, Mezzapesa FP, Di Cosmo L, Ganau M, Iaccarino C, Chibbaro S, Todeschi J, Mallereau CH, Cardia A, Milani D.
abstract: Aim Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported. Methods We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition. Results Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p p p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups. Conclusions In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.

title: Pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block with lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) block versus fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) for hip surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Wang MY, Du MQ, Xu YN, Wang Y, Yao SL, Wu X.
abstract: Background Effective analgesia that preserves motor function is essential for early mobilization after hip surgery. Although fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) is recommended for total hip arthroplasty, the comparative efficacy of combined pericapsular nerve group and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve blocks (PENG + LFCN) remains uncertain. Methods Databases including Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Central, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched up to December 8, 2024. Statistical analyses were performed using Review Manager (RevMan) (computer program, version 5.4, The Cochrane Collaboration, 2020). Results Seven randomized controlled trials involving 572 participants were included. Compared with FICB, PENG + LFCN significantly reduced static pain at 12 hours (mean difference [MD] = -0.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.28 to -0.11; P Conclusion PENG + LFCN may provide superior early analgesia and better preserve lower-limb motor function than FICB after hip surgery. However, the evidence is limited by few trials, small sample sizes, and substantial heterogeneity. Larger, adequately powered trials are warranted.

title: Patient-Reported Outcomes after Distal Radius Fractures Differ Across Geographic and Cultural Populations: A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Bilodeau RE, Bhadouriya RS, Klinger CE, van der List JP, Oquendo YA, Haeberle HS, Victory L, Katzir A, Barth KA, Dvorzhinskiy A, Ricci WM.
abstract: Objectives To assess patient reported outcome (PRO) heterogeneity across different cultural and geographical regions through a systematic review and meta-analysis of PROs after volar plate fixation of distal radius fractures. Methods Data sources PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were queried for randomized controlled trials from 2010 to 2023 reporting Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH), QuickDASH, Patient-Rated Wrist Evaluation (PRWE), or Visual Analog Scale (VAS) PROs. Study selection Randomized controlled trials with treatment arms consisting of open reduction and internal fixation using a volar locking plate for adult distal radius fracture (OTA/AO 23) and reported DASH, QuickDASH, PRWE, or VAS PROs were included. Studies not published in English or that provided insufficient extraction data were excluded. Data extraction Studies were characterized by country of origin, continent of origin, and cultural region of origin. Extracted data included PRO outcomes, patient demographics, and follow-up ranges. Data synthesis Random-effects meta-analysis was performed with restricted maximum likelihood method, and subgroup analyses were performed to determine differences in pooled PROs across geographical and cultural regions. Results A total of 52 treatment arms met inclusion criteria for DASH analysis, 33 for PRWE, and 23 for VAS. Significant mean DASH score heterogeneity existed across all studies ( P Conclusions PROs after distal radius volar plate fixation demonstrated meaningful variation across cultural and geographic contexts. Outcomes from one cultural region may not be globally generalizable. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level II. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease.
authors: Downie S, Kennedy M, Farhan-Alanie OM, Kennedy IW, McKean G, Kelly MP, Young PS.
abstract: Aims Cemented arthroplasty has previously been recommended for treating metastatic bone disease (MBD) around the hip. However, cementing has disadvantages, including restricted femoral component length, loosening due to disease progression, and bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). A long uncemented implant spanning the whole femur could negate these disadvantages; however, there is a paucity of data regarding their use. Our aim was to assess the outcomes of a long uncemented femoral component in MBD. Methods A total of 205 patients with MBD underwent femoral reconstruction using the Restoration Modular Revision Hip System Plasma stem between January 2008 and December 2025. They were identified from the prospectively collected database of a tertiary MBD service. Any patient with symptomatic bone metastases involving the acetabulum or femur, with completed or impending pathological fracture, were included. The primary endpoint was reintervention for femoral implant failure, with exclusion of reintervention for deep infection and/or instability. Results Indications for surgery included pathological fracture (46 of 205; 22%) or lesions at risk of fracture (78%; n = 159). The mean follow-up was 45 months (12 to 131). A total of 140 patients (68%) died during the study period (mean 20 months (0.1 to 128) postoperatively). The mean distance from the centre of the femoral head to the most distal femoral metastasis was 126 mm (5 to 369). Using death as a competing risk, two-year probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and probability of death was 0.507 (95% CI 0.436 to 0.577). At five years, probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and the risk of death was 0.703 (95% CI 0.629 to 0.776). Overall complication rate requiring further surgery was 8% (16 out of 205) with three reinterventions for femoral implant failure (all periprosthetic femoral fractures). Conclusion This implant demonstrates promising short- to mid-term survivorship, with no patient requiring femoral revision for loosening and a comparatively low complication rate. A long uncemented femoral component may be an appropriate option in selected patients presenting with symptomatic bone metastases around the hip.

title: Osteoporosis treatment gaps and risk of recurrent hip fracture following initial fragility fracture: Insights from over one million cases.
authors: Laurore C, Lezak BA, Xie J, Avila A, Hong C, Yassin S, Ganta A, Egol KA, Konda SR.
abstract: Introduction Patients who sustain a hip fracture are at high risk of a second hip fracture, yet most do not receive osteoporosis pharmacotherapy. We evaluated the association between bone-health medication initiation after a first hip fracture and the risk of a second hip fracture. Methods This retrospective cohort study used Epic Cosmos, a de-identified multi-institutional electronic health record database. Adults who underwent surgery for a first femoral neck, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric hip fracture were classified as having no bone-health medication, as baseline users (medication documented at admission), or as initiators within six months of the index fracture. Second hip fracture was assessed over fixed 1-, 2- and 5-year horizons. We estimated absolute risks, cumulative incidence accounting for death as a competing risk, and multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models. Results Overall, 1,051,020 patients were eligible for the 5-year analysis: 705,059 (67.1%) had no medication, 83,452 (7.9%) were baseline users and 262,509 (25.0%) initiated medication within six months. Five-year cumulative incidence of second hip fracture was 17.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] 17.1-17.3) with no medication, 14.1% (95% CI 13.8-14.4) among baseline users and 8.9% (95% CI 8.8-9.1) among initiators. In adjusted models, the hazard of second hip fracture was lower among baseline users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71, 95% CI 0.69-0.73) and initiators (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.37-0.39) than among patients with no medication. Conclusions Initiation of bone-health medication within six months of a first hip fracture was associated with a lower risk of a second hip fracture. Baseline users had intermediate risk, which may reflect confounding by indication, agent selection or adherence. These findings support early, coordinated post-fracture osteoporosis treatment; the observational design precludes causal inference.

title: Nail-Plate Constructs Permit Early Weight Bearing and Improved Outcomes Compared With Single Device Constructs in the Treatment of Distal Femur Fractures at One-Year Follow-Up: A Retrospective Analysis.
authors: Patel UJ, Holloway MR, Guedikian CR, Soin SP, Joseph NM, Ketz JP.
abstract: Objectives To investigate clinical, radiographic, and patient reported outcomes in patients undergoing surgical fixation for distal femur fractures with single device construct (lateral locked plate or intramedullary nail) or nail-plate combination. Methods . Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single, academic, tertiary Level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria The inclusion criteria were patients with DFFs (OTA/AO 33) treated operatively with lateral locked plate, IM nail, or nail-plate combination between January 2011 and December 2023 with a minimum follow up of 1 year. Outcome measures and comparisons Radiographic fracture healing, complication rates, weight-bearing status, length of stay, gait impairment, and patient-reported outcomes using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System were investigated. Multivariable regression models were used to identify predictors of union, reoperation, discharge disposition, and postoperative complications. Results A total of 191 patients were included, with 153 (131 lateral locked plate, 22 intramedullary nail) treated with a single device construct (mean age 72 years [range 22-95], 16% male) and 38 treated with nail-plate combination constructs (mean age 70 years [range 19-94], 16% male). At one-year postoperatively, nail-plate combination versus single device constructs were associated with significantly lower rates of nonunion (0% vs. 12%, P = 0.03), reoperation (10% vs. 26%, P = 0.05), and gait impairment (26% vs. 58%, P Conclusions Fixation with nail-plate combination constructs, compared with single device constructs, in DFFs seemed to support immediate weight bearing and was associated with improved short-term and midterm outcomes, including reduced rates of nonunion, reoperation, and functional impairment at 1 year. These advantages may be especially relevant for geriatric patients and those with complex or periprosthetic fracture patterns, or with preoperative risk factors for nonunion and functional decline. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Lymphedema as a Significant Risk Factor for Primary Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Failure: A Systematic Review.
authors: Zandi R, Mehrvar A, Keyhaninejad N, Shaterzadeh-Bojd S, Talebi S, Foroughi E, Gouhari F, Abdashti AA, Ehsani A.
abstract: Background Total hip and knee arthroplasty are highly effective for improving quality of life, alleviating pain, and enhancing physical function. However, failure of these joint replacements inflicts considerable burdens on patients and the healthcare system. The impact of lymphedema, as an uncommon comorbidity, in patients undergoing total hip and knee arthroplasties remains unknown. This study aimed to assess the most recent publications and evaluate the results and post-operative complications of total joint arthroplasty in patients with preoperative lymphedema. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases was conducted up to 25th October 2024 to identify relevant studies. Inclusion of studies was established through the application of a predetermined protocol by three independent reviewers. Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal checklists were used for risk of bias assessment. Results Seven articles met the inclusion criteria. Five studies evaluated the outcomes of lymphedema in total knee arthroplasty, one in total hip arthroplasty, and one in total hip and knee arthroplasty. Lymphedema is a significant risk factor for postoperative complications in total hip and knee arthroplasty. The findings highlight the significance of patient optimization and enable improved lymphedema patient counseling. Conclusion Although lymphedema can be measured as a significant risk factor for complications in total hip and knee arthroplasty, further studies are required to investigate and confirm this relationship.

title: InSafeLock endopin versus conventional distal locking screws for femoral shaft fractures: A comparative laboratory biomechanical study.
authors: Özcan S, Yurten H, Çelen ZE.
abstract: The InSafeLock femoral nail is a recently developed implant that uses endopin instead of screws in its distal locking mechanism. This study aimed to compare the biomechanical features of the distal locking mechanisms of InSafeLock and conventional nails. Twenty-four artificial femoral bones were used for mechanical tests. InSafeLock nails with endopin (Group 1) and conventional nails with distal locking screws (Group 2) were inserted into the artificial bones. The biomechanical features were evaluated using axial compression and rotational performance tests. There was no statistically significant difference between Group 1 and Group 2 in the axial compression displacement tests (P = .683). No visual damage was observed on the artificial bones or intramedullary nails after axial compression fatigue tests in either group. During axial compression failure testing performed after fatigue testing, the mean failure load of Group 1 was significantly lower than that of Group 2 (1132.5 ± 15.5 N vs 11,965.5 ± 9.5 N, respectively; P = .002). Rotational performance tests showed that the torsional yield strength of the groups was not statistically different (P = .333). While the InSafeLock endopin offers ease in distal locking, it exhibits a significantly lower failure load under high axial compression forces than conventional screws.

title: Hip-related tenotomy and progression to severe displacement of the hip in nonambulant children with cerebral palsy : a nationwide cohort study.
authors: Bakhtiyar M, Iljazi A, Wong C, Petersen MM, Balslev-Clausen A.
abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to investigate whether a hip-related tenotomy is associated with a lower risk of severe hip outcomes in nonambulant children with cerebral palsy and established displacement of the hip. Methods This nationwide register-based cohort study included children classified as Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level IV or V who were enrolled in the Danish Cerebral Palsy Follow-Up Program (CPOP) between 1 January 2008 and 31 December 2023. Hips with a baseline migration percentage (MP) of between 30% and 49% were included and followed until the first occurrence of a severe hip outcome, defined as a MP of ≥ 50% or osteotomy of the hip. Death was treated as a competing event. The cumulative incidence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen estimator. Associations were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regression with cluster-robust standard errors. Results A total of 259 children, contributing 406 hips, were included, of which 110 underwent a tenotomy. At ten years, the cumulative incidence of a severe hip outcome was 34.7% (95% CI 28.8 to 40.7) without tenotomy, and 20.4% (95% CI 12.4 to 28.5) with tenotomy. In adjusted competing-risk regression, tenotomy was associated with a significantly lower risk of a severe hip outcome (sub-distribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.53 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.84); p = 0.006). GMFCS-specific Fine-Gray analyses showed a significant association in GMFCS level IV (sHR 0.35 (95% CI 0.16 to 0.78); p = 0.010), whereas the association did not reach significance in GMFCS level V (sHR 0.68 (95% CI 0.40 to 1.19); p = 0.180). Spasticity, as classified according to the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) 1 and ≥ 3, was independently associated with a significantly increased risk of a severe hip outcome. Conclusion A hip-related tenotomy was associated with a significantly lower incidence of the subsequent development of a severe hip outcome among nonambulant children with established displacement of the hip, particularly in GMFCS level IV. In GMFCS level V, progression remained substantial irrespective of the soft-tissue release, emphasizing the importance of careful patient selection and continued surveillance.

title: Highlights of the Annual Scientific Meeting of the Australasian Musculoskeletal Imaging Group (AMSIG) 2026, Sydney, Australia.
Health-related quality of life following periprosthetic femoral fracture after total hip arthroplasty : a propensity score-matched cohort study with trajectory analysis.
authors: Ablett AD, Powell-Bowns MFR, Super JT, Neo C, Yapp LZ, Clement ND, Scott CEH.
abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to quantify the impact of a postoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture following a primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) compared with normal values in the general population, and to assess the agreement between recalled pre-fracture and prospectively collected PROMs. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study involved 140 operatively managed patients with a periprosthetic femoral fracture which was sustained around a primary THA, between 2007 and 2025, with a minimum follow-up of one year. The EQ-5D-3L, EQ-VAS, and Oxford Hip Score (OHS) were collected at a median of 2.9 years (IQR 1.9 to 5.5) after the fracture. Complete case propensity score matching (1:5) balanced patients who had a periprosthetic fracture with Health Survey for England general population controls (n = 700) by sex, age, and deprivation. An agreement cohort with data from a linked arthroplasty database enabled comparison between prospectively collected PROMs one year after THA and recalled pre-fracture PROMs, as well as the analysis of PROMs at four timepoints (before THA, one year after THA, pre-fracture recall, and after the periprosthetic femoral fracture). Results The mean EQ-5D-3L scores after periprosthetic femoral fracture were significantly lower than those in the matched general population (mean difference -0.209 (95% CI -0.264 to -0.154); p Conclusion A periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary THA was associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in PROMs in about two-thirds of patients, with one-in-ten reporting health states worse than death, at a median follow-up of about three years. These findings have important implications when counselling patients and for targeted strategies designed to prevent a periprosthetic femoral fracture.

title: Gadolinium Retention in Pediatric Bone: Linear versus Macrocyclic MRI Contrast Agents.
authors: Roberts DR, Moore RD, Harrison A, Rosenberg MJ, Hlavacek AM, Kavarana MN, Bradley SM, Davis WC.
abstract: Background Gadolinium retention in bone after gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA) exposure is documented in adults but unquantified in children, who may have higher cumulative doses from early imaging. Purpose To quantify and compare residual gadolinium in pediatric bone tissue after macrocyclic and linear GBCA exposure. Materials and Methods In this prospective pilot study, individuals under 18 years of age scheduled for median sternotomy who had undergone clinically indicated GBCA-enhanced or unenhanced MRI were included between January 2018 and August 2024 at a single academic medical center and categorized into three groups: linear GBCA exposed (gadobenate), macrocyclic GBCA exposed (gadoterate), and control (no GBCA exposure). Bone samples were obtained during surgery and analyzed for gadolinium concentration (micrograms of gadolinium per gram of bone tissue). Linear regression modeling was used to analyze the impact of GBCA exposure on bone gadolinium concentration. Results A total of 29 individuals were included: nine exposed to linear GBCA (median age, 12.0 years [IQR, 4.0-14.0 years]; five male individuals), 11 exposed to macrocyclic GBCA (median age, 13.0 years [IQR, 3.3-14.8 years]; eight male individuals), and nine control individuals (median age, 1.8 years [IQR, 0.5-6.3 years]; seven male individuals). Gadolinium was detected in bone tissue in all groups. Median bone gadolinium concentrations were 0.001 μg/g (IQR, 0.0007-0.0015 μg/g) with no GBCA exposure, 0.007 μg/g (IQR, 0.004-0.011 μg/g) with gadoterate exposure, and 0.141 μg/g (IQR, 0.079-0.374 μg/g) with gadobenate exposure. GBCA exposure was associated with gadolinium concentration (adjusted R 2 = 0.77; P P P P Supplemental material is available for this article.

title: Functional Outcomes After Bipolar Hip Hemiarthroplasty by Using the Direct Anterior Approach Versus Posterior and Direct Lateral Approaches: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Tham SYY, Ng JPH, Zhang X, Tan TL.
abstract: Objectives To compare functional recovery and length of hospital stay in patients undergoing bipolar hip hemiarthroplasty (BHH) for displaced femoral neck fractures using the direct anterior approach (DAA) versus the posterior approach (PA) and direct lateral approach (DLA). Methods Design Retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained hip fracture registry. Setting Single tertiary care institution in Singapore. Patient selection criteria Patients aged 60 years and older who underwent BHH for displaced femoral neck fractures (OTA/AO 31-B) between 2020 and 2023 were identified from the institutional hip fracture registry. Outcome measures and comparisons Functional outcomes were assessed using the Modified Barthel Index (MBI; higher scores indicate better independence) and Parker Mobility Score (higher scores indicate better mobility) at discharge, 6 and 12 months. Mobility status, length of stay, postoperative complications, reoperation, and 1-year mortality were evaluated. Outcomes were compared between DAA and PA after propensity score matching, with an exploratory comparison with the DLA. Results A total of 504 patients were identified; 400 PA, 79 DAA, and 25 DLA. After matching, 67 DAA cases and 134 PA cases were analyzed. Age and sex distribution were similar between DAA and PA groups (80.7 ± 6.3 vs. 81.1 ± 6.5 years, P = 0.655; female: 79.1% vs. 75.4%, P = 0.556). The DAA group demonstrated a smaller decline in MBI from premorbid baseline to discharge as compared with the PA group [DAA: -49.85 ± 17.88 vs. PA: -55.47 ± 18.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.11-11.13, P = 0.045]. No significant differences were observed between the DAA and PA groups in changes from premorbid to 12-month MBI (DAA: -23.97 ± 27.46 vs. PA: -18.52 ± 26.38, 95% CI: -13.67 to 2.78, P = 0.193) or from premorbid to 12-month Parker Mobility Score (DAA: -2.72 ± 2.90 vs. PA: -2.18 ± 2.46, 95% CI: -1.37 to 0.29, P = 0.198). Length of stay (DAA: 9.88 ± 5.08 vs. PA: 10.20 ± 5.20 days; P = 0.684) and 1-year mortality (DAA: 3.0% vs. PA: 8.2%; P = 0.156) were comparable between DAA and PA groups. Conclusions DAA for BHH was associated with better early functional recovery at hospital discharge than PA. However, this advantage did not persist at 12 months, with no significant differences in functional outcomes, length of hospital stay, or 1-year mortality between DAA and PA groups. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Dissecting the Metabolic Costs of Uphill and Downhill Walking.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Jessup LN, Kelly LA, Cresswell AG, Lichtwark GA.
abstract: Work- and collision-based models of locomotion relate the body's mechanical work requirements to metabolic energy expenditure at a system level, but do not capture the underlying force and work demands of muscle that drive energy use. Energy is liberated as heat to activate muscle and maintain force production ("force-related costs") and as heat and work to shorten or lengthen active muscle ("work-related costs"). We collected experimental inverse dynamics, electromyography, and ultrasound data from the main power-producing lower-limb muscles during walking at slopes spanning ±15%. These data were used to evaluate a musculoskeletal modeling approach that simulates muscle states, inputs them to a phenomenological energy cost model to estimate metabolic power, and partitions force- and work-related costs. Simulated metabolic power was compared with indirect calorimetry. Summing simulated metabolic power across only the eight muscles evaluated experimentally correlated more strongly with experimental metabolic power than summing across all modeled muscles (adjusted R 2 = 0.95 vs. 0.86), so analyses focused on this subset. Both approaches differed from experimental metabolic power in absolute terms, so results are interpreted as relative changes across slopes. Simulated force-related costs increased at steeper inclines and declines and were moderately correlated with mean joint moments (adjusted R 2 = 0.67), with unexplained variance likely reflecting muscle operating lengths. Simulated work-related costs increased as slope became more positive and were strongly correlated with net joint work (adjusted R 2 = 0.95). Knee joint mechanics seem particularly indicative of these costs. Incorporating a force-related cost term may offer a more explanatory link to muscle mechanical demands than work- and collision-based models alone.

title: Consensus guidelines in the management of paediatric flexible flatfoot : a Delphi study of the British Society of Children's Orthopaedic Surgery.
authors: Morrow EM, Bennet S, Morrison SC, Bridgens A, Mavrotas J, Brousil J, Knight D, Kokkinakis M, BSCOS Flatfoot Consensus Group, Barry M, Bartley H, Carlile G, Chomicki M, Dwyer J, Easton V, Gibbons P, Giles S, Peek A, Phillips K, Robinson E.
abstract: Aims The assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children is inconsistent, reflecting a limited and heterogeneous evidence base. This study aimed to develop a British Society for Children's Orthopaedic Surgery (BSCOS)-led consensus guideline for the multidisciplinary assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children. Methods A modified Delphi consensus opinion study was conducted among the membership of the BSCOS. A multidisciplinary steering committee developed an initial set of statements based on clinical expertise, current evidence, and recognized variation in practice. A total of 33 statements addressing assessment, conservative, and surgical management were scored over two Delphi rounds using a nine-point Likert scale. Participant responses were anonymized. Consensus was defined prospectively as ≥ 75%. Statements that did not meet the consensus threshold were revised and rescored, or discussed and voted on by the steering committee. Results A total of 169 clinicians participated in Round One and 167 in Round Two. Most respondents were consultant orthopaedic surgeons (80%; n = 136), with further representation from registrars/fellows (5%; n = 9), and allied health professionals (AHPs) and advanced nurse practitioners (14%; n = 24). Overall, 24 of 33 statements met the consensus threshold. A further two statements were included following steering committee voting, resulting in 26 final statements. Areas of uncertainty were highlighted in the statements that did not reach consensus, particularly regarding the selection of specific surgical procedures. Conclusion This national consensus guideline provides a framework for clinicians managing children's flexible flatfoot, establishing a benchmark for future evaluation.

title: Computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation of tibial fractures.
authors: Zhao Z, Cai C, Ji G, Xu W.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame (TSF) for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation (UEF) of tibial fractures. This retrospective cohort study included 18 patients with tibial misalignment after UEF between February 2019 and February 2024. Using the TSF technique, X-ray parameters (deformity, frame, and mounting) were entered into software to generate a six-axis correction prescription. Reduction time, number of X-ray exposures, total external fixation duration, clinical fracture healing time, complications, and functional recovery were recorded. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare preoperative and final visual analogue scale (VAS) scores because the paired differences were not normally distributed; data are presented as mean (range) or median (interquartile range [IQR]). All 18 patients were followed up for a mean of 14.9 months (range: 12-18 months). Satisfactory reduction was achieved in all cases after TSF adjustment. Mean reduction time was 19.0 minutes (range, 15-24 minutes), and patients received a mean of 1.4 X-ray exposures (range, 1-3). Clinical fracture healing occurred after a mean of 24.0 weeks (range, 21-29 weeks), and total external fixation lasted a mean of 25.2 weeks (range, 22-30 weeks). Johner-Wruhs ratings at final follow-up were excellent in 15 patients and good in 3 (100% excellent/good). Median VAS scores improved from 7 (IQR, 6-8) before surgery to 1 (IQR, 0-2) at final follow-up (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Z = -3.77, P < .001). Superficial pin tract infections developed in 3 patients (16.7%; 3/18) and were controlled with oral antibiotics and dressing changes. No patient had deep infection, pin loosening, nonunion, or bone exposure. In this small, single-arm retrospective cohort, all 18 patients achieved satisfactory reduction with computer-assisted TSF, and adjustment times were short. No patient underwent secondary open reduction or fixation. These preliminary findings suggest that TSF may serve as a feasible minimally invasive option for correcting early malalignment following UEF of tibial fractures; however, multicenter controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these results.

title: Comparative Analysis of Nail Plate Combination Over Alternative Fixation Constructs in Low-Energy Distal Femur Fractures: Recovery of Ambulatory Status and Outcomes.
authors: Pereira DE, Rust B, Barton D, Eggebrecht Z, Wilson JL, Obey MR, McAndrew CM, Berkes MB.
abstract: Objectives To compare ambulatory status, union, mortality, and operative complications in patients with distal femur fracture treated with the nail plate combination (NPC) and alternative fixation constructs. Methods . Design Retrospective Cohort Study. Setting Single Level 1, tertiary referral Academic center. Patient selection criteria This study included adults with a low-energy distal femur fracture (OTA/AO33A/C and Su 1-3) that received ORIF within 2018-2024. Exclusions were pathologic fractures, antegrade intramedullary devices, and baseline nonambulators (from ambulatory status evaluation only). Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome was ambulatory status at postoperative intervals using Koval-Walking-Score. Secondary outcomes included radiographic union, mortality, and reoperation. Results A total of 404 patients with a low-energy distal femur fracture were included, with 342 included for mobility analysis. Fixation constructs included 189 NPC (mean age 75.0 ± 10.2, 83.1% female), 118 lateral locking plate (LLP) (mean age 73.4 ± 10.2; 76.3% female), 79 retrograde intramedullary nail (rIMN) (mean age 73.7 ± 11.1, 74.7% female), and 18 dual plate combination (mean age 74.6 ± 10.9, 83.3% female) (age P = 0.567, sex P = 0.701). NPC was more frequently selected for Su 2 (56.2%) and Su 3 (65.9%) ( P = 0.001). NPC demonstrated lower average ambulatory impairment score over LLP: 3 weeks (-0.8; P = 0.002), 6 weeks (-1.1; P Conclusions In this study, NPC was associated with superior ambulatory recovery rates to preinjury status over single-implant constructs and improved mortality rates over rIMN. Thus, NPC represented a reliable construct for early ambulation and recovery in these injuries. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Clinical outcomes of transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum in patients aged 50 years or older with hip dysplasia : a propensity score-matched comparative study.
authors: Fujii M, Mochizuki H, Tanaka S, Kawano S, Ueno M, Oba Y, Morimoto T.
abstract: Aims To clarify whether transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum (TOA) in patients aged ≥ 50 years with hip dysplasia provides clinical, radiological, and patient-reported outcomes comparable with those in younger patients. Methods Among 615 patients undergoing TOA between November 1998 and July 2019, 131 patients aged ≥ 50 years were propensity score-matched 1:1 to 131 patients aged Results In patients aged ≥ 50 years, the median mHHS improved from 62 (IQR 54 to 75) to 92 (IQR 84 to 96) (p Conclusion TOA achieved long-term joint survival comparable with that in younger patients, supporting TOA as a joint-preserving option in this age group. However, the sport/recreation score was lower and complications more frequent than in patients aged < 45 years. Preoperative Tönnis grade 2 predicted failure, indicating that joint degeneration, rather than age alone, should guide patient selection.

title: Clinical characteristics and prognostic implications of high-burden osteoarthritis in US adults: Evidence from NHANES 2011-2018.
authors: Wu Z, Du Z, Liu D, Li H, Pan R.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is clinically heterogeneous. Most epidemiologic studies classify OA as present or absent based solely on self-report or radiographic criteria (binary diagnosis), which overlooks the wide variation in symptom burden and functional impact among individuals with OA. We aimed to define a high-burden OA phenotype in a nationally representative sample of US adults and to evaluate its clinical correlates and prognostic significance. This cross-sectional and longitudinal study used nationally representative National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011-2018 data from adults aged ≥20 years, with mortality follow-up through the 2019 public-use Linked Mortality File. OA was defined by self-reported physician-diagnosed arthritis with self-classification as osteoarthritis/degenerative arthritis. High-burden OA was identified using work limitation, activity limitation, walking difficulty, need for special equipment, and difficulty with routine physical tasks. Conventional regression and survival analyses incorporated National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey sampling weights, strata, and primary sampling units. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), random forest, and extreme gradient boosting models were trained with sampling weights; held-out performance was additionally evaluated using survey-weighted metrics. Among 22,436 eligible adults, 14,772 were included in the complete-case analysis: 12,918 without OA, 662 with low-burden OA, and 1192 with high-burden OA. Most weighted baseline characteristics differed across the 3 groups (all P ≤ .005), whereas lifetime alcohol use did not (P = .568). Age- and sex-specific prevalence differed by age-group and sex (both P < .001), without evidence of an age-by-sex interaction (P = .395), and prevalence increased across body mass index categories (P for trend < 0.001). In weighted held-out evaluation, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator had the highest area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (0.848), followed by random forest and XGBoost (both 0.839). Among 1853 participants in the OA survival cohort, 177 deaths occurred during a median observed follow-up of 4.58 years. High-burden OA was associated with all-cause mortality in the fully adjusted survey-weighted Cox model (hazard ratio 1.70, 95% confidence interval 1.08-2.68; P = .022). High-burden OA identifies a clinically vulnerable subgroup with greater functional limitation, worse metabolic and psychological health, and poorer survival. Burden-based stratification may better capture clinically meaningful heterogeneity than OA diagnosis alone.

title: Clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of denosumab-related osteonecrosis of the jaw: An aggregated analysis of published case reports and case series.
authors: Zhang H, Chen C, Zhu Z, Meng W, Fu X, Jiang J, Chen W.
abstract: Background To explore the clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of denosumab-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (DRONJ). Methods Published case studies about DRONJ were retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, and WANFANG, and relevant information was extracted for analysis. The search covered the period from the inception of each database to November 1, 2024. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to identify prognostic factors for DRONJ. Results A total of 31 articles were included in this study. Of the 110 patients with DRONJ, 57 (51.8%) healed completely. Logistic regression analysis showed that diabetes (odds ratio [OR] 4.29, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.18-15.63, P = .027) and corticosteroid use (OR 3.44, 95%CI 1.03-11.50, P = .045) were significantly associated with a poor treatment outcome, while surgical treatment (OR 0.19, 95%CI 0.07-0.54, P = .002) was significantly associated with a lower risk of poor prognosis. Conclusion Diabetes, corticosteroid use, and surgical intervention might be associated with the prognosis of DRONJ. Given that the study was based on published case studies, the generalizability of the results should be interpreted with caution due to a high risk of publication and selection bias.

title: Causal relationships of physical activity and leisure sedentary behaviors with scoliosis: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Yang F, Qiu X, Liu H, Wen J.
abstract: Scoliosis is the most common spinal deformity in children and adolescents, and modifiable lifestyle factors such as sedentary behavior and physical activity (PA) have been suggested to influence its risk, although evidence remains conflicting. This study aimed to investigate the relationships between leisure sedentary behaviors, PA, and the risk of scoliosis by using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Genetic variation in television watching time, mobile phone use time, moderate-to-high intensity physical activity (MVPA), and vigorous physical activity (VPA) were used as IVs. The outcome data were derived from the Finn-Gen Scoliosis dataset. The causal relationships were estimated with inverse variance weighted (IVW), MR-Egger, and weighted median methods. Sensitivity analysis was conducted using Cochran Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy Residual Sum and Outlier (MR-PRESSO), leave-one-out analysis, and funnel plot to estimate the robustness of our findings. The IVW results indicated the following: watching TV time (odds ration [OR] = 0.623, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.21-1.78, P = .38); time spent on mobile phones (OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.16-1.96, P = .37); MVPA (OR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.09-3.15, P = .49); VPA (OR = 0.62, 95% CI: 0.21-1.78, P = .61). The primary IVW MR analysis results were consistent with those of the multiple sensitivity MR Analysis. Genetic susceptibility to leisure sedentary behavior and PA are not associated with the risk of scoliosis. The observed associations may be the result of shared genetic effects or environmental confounding factors.

title: Causal associations between immune cell traits and hip osteoarthritis: A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Huang X, Jiang G, Xu J.
abstract: Observational studies have reported associations between immune cell phenotypes and hip osteoarthritis (HOA), but whether these associations are causal is unknown. We, therefore, used bidirectional 2-sample mendelian randomization (MR) to examine potential causal associations between 731 immune cell traits and HOA risk. Genome-Wide Association Study summary data for 731 immune cell traits were obtained from the genome-wide association study catalog, and HOA summary data were derived from the FinnGen Consortium. Instrumental variables were selected using significance thresholds of P .05; all Cochran's Q P > .05). Weighted median estimates were directionally concordant with IVW for all 17 traits, and every association met the prespecified cross-method consistency criterion (at least three of 5 methods directionally concordant). In the reverse MR analysis, 19 immune traits showed nominal associations (P 0.05), providing no robust evidence for causal effects of HOA on immune cell composition. This MR study provides genetic evidence linking CD33-related myeloid traits and multiple lymphoid and monocyte phenotypes to HOA risk. These associations are statistical and do not establish biological mechanisms. Future experimental and clinical studies are needed to determine whether these immune phenotypes contribute to HOA pathophysiology.

title: Bioimpedance-derived body composition and areal bone mineral density in chronic kidney disease: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Cai Y, Liu F, Da D, Li H, Liu M, Cai C, Wang X, Cao X.
abstract: Bone loss, reduced muscle mass, and impaired nutritional status often coexist in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Whether routinely available bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) measures are associated with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-measured areal bone mineral density (aBMD) independently of body size remains uncertain. We examined these relationships at the lumbar spine and femoral neck. This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 192 adults with CKD who had linked InBody 770 and DXA examinations. Spearman correlations were corrected within each skeletal-site family using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate. Separate multivariable linear regression models estimated the difference in aBMD per 1-standard-deviation increase in each body-composition measure after adjustment for age, sex, height, and dialysis status. Sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for body mass index (BMI) or replaced dialysis status with CKD stage. The cohort included 102 nondialysis and 90 dialysis patients. Skeletal muscle mass was positively associated with lumbar spine aBMD (β = 0.085 g/cm2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.044-0.125) and femoral neck aBMD (β = 0.066 g/cm2; 95% CI, 0.036-0.097). Skeletal muscle index, fat-free mass index, intracellular water, and body cell mass showed similar associations. After BMI adjustment, all estimates were attenuated and their 95% CIs included zero. BIA-derived muscle and cellular-mass measures were associated with aBMD at both skeletal sites, but attenuation after BMI adjustment indicates substantial shared information with overall body size and nutritional reserve. BIA may help identify patients who warrant broader musculoskeletal and nutritional assessment, but it is not a surrogate for DXA or standard CKD-mineral and bone disorder evaluation.

title: Barriers to recruitment in paediatric orthopaedic surgical trials : a qualitative study embedded in the Big BOSS trial.
authors: Kirton JA, Achten J, Young B, Perry DC, Cherry MG.
abstract: Aims Recruitment to randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remains a widely recognized challenge, particularly in surgical and paediatric contexts. The British Orthopaedic Surgery Surveillance (Big BOSS) trial aimed to compare surgical approaches for treating severe stable slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE), a relatively rare but serious adolescent hip condition. Despite national estimates suggesting feasibility, recruitment fell significantly short of targets, and Big BOSS was discontinued. This embedded qualitative study explored the perspectives of consultant surgeons to understand the barriers that contributed to the low recruitment for the trial. Methods Semistructured interviews were carried out with 24 consultant surgeons from 21 NHS sites, including recruiting, non-recruiting, and setup sites. Participants were purposely sampled to ensure variation in experience and involvement in trials. Data were analyzed inductively and thematically, guided by constant comparative methods. Results Five overarching themes were identified: 1) limited availability of eligible patients, with many cases of SCFE either unstable, too mild or managed outside trial centres; 2) challenges in interpreting and standardizing the eligibility criteria; 3) difficulty maintaining clinical equipoise, as surgeons often relied on personal experience and preferred treatment pathways; 4) systemic and logistical barriers, including limited research infrastructure, scheduling complexity, and demands on the resources for trials; and 5) patient-level factors, such as aversion to invasive procedures, logistical constraints, and predetermined expectations of treatment. Together, these themes revealed how clinical, practical, and ethical tensions limited participation in the trial. Conclusion This nested qualitative study highlighted the multifaceted barriers to recruitment in complex surgical RCTs, and showed how embedded qualitative research can help to uncover these challenges and guide the management decisions for trials. The findings emphasize the value of a qualitative investigation to understand the underlying processes and challenges within a trial. This approach facilitates the development of adaptive recruitment strategies, and supports more realistic planning when designing RCTs involving rare conditions or preference-sensitive treatments.

title: Ballistic Forearm Fractures are Associated with Higher Neurovascular Injury, Nonunion, and Complications Compared With Blunt Forearm Injuries.
authors: Barber HF, Pereira DE, Rust BD, Perugini JM, Reaver CN, Guissé NF, Wilson JL, Obey MR, McAndrew CM, Berkes MB.
abstract: Objectives To characterize injury patterns, treatment differences, and clinical outcomes associated with ballistic and blunt forearm fractures. Methods Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single Level 1 tertiary trauma center, 2018-2023. Patient selection criteria The study included adults (≥18) who underwent operative fixation of diaphyseal radius and/or ulna fractures. Exclusion criteria were ipsilateral intraarticular or unstable elbow injuries, pathologic fractures, or fractures involving preexisting implants. Patients were stratified into 2 groups: ballistic and blunt injuries, which were further subclassified as blunt-closed or blunt-open. Outcome measures and comparisons Primary outcomes included nerve deficit, complication rate, unplanned reoperation, nonunion, and postoperative infection. Results The study included 395 patients with 398 forearm fractures: 81 ballistic fractures in 78 patients [32 years (18-69), 88.9% male], 213 blunt-closed fractures [41 years (18-82), 59.2% male], and 104 blunt-open fractures [46 years (19-92), 71.2% male]. Ballistic fractures had significantly higher rates of nerve deficits (48.2% vs. 6.3%, P Conclusions Ballistic forearm fractures posed unique challenges compared with blunt injuries. They were associated with significantly higher rates of nerve deficit, unplanned reoperations, and overall complications, with higher nonunion observed when compared with blunt-closed injuries. These injuries warrant a high index of suspicion for nerve injury and close long-term follow-up to optimize patient outcomes and address the needs of a disproportionately affected, high-risk population. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Associations of Quadriceps and Prefemoral Fat Pad MRI Parameters With Postoperative Pain and Functional Outcomes After Total Knee Arthroplasty in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis.
authors: Dong Y, Zhang X, Yan L, Li B, Zeng L, Zhao F, Tao J.
abstract: Aim To investigate the relationship between quantitative magnetic resonance imaging parameters of the quadriceps fat pad (QFP) and prefemoral fat pad (PFP) and pain and functional outcomes at 1 month after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in patients with knee osteoarthritis. Methods We retrospectively collected the clinical and imaging data of patients with knee osteoarthritis who underwent primary unilateral TKA at Shihezi People's Hospital between October 2025 and April 2026 and had completed knee magnetic resonance imaging before surgery. The following imaging parameters were extracted: (1) QFP: the craniocaudal diameter, anteroposterior diameter, oblique diameter, T1 value, T2 value, proton density (PD) value, high signal intensity, and mass effect; and (2) PFP: maximum thickness and high signal intensity. Postoperative pain and physical function scores at 1 month after surgery were obtained from the medical record system. Spearman correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis were performed to identify imaging markers associated with postoperative clinical outcomes. Results Spearman correlation analysis showed that the T2 value, hyperintensity, and mass effect of the QFP, as well as the hyperintensity and maximum thickness of the PFP, were positively correlated with postoperative pain and physical function scores. Multiple linear regression analysis showed that the T2 value of QFP, mass effect, QFP hyperintensity, and PFP hyperintensity were significantly associated with postoperative pain. The T2 value of QFP, mass effect, and PFP hyperintensity and maximum thickness were significantly associated with postoperative physical function scores. Conclusions This retrospective study showed that quantitative and morphological parameters of the QFP and PFP extracted from preoperative routine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were significantly associated with postoperative pain and functional outcomes in patients with knee osteoarthritis undergoing TKA. These findings suggest that specific imaging features may be associated with poorer outcomes and provide preliminary evidence for clinical consideration. However, prospective studies with larger sample sizes are warranted to validate these exploratory findings.

title: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: He M, Chen Y, Zou X, Zou Y, Ding H.
abstract: Aim To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated. Results No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p Conclusions In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.

title: Articular compliance and tolerance to residual incongruity after intra-articular fracture: A hypothesis-driven narrative review.
authors: Dhar SA, Dar TA, Dar RA, Farooq S, Maajid A, Zargar S, Mughal I.
abstract: Background Residual articular incongruity after intra-articular fracture is widely held to cause post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), yet tolerance of a given step-off differs between joints and between regions of the same joint. Reduction targets are nonetheless expressed as uniform millimetre thresholds, and no tissue-level mechanism has been offered for the variation. Hypothesis The compliance of the osteochondral unit - cartilage thickness, cartilage material properties and subchondral bone stiffness together - modulates tolerance of residual incongruity, and incongruity is more informatively expressed relative to local cartilage thickness than in absolute millimetres. Methods Narrative review with a documented search of PubMed/MEDLINE (inception to 14 October 2026) covering cartilage and subchondral properties of opposing surfaces, experimental and computational studies of articular incongruity, and clinical studies relating residual displacement to outcome. Four searches returned 3928 records, 3579 after deduplication; 54 sources informed the synthesis. This is not a systematic review; reporting follows SANRA. Findings Small, localised contact-stress elevations appear tolerable; step-offs remodel less completely as their height increases; and cumulative contact-stress exposure above a threshold predicts PTOA after tibial plafond fracture. Opposing surfaces differ measurably in cartilage thickness, modulus and subchondral bone thickness, but the direction of the difference reverses between joints and between regions of one joint, so curvature is not a usable proxy for compliance. Clinically, the acetabulum and tibial plafond appear least tolerant, the meniscus-covered tibial plateau more tolerant, and distal radius incongruity predicts radiographic arthrosis more strongly than functional loss. Conclusions The evidence is consistent with, but does not establish, a contribution of osteochondral compliance; joint-level factors confound the clinical data. We set out a Compliance Framework defining measurable determinants, propose relative incongruity as a testable metric, and state four falsifiable predictions with the designs that would test them. Current joint-specific reduction standards should guide practice until those predictions are tested.

title: Application of a Risk Assessment-Based Stratified Early Warning Nursing Model to Prevent Postoperative Delirium in Geriatric Patients Undergoing Orthopedic Surgery.
authors: Liu W, Li D.
abstract: Aim To investigate the effectiveness of a risk assessment-based stratified early warning nursing model in preventing postoperative delirium (POD) in geriatric orthopedic patients. Methods A retrospective study was conducted. Elderly patients who underwent elective orthopedic surgery at The First Hospital of Jilin University between January 2024 and December 2025 were enrolled. Based on the nursing model received, patients were divided into two groups: those receiving routine care were assigned to the control group (98 patients), while those receiving the risk assessment-based stratified early warning nursing model were assigned to the intervention group (113 patients). In the intervention group, a delirium risk assessment tool was used for preoperative risk stratification (low, moderate, and high risk), and graded early warning measures and targeted interventions were implemented according to the risk level. The incidence of postoperative delirium, delirium duration, length of hospital stay, and nursing satisfaction were compared between the two groups. Results The incidence of postoperative delirium was significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (9.73% vs. 19.39%, p = 0.045). The intervention group also had a shorter median delirium duration (3.0 d vs. 5.0 d, p = 0.005), a shorter mean length of hospital stay (12.18 ± 2.60 d vs. 16.48 ± 3.13 d, p p = 0.032).
