Conclusions The risk assessment-based stratified early warning nursing model may reduce the incidence of postoperative delirium in geriatric orthopedic patients, shorten delirium duration and hospital stay, and improve nursing satisfaction, highlighting its potential clinical value.

title: Anterior reconstruction using femoral ring allografts for thoracolumbar infectious spondylitis: Clinical and radiologic outcomes of a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Sung MJ, Park CG, Seo HY.
abstract: Surgical treatment is required in infectious spondylitis when conservative management fails or vertebral destruction causes instability. Autologous bone graft is considered the gold standard but is limited by donor-site morbidity and availability. Femoral ring allografts are widely used in degenerative conditions, but their role in infectious spondylitis is unclear. This study evaluated the clinical, radiologic, and laboratory outcomes of anterior reconstruction using femoral ring allografts. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology statement, we reviewed 25 patients who underwent anterior corpectomy and reconstruction using femoral ring allografts followed by posterior instrumentation between December 2011 and September 2023. Clinical outcomes (VAS, Oswestry Disability Index, Frankel grade), laboratory parameters (erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein), and radiologic outcomes (Cobb angle, fusion) were compared preoperatively and at final follow-up. Paired comparisons used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with Hodges-Lehmann estimates, distribution-free 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and effect sizes (r). Infection control and complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 29.2 ± 23.9 months (range, 12.0-87.2 months). VAS improved from 7.3 ± 1.1 to 1.9 ± 1.0 (Hodges-Lehmann estimate -5.50; 95% CI, -6.00 to -5.00; r = 0.87) and Oswestry Disability Index from 37.7 ± 5.9 to 10.7 ± 3.5 (-26.50; 95% CI, -29.50 to -23.50; r = 0.87; both P < .001). Neurological function improved significantly (r = 0.76, P < .001). Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein decreased significantly (both P < .001). Sagittal alignment was corrected with partial loss over time but remained improved at final follow-up (5.55°; 95% CI, 3.40°-8.95°; r = 0.69; P < .001). Fusion was achieved in 92% and infection control in 96%. Complications occurred in 16%. In patients with large anterior column defects not amenable to tricortical iliac autograft, femoral ring allograft reconstruction achieved reliable infection control, a high fusion rate, and satisfactory clinical and radiologic outcomes over a mean follow-up of 29.2 months. Within this period, it appears a reasonable alternative to structural autograft when donor-site morbidity or graft availability is a concern. Longer-term comparative studies are needed to confirm the durability of graft incorporation and to define its role relative to contemporary titanium-based reconstruction.

title: Analysis of Video Footage and Running Metrics Around Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries in Men's Elite Football. A Retrospective Observational Study of 43 Cases.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Manchón-Davó M, Miralles-Iborra A, Del Coso J, Vera-Garcia FJ, Urban T, Campo RL, Resta R, Moreno-Pérez V.
abstract: This study aimed to describe the situational, biomechanical, and neurocognitive context of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) ruptures in elite men's football across six seasons, with a novel focus on objectively quantifying running speed and acceleration in the moments preceding injury. This retrospective video-based observational study included 43 complete primary ACL ruptures in male professional football players (mean age, 26.9 ± 4.6 years) confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging during official matches of the Spanish first division between 2019/2020 and 2024/2025. Cases were identified through injury surveillance and official reports, and footage was obtained from LaLiga's official digital platform. Two independent observers analyzed and classified each injury event using a predefined protocol to ensure consistency in the results. External running metrics, defined as running speed and acceleration, were extracted at initial contact (i.e., the first ground contact of the injured leg) and the estimated injury frame (i.e., the frame showing visual signs consistent with ACL rupture) using Mediacoach, LaLiga's validated optical tracking system. Non-contact ACL injuries were further analyzed for kinematic patterns and neurocognitive error indicators, defined as observable attentional or motor response inhibitory errors preceding the injury event. Categorical variables were analyzed using chi-square tests, and running metrics were compared across mechanisms using one-way ANOVAs. Defenders accounted for the largest proportion of ACL rupture cases (51.2%), and non-contact injuries were the most frequent mechanism (60.5%). The most frequent action was pressing/tackling (39.5%). Running metrics did not differ significantly across mechanisms (p > 0.05, η p 2 = 0.02-0.06). Among 26 non-contact injuries, 80.8% displayed neurocognitive error indicators. In the overall non-contact injury group, the estimated injury frame was characterized by knee flexion (60° ± 35°), knee valgus (72.0%), rapid deceleration (acceleration, -2.63 ± 2.03 m·s -2 ), and a running speed of 20.96 ± 5.06 km·h -1 (64.8% ± 15.2% of seasonal maximal speed). In conclusion, most ACL ruptures in elite men's football occurred through non-contact mechanisms. In these events, players were running at a mean speed of 20.96 ± 5.06 km·h -1 at the estimated injury frame and showed marked deceleration, knee flexion-valgus alignment, and observable neurocognitive error indicators under unanticipated match conditions.

title: ASO Video Abstract: How to Deal with Median Arcuate Ligament during Pancreaticoduodenectomy? Management Strategies and Impact on Perioperative Outcomes.
authors: Fernandez-de-Sevillaa E, Collard MK, de Rosa RV, Laroche S, Scoleri I, Boubaddi M, de Ponthaud C, Perinel J, Leclerc J, Bustamante R, Addeo P, Cherif R, Ayav A, Adham M, Gaujoux S, Laurent C, Truant S, Cunha AS, Sulpice L, Gelli M.

title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Mohammad HR, Rahman A, Muhammad IM, Gill SS, Selim A, Thomas G, Murray DW, Griffin XL.
abstract: Aims To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. Results A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. Conclusion DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

title: A Primer on Statistical Certainty and Its Distinction From Clinical Importance.
authors: Ebramzadeh E, Slobogean GP, Ricci WM, McKellop H.

title: Title: Impact of Coexisting Gout on Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Data from the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative (OBRI).
authors: Kwok TS, Movahedi M, Cesta A, Akhavan P, Carter Thorne J, Pope J, Lau A, Mirza R, Hepworth E, Chow A, Aydin SZ, Kuriya B, OBRI Investigators.
abstract: Objective To determine the prevalence and factors associated with coexisting gout in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and evaluate whether concomitant gout is associated with worse RA disease activity. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of RA patients enrolled in the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative, a multicentre real-world cohort across Ontario, Canada. Coexisting gout was defined by patient- or physician-reported diagnosis or xanthine oxidase inhibitor use. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with coexisting gout and the impact of gout on oral glucocorticoid (GC) use. The association between baseline gout and longitudinal RA disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index, CDAI ≤10) was examined using mixed-effects logistic regression at 24-months, adjusting for prespecified confounders. Results Among 3,703 RA patients, 113 (3.1%) had coexisting gout with mean (SD) age of 66.1 (8.7) years and 52.2% were female. Coexisting gout was associated with older age (OR 1.05 per year), obesity (OR 1.67), cardiovascular disease or hypertension (OR 1.95) and diuretic use (OR 1.68), while female sex was inversely associated (OR 0.31). CDAI scores were similar between patients with and without gout at baseline (18.3±12.5 vs 20.2±13.5) and at 12-months (10.9±9.8 vs 11.0±10.4). After adjustment, baseline coexisting gout was neither significantly associated with oral GC use at 12-months (OR 1.73, 95% CI: 0.96-3.13) or the attainment of CDAI low disease activity/remission by 24-months (OR 1.19, 95% CI: 0.72-1.97). Conclusion In this large real-world RA cohort, coexisting gout was uncommon and associated with traditional gout risk factors but did not statistically influence oral GC use or RA treatment target attainment.

title: Three working windows posterior midline approach for posterior column tibial plateau fractures.
authors: Wang X, Zhang S, Yan J, Jiang D, Shi C, Yin Z, Liang B.
abstract: Background Isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression are challenging because conventional posterior approaches limit instrument trajectories and reduction vectors for distinct posterior fragments. Methods Ten patients with isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures accompanied by combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression were treated using a posterior midline skin incision organized into three working windows. The central window served as the foundational posterior corridor, with medial and lateral windows developed as functional extensions to facilitate region-specific reduction and fixation. Relevant clinical data and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed. Results Postoperative radiographs of all 10 patients showed satisfactory joint reduction and alignment. Radiographic fracture union was achieved in all cases at a mean of 13.9 weeks, with a mean follow up of 11.8 months. At final follow up, mean knee flexion was 124.0°, and mean knee extension was -2.1°, and the mean Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee score was 90.8 points. One patient developed a superficial wound infection that resolved with antibiotic treatment, and one patient experienced deep vein thrombosis that was successfully treated with anticoagulation therapy. No neurovascular injuries, deep infections, or fixation failures were observed during follow up. Conclusion A posterior midline approach organized into three working windows may provide a feasible option for selected isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression, allowing region-specific posterior fixation through a single posterior skin incision.

title: The osteoporosis-fracture paradox in older Taiwanese men: lower osteoporosis prevalence but comparable fragility fracture burden.
authors: Lee YY, Huang YC, Kao SW, Chen YC, Cheng MT.
abstract: Despite a substantially lower prevalence of osteoporosis than age-matched women, older men experienced a relatively comparable burden of fragility fractures, demonstrating a marked dissociation between osteoporosis prevalence and fracture burden. Purpose Although osteoporosis is less common in men than in women, male fragility fractures carry substantial morbidity and post-fracture mortality. Whether the lower prevalence of osteoporosis translates into a proportionally lower fracture burden remains unclear. We compared the prevalence of osteoporosis and fragility fractures between age-matched Taiwanese men and women. Methods This retrospective cohort study evaluated 2093 men undergoing clinical dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) between 2021 and 2023, of whom 2031 met eligibility criteria and were compared with 2031 age-matched women selected via 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching. Osteoporosis was defined as a T-score ≤-2.5 at the lumbar spine, femoral neck and/or total hip. Vertebral and hip fractures were identified from radiographs and electronic medical records. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of fracture. Results The prevalence of osteoporosis in men was approximately half that in women (32.4% vs. 51.4%; P Conclusions Older Taiwanese men exhibited a substantially lower prevalence of osteoporosis than age-matched women but experienced a relatively comparable burden of fragility fractures. These findings demonstrate a marked dissociation between osteoporosis prevalence and fragility fracture burden in older men and reinforce the importance of comprehensive fracture risk assessment integrating BMD with clinical risk factors.

title: The osteoporosis diagnosis and treatment gaps in Iranian older adults: Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) Program.
authors: Hesari E, Fahimfar N, Khalagi K, Yarmohammadi H, Shahrousvand S, Zarepour P, Gharibzadeh S, Mansourzadeh MJ, Sahafiee G, Farhadi A, Larijani B, Ostovar A, Sanjari M.
abstract: This study examined why many older adults in Iran with osteoporosis are not diagnosed or treated. It found very high rates of missed diagnosis and lack of treatment, especially influenced by age, gender, and education. Addressing these gaps is essential to improve awareness, care access, and prevent serious bone-related health problems. Background Despite the availability of diagnostic and therapeutic facilities for osteoporosis, a significant proportion of older adults remain undiagnosed and untreated. This care gap may stem from various barriers and understanding the underlying reasons for these disparities is crucial for developing targeted interventions. This study aimed to investigate the gaps in osteoporosis diagnosis and treatment among older adults in Iran and to identify the key factors contributing to these gaps. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed data from two phases of the Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) Program. Participants were selected using multistage cluster random sampling. The first phase, conducted between 2015 and 2017, included 2424 residents aged 60 and above. The second phase, from 2018 to 2021, involved 1721 residents aged 50 and above. Bone mineral density (BMD) was measured using the Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry method and T-score ≤ -2.5 in either of the femoral neck, total hip, or spinal sites was defined as osteoporosis. Participants reported whether a doctor had diagnosed them with osteoporosis and if they received treatment. Those diagnosed via bone densitometry but unaware of their condition were considered underdiagnosed. Those diagnosed through BMD tests but not on osteoporosis medication were considered undertreated. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify determinant factors of the underdiagnosis and undertreatment of osteoporosis. Results A total of 4145 elder adults with a mean age of 65.5 (54.40% female) participated in this study. Underdiagnosis and undertreatment in the participants who underwent DXA were estimated at 1050 (73.06% (and 1328 (92.41), respectively. The undertreatment rate was 666 (91.98%), 836(90.96%) and 868 (92.53%) based on the intervention thresholds of FRAX without BMD, MOF-FRAX with BMD and FRAX with TBS for MOF, respectively. A statistically significant association was found between osteoporosis underdiagnosis and variables including male (OR = 0.57, P Conclusion This study highlights significant gaps in the diagnosis and treatment of osteoporosis among participants, with significant disparities linked to demographic and socioeconomic factors. Further research is needed to investigate the causes and extensive interventions at the population level should be taken to fill the gap and raise awareness on osteoporosis as a growing public health concern and provide access to the treatment of the disease.

title: Smaller Ischiofemoral Space Is Associated With Proximal Hamstring Injuries.
authors: Itthipanichpong T, Retzky J, Curran P, Menta SV, Ranawat AS.
abstract: Purpose To develop a reference ischiofemoral space (IFS) value for patients with proximal hamstring injuries (HSI) and to compare it with individuals without proximal hamstring pathology. Methods We retrospectively collected the data from our institution. Patients aged 18 years or older with a proximal HSI were included. Patients with insufficient imaging data, those with prior hip surgery, those with concurrent femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, and those with concurrent ischiofemoral impingement as defined by quadratus femoris edema on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were excluded. A 1:2 matched-cohort analysis was conducted. Two cohorts were (1) patients with proximal HSI and (2) patients with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome as a control cohort (Control). Both pelvic anteroposterior (AP) radiographs and axial MRI were used to assess IFS and were compared between the 2 cohorts. Additionally, the neck-shaft angle was collected and compared. Results There were 60 patients in the HSI cohort and 124 patients in the control cohort. The mean neck-shaft angle, IFS from the AP pelvis, and IFS from the axial MRI for the HSI cohort were 136.35° ± 5.63°, 24.35 ± 8.60 mm, and 26.57 ± 7.96 mm, respectively. For the control cohort, these values were 135.30° ± 4.53°, 29.83 ± 9.84 mm, and 29.28 ± 8.54 mm, respectively. The IFS in the HSI group was significantly lower than that in the control group on both pelvic AP radiograph ( P P = .036). Conclusions Patients with proximal HSI had a smaller IFS compared with those with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Research culture methods detect more anaerobes compared to conventional clinical workflows in periprosthetic joint infection: a pilot study of 14 cases.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Visperas A, Lu Q, Lehman B, Foo SS, Chen W, Vachharajani V, Stappenbeck T, Piuzzi N.
abstract: Introduction Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most challenging complications of total joint arthroplasty, often complicated by limitations in diagnostic sensitivity. Standard clinical culture methods fail to identify pathogens in 20%-50% of cases, leading to potential under- or overtreatment. This pilot study aimed to compare the microbial detection capabilities of standard clinical culture methods with enhanced research laboratory techniques, and to explore whether additional microbial findings might have the potential to influence antibiotic treatment planning. Materials and methods Thirteen patients undergoing surgery for PJI, as defined by the 2018 International Consensus Meeting (ICM) on Infection criteria, were prospectively enrolled at a single academic medical center between August 2023 and September 2024. Intraoperative synovial fluid, periprosthetic tissue, and implant swabs were collected and processed using both standard clinical workflows and optimized research protocols. Culture results and treatment decisions were reviewed in collaboration with Infectious Disease specialists. Results Both methods identified primary organisms. However, research techniques detected additional organisms not captured by clinical cultures (p = 0.013). Despite these differences, overall detection rates were comparable (57.1% vs. 59.5%; p = 0.963), with the research workflow achieving similar yield with fewer samples. The potential impact of additional isolate identification on antibiotic selection, if deemed clinically significant, did not appear to result in meaningful changes to antibiotic regimens, although this may have been influenced by the empiric use broad-spectrum antibiotics. Conclusions Clinical culture methods may not detect all organisms in PJI, highlighting possible limitations in current diagnostic approaches. Although this pilot study did not directly assess the impact of enhanced microbial detection on antibiotic prescribing and treatment decisions were largely unchanged, these findings suggest that a more comprehensive microbial detection could potentially inform antibiotic selection and warrants further investigation.

title: Normal Creatine Kinase in Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies: Disease Characteristics and Outcomes.
authors: Keret S, Chandra T, Kaly L, Silva RL, Gkiaouraki E, Pongtarakulpanit N, Gopalarathinam R, Reddy KS, Moghadam-Kia S, Oddis CV, Aggarwal R.
abstract: Objectives Creatine kinase (CK) is an important biomarker for monitoring idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM). Data regarding normal CK in IIM are limited. We aimed to characterize patients with normal CK levels and investigate the association between CK and disease activity and outcomes. Methods Data were collected from the Rituximab in Myositis (RIM) trial, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of refractory adult IIM. Myositis core set measures (CSMs) were collected every 4 weeks for 44 weeks. Normal/ near-normal was defined as Results Of 143 patients, 53 (37%) had normal CK. These patients were more frequently White (85% vs. 62%, p Conclusion Normal CK levels are common in IIM, especially in DM, and do not exclude active muscle disease. CK functions as a longitudinal biomarker across IIM, with performance varying by disease subset and baseline CK, supporting nuanced clinical interpretation.

title: Lumbopelvic fixation for high-energy sacral fractures and spinopelvic dissociation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of complications, unplanned revision and implant removal.
authors: Patel HA, Patel S, Suresh RI, Yang E, Lindley AK, Kidd G, Schneider MB, Zareef U, Padovano A, Bivona LJ, Cavanaugh DL, Koh EY, Hashmi SZ, France JC, O'Toole RV, Ludwig SC, Jauregui JJ.
abstract: Introduction Secondary procedures after lumbopelvic fixation (LPF) include planned implant removal, removal for symptoms and revision for complications. Their differing indications, together with limited comparative evidence, complicate counselling and surgical planning. Methods PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched to May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420251036375) for comparative and single-arm studies (≥10 LPF patients). High-energy injuries and fragility fractures were considered separately. Random-effects models summarised complications, unplanned revision, implant removal and within-study comparisons of surgical approaches and fixation strategies. Results Twenty-five studies were included (22 high-energy, 3 fragility). Across 19 high-energy LPF cohorts (564 patients), pooled surgical-site infection was 9.3% (95% CI 6.1-14.1), implant loosening or failure was 5.3%, nonunion occurred in 4 of 389 patients (1.0%) and loss of reduction in 2 of 355. Pooled unplanned revision was 11.9% (95% CI 8.7-16.0; prediction interval 5.3-24.3), most often for infection or wound complications. Implant removal was 79.0% in routine-removal series and 17.3% in selective-removal series. Four studies compared minimally invasive and open LPF. Pooling three studies showed less blood loss with minimally invasive LPF (mean difference -271 mL, 95% CI -367 to -175) and shorter operative time (-51 min, -97 to -5); the operative-time association did not persist with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Infection (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.09-1.83) and revision (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.09-1.43) estimates were inconclusive. Four cohorts comparing LPF with posterior pelvic-ring fixation alone reported higher odds of revision after LPF (OR 3.96, 95% CI 1.63-9.60), with substantial potential for confounding by indication. Certainty was very low. Conclusions Nonunion and loss of reduction were infrequent after LPF, while unplanned revision most often involved infection or wound complications. Implant removal varied with institutional policy and warrants separate counselling. Minimally invasive LPF was associated with less blood loss, but comparative evidence remains insufficient to establish lower complication rates, equivalent mechanical outcomes or superiority of either fixation strategy.

title: Inequality in secondary fracture prevention supports prioritisation of fracture liaison services in coastal health plans in England and Wales.
authors: Pugh L, Clemeno F, Ghumman R, Javaid MK.
abstract: The 2021 UK Chief Medical Officers' annual report highlighted poorer health in coastal communities but did not include osteoporosis or secondary fracture prevention. Using Fracture Liaison Services database (FLS-DB) data, FLSs in coastal areas were shown to have poorer performance and lower parenteral osteoporosis medication recommendation rates, supporting inclusion of FLSs in coastal health improvement plans. A number of studies have highlighted socio-economic deprivation as a predictor of fragility fractures and poorer outcomes after fracture. In parallel, coastal areas are recognised to be areas with poorer health outcomes, in part due to socio-economic deprivation. Purpose To describe secondary fracture prevention in terms of FLS provision and quality in coastal vs. non-coastal healthcare settings using routinely collected audit data. Methods A cross-sectional, ecological analysis using the missed opportunity counts from the national Fracture Liaison Service (FLS-DB) and Hip Fracture (NHFD) Databases of England and Wales audit data with Office for National Statistics classification of coastal towns. Results Results Coastal sites were not significantly more likely to be non-FLS vs FLS providers (38% vs 24%, p = 0.18). However, coastal FLSs had higher missed opportunity patient counts than non-coastal FLSs (p = 0.02), with lower vertebral identification rates (14.2% vs 20.9%, p = 0.02). While treatment rates were similar, coastal FLSs had significantly lower rates of parenteral anti-resorptive therapy recommended (p Conclusion We have demonstrated a coastal deleterious effect on the quality of secondary fracture prevention of FLS providers as measured by missed opportunities for treatment, vertebral fracture identification and recommendation of parenteral anti-resorptive therapies. Coastal health priority plans in the NHS should prioritise effective FLS provision.

title: Global research on cricket injuries (1982-2025): A bibliometric analysis.
authors: Vaishya R, Singh A, Gupta BM, Vaish A, Dhillon MS, Parmar Y, Orchard J.
abstract: Background Cricket is one of the most widely played sports worldwide and carries a significant burden of musculoskeletal injuries, particularly among fast bowlers. Over the past four decades, research in cricket injury epidemiology, biomechanics, workload monitoring, and surveillance has expanded substantially. Objective To conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global cricket injury research, identifying growth trends, influential publications, leading contributors, collaboration networks, and major thematic domains. Methods Publications from 1982 to 2025 were systematically analyzed using bibliometric indicators including annual growth, authorship productivity, institutional and country contributions, citation impact, total link strength (TLS), and co-authorship networks. The top 100 cited papers and the top 10 highly cited papers (HCPs) were examined in detail to identify landmark contributions and research priorities. Results A sharp rise in publications occurred after 2003, with nearly 90% of output produced in the last two decades. Australia, the United Kingdom, and South Africa led in productivity, citation impact, and collaborative link strength. The top 10 HCPs accounted for 10% of papers but 37.25% of total citations, underscoring concentrated scholarly influence. Fast bowlers consistently demonstrated the highest injury incidence, particularly lumbar spine and lower limb injuries. Workload spikes were strongly associated with increased injury risk, establishing load monitoring as a central preventive strategy. Biomechanical factors such as mixed bowling action, trunk rotation, and front-knee mechanics were linked to lumbar stress injuries. Standardized injury definitions and international consensus surveillance frameworks significantly improved research quality and comparability. Conclusion Cricket injury research has evolved into a mature, collaborative, and high-impact domain centered on fast bowling biomechanics, workload regulation, and surveillance standardization. Expanded global participation and integration of advanced analytics are essential for future injury prevention strategies.

title: Fracture characteristics in coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus: Clinical significance of medial trochlear involvement.
authors: Ishihara N, Saeki M, Fujihara Y, Saeki S, Tanaka H, Ota H, Kumagai H, Yazaki N, Yamamoto M.
abstract: Background Coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus exhibit diverse fracture-extension patterns that are not fully characterized by conventional classification systems. The clinical significance of fracture extension into the medial or lateral column remains incompletely understood. This study investigated fracture-extension patterns beyond the conventional Dubberley classification and evaluated their associations with clinical outcomes and bone-related complications. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included surgically treated coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus with a minimum follow-up of 12 months at four affiliated institutions between 2012 and 2024. Fractures were classified using the AO/OTA and Dubberley systems. Computed tomography (CT) images were reviewed to assess medial trochlear involvement, lateral column involvement without posterior condylar comminution, and isolated trochlear fractures. Clinical outcomes included elbow range of motion (flexion, extension, and arc of motion) and postoperative complications. Univariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with bone-related complications. Results Among 374 surgically treated distal humeral fractures, 35 coronal shear fractures were included in the final analysis. Medial trochlear involvement was identified in 8 fractures (23%) and was most frequently observed in Dubberley type 3 fractures. Patients with medial trochlear involvement had significantly greater loss of elbow extension at final follow-up than those without medial trochlear involvement (-29° vs. -16°, P = 0.042). Bone-related complications were more frequent in fractures with medial trochlear involvement than in those without (50% vs. 7%, P = 0.016). In univariate logistic regression analysis, medial trochlear involvement was significantly associated with bone-related complications (odds ratio, 12.5; 95% confidence interval, 1.69-92.3; P = 0.013). Neither the AO/OTA nor the Dubberley classification was significantly associated with bone-related complications. Conclusions Medial trochlear involvement was significantly associated with greater loss of elbow extension and bone-related complications at final follow-up in coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus. Preoperative CT assessment of medial trochlear involvement may provide clinically useful information complementary to conventional fracture classification systems and may aid surgical planning.

title: Femoral Stem Design Influences Early Periprosthetic Fracture Risk Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
authors: Krez AN, Toomey SD, Swanson KC, Herndon CL, Danoff JR.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic femur fracture (PFF) is a significant complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Modern collared, triple-taper metaphyseal-filling stems may reduce fracture risk. This study compared a triple-taper metaphyseal stem with other cementless designs to assess early PFF risk, fracture risk by age and bone quality, and the impact of collar position. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 774 primary cementless THAs, including triple-taper metaphyseal (n = 311), single-wedge (n = 294), double-wedge (n = 116), and gradual taper/metadiaphyseal-filling (n = 53) stems. Triple-taper stems were implanted through a prospective multicenter trial, while comparison stems were from a single health system. Patients were stratified by stem design, age, Dorr classification, and collar position. The primary outcome was 90-day PFF. Results PFF occurred in 53 patients (6.8%), including 15 (1.9%) postoperative fractures requiring reoperation. Patients with PFF were older ( P P = .02). Triple-taper stems demonstrated lower PFF risk than other designs (odds ratio 0.20; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.48; P P P = .02). Conclusions Collared, triple-taper metaphyseal stems were associated with lower early PFF risk across patient ages and bone quality profiles. Seating the collar on the calcar further reduced fracture incidence.

title: Diagnostic performance and reproducibility of standardized two-plane ultrasound cine clips for supraspinatus tendon pathology.
authors: Khan S, Lee J, Jibri Z, de Oliveira Cyrineu F, Sampaio ML.
abstract: Objective To determine the diagnostic performance and reader reproducibility of standardized two-plane cine clips for supraspinatus tendon pathology, using the complete radiologist-supervised shoulder ultrasound examination as the clinical reference standard. Materials and methods This prospective single-centre study screened 140 consecutive shoulder ultrasound examinations. Standardized longitudinal and transverse supraspinatus cine clips were independently reviewed by two fellowship-trained musculoskeletal radiologists blinded to the clinical report. Reader 1 read all included examinations (24 twice); Reader 2 read 51. Diagnostic performance (exact 95% confidence intervals) was calculated against the same-day clinical ultrasound report, and reliability with Cohen's κ. Reporting radiologists could access the standardized clips. Results Of 140 examinations, 114 were analyzed (mean age 57 years; 56 women). Reader 1 showed high performance for full-thickness tears (sensitivity 87% [95% confidence interval 69-96%], specificity 98% [92-100%]) and complete tears (sensitivity 73% [39-94%], specificity 97% [92-99%]). Calcific tendinopathy yielded sensitivity/specificity of 79%/85%; partial-thickness tears, 57%/87%; and tendinopathy, 92%/28%. Reader 2 sensitivity was 92% [64-100%] for full-thickness and 18% [2-52%] for partial-thickness tears. Intra-observer κ ranged from 0.17 (tendinopathy) to 0.89 (full-thickness tears). Inter-observer κ was 0.95 for full-thickness, 0.56 for complete and 0.21 for partial-thickness tears. Conclusion Standardized two-plane cine clips demonstrate high diagnostic performance and inter-observer reliability for full-thickness supraspinatus tears. For complete tears, inter-observer agreement was moderate and sensitivity was imprecise. Given limited sensitivity for partial-thickness tears and low specificity for tendinopathy, cine clips alone are insufficient for these pathologies and should complement rather than replace complete real-time shoulder ultrasound examinations.

title: Cost saving strategies for management of postmenopausal women with fragility fractures in Taiwan: a simulation projection model from 2025 to 2045.
authors: Huang ST, Lai HY, Wang CY, Hsiao FY, Yang RS.
abstract: This study used a microsimulation model to assess the impact of improved osteoporosis diagnosis, treatment, and adherence in Taiwan. The combined approach prevented 42,605 fractures and saved NT$4.64 billion by 2045. The results emphasize the importance of comprehensive anti-osteoporosis management in evidence-based healthcare policy. Introduction Taiwan's rapidly aging population presents mounting challenges for osteoporosis management, with healthcare resources increasingly constrained under the National Health Insurance system. This study projected the clinical and economic impact of enhanced osteoporosis diagnosis, treatment, and adherence strategies among postmenopausal women in Taiwan from 2025 to 2045. Methods A cross-sectional microsimulation model projected annual osteoporotic fracture incidence and costs among postmenopausal women aged ≥65 years. Fracture risk was estimated using simplified Fracture Risk Assessment Tool (FRAX), with inputs from published literature and national health insurance data informing demographic distribution, treatment patterns, and healthcare costs. Three scenarios evaluated: (1) improved medication adherence alone, (2) increased case finding through enhanced screening and treatment rates, and (3) combined case finding and adherence improvements. Results In the reference scenario, the annual number of osteoporotic fractures are projected to increase by 99% from 137,557 in 2025 to 273,820 in 2045, with annual costs rising from NT$20.10 billion to NT$39.32 billion. Enhanced case finding prevented 12,061 fractures and saved NT$1.21 billion in 2025, escalating to 23,983 prevented fractures and NT$2.49 billion saved by 2045. Improved adherence alone prevented 14,853 fractures (NT$1.57 billion saved) in 2025, increasing to 22,525 fractures (NT$2.33 billion saved) by 2045. The combined approach demonstrated superior outcomes, preventing 22,045 fractures (NT$2.32 billion saved) in 2025 and 42,605 fractures (NT$4.64 billion saved) by 2045. Conclusion Comprehensive osteoporosis management strategies incorporating enhanced case finding and improved adherence will substantially reduce clinical and economic burden in Taiwan's aging population over the next two decades, supporting evidence-based healthcare policy development.

title: Closed reduction in distal radius fractures: manual manipulation vs. finger trap traction-a prospective randomized controlled clinical trial.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Benedikt S, Horling L, Bode S, Stock K, Schmidle G, Arora R.
abstract: Background Initial treatment of distal radius fractures (DRF) can be either performed without reduction or with a reduction method as finger-trap traction (FTT) only or by additional manual reduction (MR) under hematoma block. There is no clear evidence on which reduction method is superior, however, MR is more invasive and seems to lead to higher pain levels and more post reduction complications. The objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical relevance of MR compared to FTT in acute DRFs. Materials and methods Study design was a prospective, single-centre, balanced randomized [1:1], and parallel grouped, controlled trial. Inclusion criteria were patients with a DRF type A2, A3 or C according to the AO classification and a dorsal tilt of ≥ 10°. The patients were randomized either in the FTT or in the MR group. Depending on the patient's functional demand and the fracture configuration, conservative or operative treatment was initiated. Over one year, clinical and radiological data were assessed at six follow-ups. Results A total of 53 patients were included. Regarding radiological results neither FTT nor MR achieved sufficient reduction results (median dorsal tilt was - 16 to -18 after one year) and none of the techniques was superior. The clinical results between the conservatively treated groups were comparable and showed no significant difference. Complications included one CRPS in the conservative MR group, one CRPS after FTT and operation, one secondary carpal tunnel syndrome in the conservative FTT group and one skin lesion after MR. Conclusion Manual reduction under haematoma block showed no benefit. In patients with AO type A2, A3 and type C fractures and a dorsal tilt ≥ 10° only FTT (if required under a haematoma block or comparable analgesia) is recommended regardless of whether surgery is performed or not. Level of evidence Level I randomized controlled trial. Trial registration number ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07697976, registered 06/22/2026, retrospectively registered, www. Clinicaltrials gov .

title: Bilateral Lateral Tarsal Artery Bypass and Free Flap Reconstruction of an Infected Gangrenous Heel in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: A Case Report of Three-Year Functional Limb Salvage.
authors: Yokoyama N, Kikuchi S, Jinno H, Uramoto T, Takahashi K, Kamada K, Tatsukawa T, Moriyama U, Yoshida Y, Hinooka R, Fujiki T, Azuma N.
abstract: Introduction Distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is technically demanding when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and revascularization alone seldom heals an extensive heel defect. Case presentation A man in his 60s receiving maintenance hemodialysis presented with bilateral CLTI and gangrene of the left heel after failed endovascular therapy, and bilateral major amputations had been considered before referral. Both limbs were classified as Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection clinical stage 4. Diffuse calcification of the infrapopliteal and pedal arteries left the lateral tarsal artery (LTA) as the only suitable distal target, and bilateral superficial femoral artery-to-LTA bypasses were performed with in situ great saphenous vein grafts under nerve block anesthesia. Because repeated debridement left the calcaneus exposed, a free latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap anastomosed to the left bypass graft was transferred and covered with a split-thickness skin graft. The wounds healed after minor amputations, and the patient regained independent ambulation. An ulcer subsequently developed on the weight-bearing surface of the transferred flap and never healed despite pressure-relieving insoles and additional inflow angioplasty; nevertheless, the flap remained viable, both grafts remained patent, and ambulatory function was preserved until the patient died of an unrelated cause 3 years after revascularization. Conclusions The LTA can serve as a distal bypass target when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and, when combined with free flap reconstruction, it may achieve long-term functional limb salvage despite extensive heel gangrene. The reconstructed weight-bearing heel nevertheless remains prone to ulceration that may not heal, so preventive off-loading and long-term surveillance are essential.

title: A composite inflammation-nutrition-coagulation score and 1-year mortality in geriatric proximal femur fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Bozgeyik B, Kaya O, Önder C, Atmaca E, Çakar A.
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of a composite score integrating the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), serum albumin, and D-dimer levels for predicting 1-year mortality in geriatric patients with proximal femur fractures. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort study included 300 patients aged ≥ 65 years who were admitted with proximal femur fractures and underwent surgical treatment between November 2023 and March 2026. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected from hospital records. A composite score based on NLR, albumin, and D-dimer was calculated. An exploratory unweighted 0-3 composite score was constructed from cohort-derived ROC thresholds for NLR, albumin, and D-dimer. Logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox regression, calibration analysis, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were performed to evaluate predictive performance. Results A total of 300 patients were analyzed, of whom 75 (25.0%) died within 1 year. Non-survivors were older and had significantly higher NLR and D-dimer levels and lower albumin levels (all p Conclusions In this retrospective single-center cohort, the composite score integrating NLR, albumin, and D-dimer was associated with 1-year mortality and showed promising apparent discriminatory performance. The score should be considered an exploratory prognostic tool that may complement comprehensive clinical assessment and support future risk-stratification research. Prospective multicenter studies with external validation and evaluation of clinical impact are required before its use in routine practice can be considered.

title: YouTube Videos on Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition Show Low-to-Moderate Quality and Reliability.
authors: Conteduca J, Longo D, Piacquadio F, Casto A, Valentino L, Bernetti A, Rollo G.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the quality and reliability of YouTube videos on arthrogenic muscle inhibition (AMI) using validated assessment instruments and to identify predictors of higher-quality content. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed English-language YouTube videos identified on November 2, 2025, using the search terms "arthrogenic muscle inhibition" and "AMI." Video quality was assessed using the DISCERN, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Global Quality Score instruments. Assessments were performed independently by 2 experienced knee surgeons. Correlations between quality scores and video characteristics (views, likes, comments, time online, duration, source, and topic) were analyzed using nonparametric tests and multivariate regression with Bonferroni correction. Results A total of 45 videos were analyzed. Mean scores were 44.9 ± 20.5 for DISCERN, 1.47 ± 1.56 for Journal of the American Medical Association, and 2.93 ± 1.53 for Global Quality Score, indicating overall low-to-moderate quality. Video quality was strongly correlated across scoring systems ( ρ > 0.86, P P ρ = -0.37, P = .046). Video topic was the strongest independent predictor of video quality ( P Conclusions YouTube videos on AMI demonstrate low-to-moderate quality and reliability, with substantial variation by topic and content type. Clinical relevance Improving the quality of online AMI-related content may enhance patient education and promote accurate dissemination of rehabilitation information.

title: Two-Dimensional Electromagnetic Navigation-Assisted Percutaneous Transforaminal Endoscopic Discectomy for Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
authors: Wei Z, Cheng H, Gao R, Wang X, Niu K, Tao Z, An H, Huang B, Xiong C, Lian J.
abstract: Objective To compare the clinical performance, safety, radiation exposure, and learning curve of two-dimensional (2D) electromagnetic navigation-assisted percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy (PTED) with those of three-dimensional (3D) electromagnetic navigation-assisted PTED in patients with lumbar disc herniation (LDH). Methods This retrospective cohort study included 82 patients with LDH who underwent PTED between January 2022 and June 2024. Patients were classified into the 2D electromagnetic navigation group or the 3D electromagnetic navigation group according to the navigation workflow used during surgery. Perioperative variables, including total operative time, navigation registration time, radiation exposure, and complications, were recorded. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the visual analogue scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and modified MacNab criteria. Learning curves for both the surgeon and the radiologic technologist were evaluated using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis. Results Compared with the 3D group, the 2D group demonstrated a significantly shorter total operative time (66.64 ± 9.67 vs. 88.92 ± 15.98 min, p Conclusion 2D electromagnetic navigation-assisted PTED is a safe and clinically effective alternative to 3D electromagnetic navigation-assisted PTED for the treatment of LDH. Relative to the 3D workflow, the 2D approach offers greater procedural efficiency, reduced radiation exposure, and a shorter learning curve. Although longitudinal analysis revealed different recovery patterns over time for low back pain and ODI between the two groups, both techniques achieved substantial postoperative improvement, favorable final clinical outcomes, and comparable safety. These findings suggest that simplified 2D electromagnetic navigation may represent a more practical and scalable option for routine clinical application.

title: The "Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability Technique" (MERI Technique): A Simple Lateral Tenodesis Reconstructing the Condylar Strap, the Distal Kaplan Fibers, and the Femoral Insertion of the Anterolateral Ligament to Control Internal Rotation During Anterior Cruciate Ligament Surgery.
authors: Bouguennec N, Colombet P, Graveleau N.
abstract: The Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique is a simple and minimally invasive lateral tenodesis designed to enhance internal rotation control during anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction by reconstructing the distal Kaplan fibers, the condylar strap, and the femoral insertion of the anterolateral ligament. Using a 1-cm-wide fascia lata strip, the procedure involves fixation with a single anchor at an isometric point proximal to the anterolateral ligament insertion, followed by a continuous locking suture and fascia lata closure on the anchor, which further reinforces rotational stability without excessive constraint. Although possibly biomechanically less restrictive than traditional lateral extra-articular tenodesis, the Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique strikes a balance between stability and flexibility, potentially reducing postoperative stiffness and morbidity. Its simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and minimal invasiveness make it a valuable alternative for addressing anterolateral instability in select anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction patients.

title: Temporal MRI appearance of postoperative healing after proximal hamstring musculotendinous complex repair.
authors: Mechó S, Pérez P, Congo A, Isern-Kebschull J, Alomar X, Pruna R, Valle X, Yanguas X, Moix I, Puigdellívol J, Lempainen L, Aguilar M, Pedret C, Kassarjian A, Rodas G.
abstract: Objective To describe the temporal MRI features of healing during the first 4 months following surgical repair of complete tears of the proximal hamstring musculotendinous complex. Materials and methods Consecutive case series. Professional football players with MRI-confirmed complete tears surgically repaired between May 2017 and December 2025 were retrospectively identified. Postoperative MRI examinations were obtained during routine clinical follow-up using 3-T systems. Two musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated longitudinal and transverse intratendinous clefts, scar maturation, edema-like signal, postoperative subcutaneous soft-tissue signal change, tendinous angulation, blunt muscle outline, and denervation-like signal. Results Twenty-four complete tears in 20 players underwent surgical repair. Fifteen tendons with an uncomplicated postoperative course comprised the primary descriptive cohort, yielding 43 MRI examinations. Longitudinal intratendinous clefts were observed in 11/15 (73.3%) of tendons, transverse intratendinous clefts in 13/15 (86.7%), postoperative subcutaneous soft-tissue signal change and tendinous angulation in 15/15 (100%), blunt muscle outline in 13/15 (86.7%), and denervation-like signal in 10/15 (66.7%). In the within-tendon analysis, longitudinal and transverse intratendinous clefts resolved by the last available MRI in 6/10 (60%) and 7/12 (58.3%) tendons, respectively. All 10 tendons with an initially immature scar progressed to a mature scar. Among six tendons with postoperative exacerbation, four showed extensive, prominent intratendinous clefts with marked PD-FS hyperintensity on the preceding MRI, associated with immature scar, intratendinous cavity, or persistent interstitial edema-like signal. Conclusion Serial MRI demonstrated different temporal patterns of postoperative healing. Residual intratendinous clefts may coexist with a mature scar during tendon remodeling and do not necessarily indicate delayed healing.

title: Single-stage matrix-assisted bone marrow-derived cell concentrate implantation for osteochondral talar lesions: a 24-month clinical and MRI follow-up.
authors: Caggiari G, Rinaldi M, Santandrea A, Mercurio D, Lugani G, D'Alessandro S, Deng H, Migliorini F, Pisanu F, Doria C, Cortese F, Puddu L.
abstract: Background The optimal surgical management of larger chronic osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT) remains debated. This study describes 24-month clinical and MRI outcomes after a combined single-stage matrix-assisted procedure using debridement, bone-marrow stimulation, autologous bone marrow-derived cell concentrate, a type I collagen scaffold, and fibrin glue. Methods This exploratory retrospective case series screened consecutive patients treated between January 2016 and December 2020. Twenty-six patients were identified; 15 had sufficiently complete clinical and MRI data for the predefined 24-month complete-case analysis. Eligible lesions were classified as Giannini type II-IIA and Outerbridge grade III-IV. The principal clinical endpoint was the 24-month change in the American Orthopaedic Foot Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot score. Secondary outcomes included Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain, 24-month MRI morphology assessed with the MOCART system, and reoperations. Six- and 12-month assessments were part of routine care but were not sufficiently complete for formal longitudinal analysis. Results The mean AOFAS score increased from 57.3 ± 12.0 at baseline to 92.4 ± 7.1 at 24 months, an absolute improvement of 35.1 points. The mean VAS score decreased from 4.7 ± 1.2 to 1.8 ± 0.8, an absolute reduction of 2.9 points. At 24 months, complete defect filling was observed in 12 of 15 patients (80.0%), hypertrophic filling in 2 (13.3%), and incomplete filling in 1 (6.7%). Complete integration with adjacent tissue was observed in 14 patients (93.3%); preserved surface morphology and uniform repair-tissue structure were each observed in 12 (80.0%). Mean MOCART score was 83.7 ± 14.4. Three patients (20.0%) underwent arthroscopic reoperation for symptomatic anterior impingement. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort, the combined single-stage procedure was associated with improved 24-month pain and functional scores and favorable MRI morphology of repair tissue. The uncontrolled design and multimodal procedure do not establish comparative efficacy, superiority, or an independent cell-specific treatment effect. Larger prospective controlled studies are needed.

title: Significant Geographic Variation in the Epidemiology and Management of Pediatric Osteochondritis Dissecans Exists Between the Asia-Pacific and North America.
authors: Wong JRY, Lam YX, Tan SHS, Hui JHP, Wang M.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate regional variations in epidemiology, diagnostic approaches, and surgical interventions for pediatric osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) between Asia-Pacific (APAC) and North America (NA). Methods A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library databases was conducted from database inception until August 2025. Studies on epidemiology and surgical treatment of pediatric OCD were screened independently by 2 reviewers. Data was extracted and collated according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis guidelines, and risk of bias was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies. Results Sixty-five studies comprising 2194 patients were analyzed-29 from APAC (803 patients) and 36 from NA (1391 patients). Patients' age (APAC: 9-18 years; NA: 6-19 years) and follow-up duration (APAC: 8-184 months; NA: 2-216 months) were similar. Significant regional differences were observed across multiple domains. Sex distribution was markedly skewed in APAC, where most studies included predominantly male participants (91.9%) without intentional female disaggregation, compared with a more balanced cohort in NA (55.3%). Although the elbow was the most common OCD site overall, knee involvement was significantly higher in NA (36.1%) than APAC (20.7%). Imaging modalities differed-radiographs were the most common imaging tool in both regions, but magnetic resonance imaging was more frequently used in NA (48.9%) compared with APAC (35.8%). Surgical approaches also varied significantly: osteochondral grafting was more common in APAC (41.7%), whereas arthroscopic techniques were favored in NA (73.5%). In situ fixation rates were similar between regions. Standardized reporting and prospective, multicenter registries are essential for enabling patient-level analysis and guiding region-specific, evidence-based care for pediatric OCD. Conclusions There are significant regional variations in epidemiology, imaging modalities, and surgical management for pediatric OCD. The predominantly male bias in the APAC region, greater use of magnetic resonance imaging, and arthroscopic techniques in the NA region reflect underlying biological, cultural, and health care-related differences. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level III and IV studies.

title: Shear-wave elastography in rotator cuff tears: a systematic review of measurement properties, tissue-stiffness findings, and clinical interpretability.
authors: Trybulski R, Sozański T, Kużdżał A, Wang HK, Olaniszyn G, Kawczynski A.
abstract: Objectives Shear-wave elastography (SWE) may quantify rotator cuff mechanical properties, but its measurement performance and clinical interpretability remain incompletely established. This work sought to synthesize evidence on the feasibility, measurement properties, and interpretability of rotator cuff SWE in adults with rotator cuff tears (RCTs). Materials and methods PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies were in vivo primary studies in adults (≥ 18 years) with suspected or symptomatic rotator cuff disease in whom partial- or full-thickness RCT was confirmed by an imaging or surgical reference standard, including conventional ultrasound, MRI, CT, or arthroscopy, and/or studies including clinically relevant comparator shoulders or asymptomatic controls. Studies had to use ultrasound SWE with quantitative outputs, including shear-wave speed/velocity or modulus, in the supraspinatus tendon and/or rotator cuff muscles. Results Thirteen SWE studies were retained from 6273 records. Two primarily assessed reliability/repeatability. Intra-rater reproducibility was high in the primary reliability studies, including ICCs > 0.87 and 0.96, whereas inter-rater reproducibility was lower and variable, ranging from ICCs > 0.73 to 0.45. Eleven studies contributed construct-validity or known-groups evidence, one provided strict criterion-validity evidence against intraoperative passive stiffness, and two provided longitudinal postoperative evidence. SWE findings varied across tissue targets, devices, regions of interest, arm positions, comparators, and reference standards. Only one study explicitly defined chronicity, and direct postoperative/prognostic evidence was limited. Conclusions SWE appears useful as a complementary quantitative imaging tool for selected rotator cuff tissue-characterization and measurement-property applications. However, inter-rater reproducibility, measurement error, chronicity assessment, and prognostic validity remain insufficiently established. Key points Question Can shear-wave elastography (SWE) address the unmet need for reliable quantitative rotator cuff tissue assessment beyond conventional imaging in adults with tears? Findings Thirteen studies showed high intra-rater reproducibility but variable inter-rater reproducibility. Evidence for chronicity assessment and prognosis remained sparse and heterogeneous. Clinical relevance SWE may complement ultrasound or MRI by quantifying selected rotator cuff mechanical properties, but current evidence does not justify using it alone to determine tear chronicity, reparability, or prognosis.

title: Serum uric acid and bone mineral density: Reappraising an overstated association.
authors: Dimnik JM, Lavender B, Topham JJ.
abstract: A recent acceleration in NHANES-based serum uric acid (SUA) and bone mineral density (BMD) publications has encouraged recommendations to relax the treatment target for hyperuricemia, possibly placing patients at higher risk for gout. We reappraised pooled 2005-2018 NHANES data to determine whether SUA supports a clinically meaningful bone-protective role. Survey-weighted analyses of 3687 to 6039 participants assessed the influence of SUA on BMD at 10 anatomical sites, with femoral neck and total lumbar spine BMD as co-primary outcomes, as well as osteoporosis and fragility fracture. Higher SUA was nominally associated with slightly higher total lumbar spine BMD (βˆ=0.0062, 0.0003-0.0122, P=0.042) but not femoral neck BMD (βˆ=0.0035, -0.0006-0.0076, P=0.093). Allometric analyses revealed a similar pattern. Restricted cubic splines depicted a linear association at the lumbar spine and a nonlinear femoral neck association which flattened near the SUA solubility limit of 6.8 mg/dL. Importantly, all clinical end points were null; SUA was not associated with osteoporosis or fragility fracture in the primary continuous models (ORs 0.960 to 1.007; all P≥0.743). Alternative thresholds, quintile trends, and sensitivity analyses showed no consistent association. Higher SUA was not associated with femoral neck BMD or total lumbar spine BMD across 18/21 and 13/21 sensitivity tests, respectively. Notably, when 24-hour dietary intake was considered in sensitivity analyses, none of the outcomes maintained statistical significance. Thus, modest site-specific associations between SUA and BMD did not translate into clinical benefit. These findings do not support a direct bone-protective role for SUA or relaxation of the 6.0 mg/dL hyperuricemia treatment target.

title: Semimembranosus Autograft Harvesting and Reconstruction for Knee Posteromedial Complex Laxity Using a "Romal Reins" Technique.
authors: Kodkani P.
abstract: This technical report presents semimembranosus tendon harvest and its use as an autograft in knee ligament reconstruction. The distal semimembranosus tendon is a robust and long tendon, which makes it a suitable autograft option with its distal insertions kept intact. It has multiple insertions onto the posteromedial corner of the tibia and the posteromedial ligament complex (PMC). Tensioning this tendon insertion results in tightening of the PMC and thus achieves posteromedial stability. Harvesting the tendon with its lateral third left intact with its muscular attachment retains its dynamic action. Using the medial two-thirds of the tendon as an autograft for PMC reconstruction with a "Romal Reins" concept restores joint stability. The graft is notably beneficial in cases of multiligament laxity where there may be a shortage of free autografts for PMC reconstruction. This technique tightens and reconstructs the major PMC stabilizing structures without requiring individual structural reconstructions. It reduces the need for multiple grafts, reconstructions, bone tunnels, and implants for managing PMC laxity. This technique of semimembranosus tendon graft harvest and PMC reconstruction is safe, simple, minimally invasive, and effective with the least risk of complications. It could possibly be a preferred graft and reconstruction technique for PMC reconstruction.

title: Rotational-progress-dependent pelvic, thoracic, and support-foot kinematics during a standardised Rumba spiral turn in highly trained adolescent female Latin dancers.
authors: Guo M, Ismail MHB, Abdul Ghani DZB, Liang Q, Gao Y.
abstract: Rumba turning involves continuous whole-body reorientation, but discrete kinematic summaries do not localise where consistent directional deviations occur across the turn. This exploratory study examined rotational-progress-dependent patterns of pelvic obliquity, thoracic frontal-plane angle, and right support-foot progression angle during the initial 360° Rumba spiral turn in highly trained adolescent female Latin dancers. Fifteen dancers aged 14-16 years completed five valid trials each (75 trials). Three-dimensional kinematics were recorded using a 10-camera Vicon system at 100 Hz. For each trial, accumulated pelvic rotation was used to define rotational progress, and the three outcome waveforms were resampled to 101 points across 0%-100% of the turn. The five trials from each participant were averaged point by point, yielding 15 participant-level representative waveforms per outcome. Two-tailed one-sample statistical parametric mapping (SPM{t}) tests identified intervals in which group mean waveforms differed from their corresponding Plug-in Gait model-defined 0° references, using a Bonferroni-adjusted primary α = 0.0167 across the three outcomes. Pelvic obliquity showed a positive deviation at 11.3%-47.2% and a negative deviation at 56.5%-97.3% of rotational progress. Thoracic frontal-plane angle showed a negative deviation at 13.2%-41.9% and positive deviations at 57.6%-83.0% and 85.7%-92.0%. Right support-foot progression angle showed negative, positive, and negative deviations at 0.0%-4.8%, 10.4%-49.1%, and 56.2%-100.0%, respectively. Sensitivity analyses without the additional across-outcome Bonferroni adjustment preserved the principal directional patterns, with only modest changes in cluster extent and continuity. These findings identify where, across rotational progress, the measured segmental orientations consistently departed from model-defined references during a standardised Rumba spiral turn, without implying normative targets of optimal dance technique.

title: Patellar Tendon Allograft Reconstruction Using Achilles Graft With Traversing Suprapatellar Cerclage Limbs.
authors: Mahatme RJ, Moore SA, Muthusamy N, Grawe BM, Lamplot JD, Bernholt DL.
abstract: Patellar tendon rupture and chronic extensor mechanism deficiency present significant reconstructive challenges, particularly in revision settings or when native tissue quality is poor. We describe a reproducible surgical technique for patellar tendon reconstruction using an Achilles allograft with traversing suprapatellar cerclage limbs. This construct helps facilitate controlled restoration of patellar height, immediate continuity of the extensor mechanism, and load sharing across the reconstruction during early healing.

title: Paraparesis and left upper extremity weakness after total arch replacement with frozen elephant trunk: possible contributions of spinal cord ischaemia and cervical radiculopathy.
authors: Ishihama T, Yokawa K, Shimatani Y, Uesugi K, Ishimoto K, Higuma T, Yoshida K, Obo H, Wakiyama H.
abstract: An 82-year-old man underwent total arch replacement with the frozen elephant trunk technique for an aortic arch aneurysm. Upon awakening 3 hours postoperatively, the patient exhibited flaccid paralysis of both lower extremities and left upper extremity weakness, whereas the right upper extremity was largely preserved. Cerebrospinal fluid drainage and blood pressure augmentation were initiated for suspected spinal cord ischemia. Lower-extremity motor function partially recovered, but left upper-extremity weakness persisted. Spinal magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated intramedullary T2 hyperintensity at T2/3 and bilateral neural foraminal stenosis from C3/4 to C6/7. Neurological examination revealed predominant weakness in the left C7 myotome with an absent left triceps reflexes, suggesting concomitant C7 radiculopathy. This case demonstrates that neurological deficits after aortic arch surgery may be multifactorial and highlights the value of detailed neurological examination and spinal imaging when upper extremity weakness is disproportionate.

title: Nationwide trends and demographic projections of hospitalisations for vertebral fractures and postmenopausal osteoporosis in Germany: a 24-year registry-based study.
authors: Anees H, Qadourah K, Georgievski G, Heiss C, El Khassawna T.
abstract: Hospitalisations for vertebral fractures increased in Germany over the past two decades. Although hospitalisation rates have recently stabilised or declined, demographic projections indicate that the absolute inpatient hospitalisation burden may remain substantial through 2050. These findings highlight the need for better osteoporosis prevention and long-term healthcare planning. Background Vertebral fractures represent one of the most common manifestations of skeletal fragility and contribute substantially to morbidity, disability, and healthcare utilisation in ageing populations. However, nationwide long-term hospitalisation trends and the impact of demographic ageing on future inpatient burden remain insufficiently characterised. This study investigated inpatient hospitalisation trends for vertebral fractures and postmenopausal osteoporosis in Germany over a 24-year period and estimated the future inpatient burden through 2050. Methods Nationwide inpatient data from the German Federal Health Monitoring (GBE) database were analysed between 2000 and 2023. Hospitalisations were identified using ICD-10-GM codes for thoracic vertebral fractures (S22.0), lumbar vertebral fractures (S32.0), and postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture (M80.0). Absolute hospitalisations, age-standardised hospitalisation rates, sex-specific trends, in-hospital mortality, and length of hospital stay were evaluated. Temporal trends were assessed using joinpoint regression. Future hospitalisations were projected by applying age-specific hospitalisation rates observed during 2021-2023 to the official German population projections (Destatis main scenario G2L2W2). Results Between 2000 and 2023, annual hospitalisations increased from 14,057 to 27,563 for thoracic vertebral fractures, from 27,683 to 45,280 for lumbar vertebral fractures, and from 2,617 to 11,800 for postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture. In contrast, age-standardised hospitalisation rates increased until the mid-to-late 2010s before stabilising or declining across all three diagnoses. Joinpoint regression identified significant trend reversals for thoracic vertebral fractures (2016), lumbar vertebral fractures (2018), and postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture (2015). Overall, lumbar vertebral fractures (AAPC - 0.65%, p = 0.01) and postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture (AAPC - 1.17%, p Conclusions Although age-standardised hospitalisation rates have stabilised or declined in recent years, demographic projections indicate that the inpatient hospitalisation burden associated with vertebral fractures may remain substantial in Germany. These findings underscore the need for timely osteoporosis diagnosis, systematic secondary fracture prevention, and long-term healthcare planning for an ageing population.

title: Musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America: Workforce characteristics, resource availability, and territorial disparities.
authors: Zamora T, Vidal C, Suarez H, Botello E, Galli Serra M, Casales N, Zeballos J, Zumarraga JP, Cuervo C, Linares F.
abstract: Purpose Musculoskeletal oncology requires highly specialized, multidisciplinary care. Although the subspecialty has evolved worldwide, information on workforce characteristics, resource availability, and practice patterns across Latin America remains limited. Methods A cross-sectional survey using convenience sampling was conducted among orthopaedic surgeons involved in musculoskeletal oncology throughout Latin America. An adapted version of a previously published questionnaire was distributed through the Latin American Society of Musculoskeletal Tumors (SLATME) and professional networks. The survey explored training background, clinical practice characteristics, perceived support from selected specialties and specialized resources, perceived professional challenges, and treatment preferences. We performed descriptive analyses and comparisons by practice-location population size ( Results A total of 147 surgeons from 17 countries participated. Most respondents reported formal orthopaedic oncology training (76%) and academic orteaching involvement (93%). Respondents practicing in locations with ≥ one million inhabitants were significantly more likely to report treating ≥ 30 cases annually of soft tissue sarcoma (47% vs. 14%, p Conclusion Among survey respondents, musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America was characterized by high rates of specialized training and academic or teaching involvement. However, differences in the reported annual numbers of new malignant tumour cases treated and in access to advanced resources were observed according to practice-location population size. Because this study used a convenience sampling strategy, these findings reflect the respondents' practices but should not be generalized to the entire Latin American musculoskeletal oncology community.

title: MRI for the detection of hip abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients with total hip arthroplasty following a lateral surgical approach.
authors: Marth AA, Allen M, Liu Y, Joseph GB, Bini SA, Link TM, Feuerriegel GC.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of MRI for detecting clinically suspected hip abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients after total hip arthroplasty and to evaluate the association between specific MRI features and surgically confirmed tears. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 36 patients with total hip arthroplasty who underwent revision surgery for a suspected abductor tendon tear and had preoperative MRI available. Intraoperative findings served as the reference standard for the presence of partial or full-thickness tears of the gluteus medius (Gmed) and gluteus minimus (Gmin) tendons. Two readers evaluated MRI for tendon integrity (intact, partial-thickness, or full-thickness tear). Associations between tendon defects, peritrochanteric fluid, tendon signal abnormalities, and Gmed/Gmin Goutallier grades with surgical findings were analyzed using regression models to calculate odds ratios (ORs). Results For detection of abductor tendon tears, Reader 1 achieved sensitivities of 0.86-1.00, specificities of 0.93-1.00, and accuracies of 0.92-0.97, while Reader 2 achieved sensitivities of 0.86-1.00, specificities of 0.90-1.00, and accuracies of 0.89-1.00. Imaging findings associated with partial- or full-thickness tears included tendon defects (Gmed: OR = 35.5, p = 0.007; Gmin: OR = 30.0, p Conclusion MRI demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting surgically confirmed hip abductor tendon tears in this selected symptomatic surgical cohort following total hip arthroplasty. Tendon defects and peritrochanteric fluid were significantly associated with partial- or full-thickness tendon tears. Key points Question There is limited data on the diagnostic accuracy of MRI for hip abductor tendon tear detection following total hip arthroplasty. Findings MRI demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting surgically confirmed abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients with total hip arthroplasty. Clinical relevance In symptomatic patients with clinical suspicion of an abductor tendon tear undergoing evaluation for revision surgery, MRI can be used to noninvasively assess the integrity of the abductor tendons after total hip arthroplasty.

title: Long-term use of opioids and neuropathic medication after diaphyseal humerus fractures with or without nerve injury: a nationwide register-based cohort study of 4,185 patients.
authors: Nyman E, Andersson S, Perez R, Zimmerman M, Merlo J, Dahlin LB.
abstract: Background and purpose Diaphyseal humerus fractures may lead to prolonged pain medication use. We aimed to study pain medication use after such fractures, focusing on nerve injury. Methods Using Swedish register data (2007-2015), we identified individuals with diaphyseal humerus fractures. High use of opioids and neuropathic pain medication (≥ 60% of days covered/year; 2-month post-fracture washout) was evaluated in 5 groups: the general population (reference) and fractures treated nonoperatively or surgically, with and without nerve injury. Relative risks (RRs; 95% confidence intervals [CIs]; crude and adjusted [aRR] models; adjusted for age, sex, country of birth, income, and cohabitation status; and for previous high use of pain medication during the first year when analyzing the second year) were estimated in Cox proportional hazards regression models. Results We identified 4,185 individuals with diaphyseal humerus fractures (3.7% with nerve injury; 23% surgically treated). In the first year, opioid use was higher among surgically treated fractures with nerve injury (aRR 17.6, CI 11.0-28.3) and without nerve injury (aRR 9.5, CI 8.2-10.9) than in the general population. In the second year, opioid use declined across most groups but remained elevated among nonoperatively treated fractures with nerve injury (aRR 8.3, CI 2.6-26.1). Neuropathic pain medication use increased in the first year, with no elevated use in the second. Adjustment did not change overall patterns. Women, older adults, lower-income individuals, and those living alone showed higher medication risk use. Conclusion Patients with a diaphyseal humerus fracture were associated with a substantial burden of pain medication use, particularly for opioids during the first year post-injury in surgically treated fractures with nerve injury (RR 17.6) and a persistent risk in the second year among nonoperatively treated fractures with nerve injury (RR 8.3). Demographics and socioeconomic factors strongly relate to medication use, highlighting the need for careful early pain management and monitoring for prolonged medication use in exposed groups.

title: Joint-preserving reconstruction of an acute Type IV reverse Hill-Sachs lesion following posterior shoulder fracture-dislocation: a case report.
authors: Vitali M, Montalbano F, Salini V.
abstract: Posterior shoulder fracture-dislocation is a rare injury frequently associated with delayed diagnosis because of its subtle clinical and radiographic presentation. Management is primarily determined by the size of the reverse Hill-Sachs lesion, with shoulder arthroplasty generally recommended for extensive humeral head defects.
