Independent risk markers included older age, female sex, lower bone mineral density (BMD) T-score, prior fragility fracture, two-level treatment, intravertebral cleft, intradiscal leakage, absence of anti-osteoporosis treatment, chronic glucocorticoid exposure, and deviation from a midrange cement volume. The association for group IV was stronger during months 0-12 than during months 13-24. Conclusions Cement contact with both endplates was associated with better long-term pain and functional outcomes and greater refracture-free survival after extensive adjustment. However, the adjusted 24-month differences in VAS and ODI did not exceed commonly accepted minimal clinically important difference (MCID) thresholds, so the clinical magnitude remains uncertain. These findings provide useful prognostic information for surgical planning, although prospective validation is warranted.

title: Direct anterior versus conventional approaches for hemiarthroplasty in femoral neck fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis of functional outcomes.
journal: Journal of Clinical Orthopaedics and Trauma
authors: Sarkar MH, Maheshwari S, Vardhan S, Singh L, Das SL, Goyal T.
abstract: Background Femoral neck fracture (FNF) in older adults is associated with morbidity and functional decline. The optimal surgical approach for hemiarthroplasty (HA) remains uncertain. The direct anterior approach (DAA), a muscle-sparing technique, may improve early recovery compared with conventional approaches. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared DAA with conventional approaches following HA for FNF. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched through December 2025 according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Comparative studies of DAA versus conventional approaches were included. The primary outcome was Harris Hip Score (HHS); secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, operative time, blood loss, transfusion, and hospital stay. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251270460). Results Forty-two studies involving 7582 patients were included. Three studies contributed to early HHS analysis, showing no significant difference between approaches (MD, 1.38; 95% CI, -4.85 to 7.60; I 2 = 77.2%). Similarly, three studies at mid-term follow-up showed no significant difference (MD, 1.04; 95% CI, -3.67 to 5.76; I 2 = 67.8%). Only 1 study provided quantitatively evaluable long-term HHS data (MD, 0.70; 95% CI, -2.41 to 3.81). DAA was associated with lower postoperative pain (SMD, -0.38; 95% CI, -0.72 to -0.05; P = 0.02), lower blood loss (MD, -61.0 mL; 95% CI, -103.2 to -18.9 mL; P Conclusions DAA was associated with modest perioperative benefits following HA for FNF. However, HHS analyses did not demonstrate statistically significant functional differences at early or mid-term follow-up, and long-term evidence was limited. Sustained functional superiority of DAA remains uncertain. Level of evidence Level III (systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised and observational comparative studies).

title: Development of a composite pain sensitivity index and its relationships with knee pain severity and patterns in people with or at risk for knee osteoarthritis: The multicenter osteoarthritis study.
authors: Aoyagi K, Bacon K, LaValley M, Frey-Law LA, Lewis CE, Nevitt M, Neogi T.
abstract: Objective Altered ascending and descending nociceptive signaling in the nervous system is associated with pain severity and patterns in knee osteoarthritis (OA). Because alterations across multiple nociceptive pathways can co-occur, a composite assessment may yield better insight than examining individual pathways separately. We therefore developed a composite pain sensitivity index (PSI) and evaluated its relation to the pain outcomes in those with or at risk of knee OA. Design Using data from the Multicenter Osteoarthritis (MOST) Study, a NIH-funded longitudinal cohort, we developed an age- and sex-specific composite PSI incorporating quantitative sensory testing (QST) measures of ascending pain facilitation and descending pain modulation, including pressure pain threshold (PPT) at the knee and wrist, temporal summation (TS), and conditioned pain modulation (CPM). PSI was scaled to range 0-100 such that higher scores indicate greater pain sensitivity. Pain outcome measures included WOMAC pain severity, frequent knee pain (FKP), and constant pain, assessed with the Intermittent and Constant Osteoarthritis Pain (ICOAP). We evaluated the relations of the PSI and each individual QST measure to these pain outcomes cross-sectionally and longitudinally over two years using log-binomial, Poisson, and linear regression models as appropriate, adjusting for potential confounders. Results We included 2679 participants. Cross-sectionally, each 10-unit increase in PSI had greater WOMAC pain severity (adjusted β: 0.45, 95%CI: 0.38-0.52), a 20% greater risk of FKP (95%CI: 1.15-1.26), and a 27% greater risk of constant pain (95% CI 1.14-1.41); these associations were generally larger than for the individual QST measures. Longitudinally, baseline PSI was associated with WOMAC pain severity 2 years later (adjusted β: 0.40, 95%CI: 0.33-0.49) and development of constant pain (aRR: 1.18, 95%CI: 0.99-1.40), whereas its association with incident FKP was minimal and not statistically significant (aRR: 1.06, 95%CI: 0.98-1.14), similar to that of wrist PPT (aRR: 1.05, 95%CI: 1.00-1.10). Conclusions A composite PSI combining QST measures of ascending (PPT/TS) and descending (CPM) nociceptive signaling had generally stronger associations than individual QST measures cross-sectionally, and to a lesser extent longitudinally. A composite PSI may provide better insights into capturing concurrent pain status than individual QST measures, whereas its predictive utility over time appears to be more pain outcome-specific.

title: Comparable clinical outcomes but different postoperative Dynamic Alignment of the Knee (DyAK) patterns between cruciate-retaining and posterior-stabilized inserts in functionally aligned robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
authors: Koutserimpas C, Veizi E, Lustig S, Dretakis K.
abstract: Purpose The influence of polyethylene insert design during robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) performed according to functional alignment (FA) principles remains poorly understood. This study compared cruciate-retaining (CR) and posterior-stabilized (PS) inserts with respect to implant positioning, clinical outcomes, implant survivorship and postoperative dynamic knee behaviour using the Dynamic Alignment of the Knee (DyAK) classification. Methods A retrospective comparative study was performed on 284 primary functionally aligned robotic-assisted TKAs. The cohort comprised 148 CR and 136 PS fixed-bearing cemented implants with a minimum follow-up of 3 years (median 44.5 months). Clinical outcomes included Knee Society Score (KSS) and Forgotten Joint Score (FJS). Intraoperative robotic implant positioning, bone resections, polyethylene thickness, DyAK classification, complications and Kaplan-Meier implant survivorship were compared between groups. Results The CR group demonstrated greater preoperative varus alignment (median robotic hip-knee-ankle angle [rHKA] 5° vs. 3°, p = 0.01). Compared with PS implants, CR inserts were implanted with greater tibial varus (2° vs. 1°, p p p = 0.009). Polyethylene inserts >9 mm were required more frequently in the PS group (39.0% vs. 15.5%, p p = 0.56), KSS function ( p = 0.62) and FJS ( p = 0.06) were comparable between groups. No statistically significant difference in survivorship was detected for aseptic loosening (0.68% vs. 0.74%, p = 0.95) and all-cause revision (2.03% vs. 1.47%, p = 0.72). The DyAK classification changed significantly more frequently in the PS group than in the CR group (69.9% vs. 52.7%, p = 0.003), despite similar postoperative clinical outcomes. Conclusion CR and PS polyethylene inserts showed no significant differences in final clinical scores or implant survivorship at a minimum follow-up of 3 years but demonstrated different patterns of postoperative dynamic alignment, suggesting that the DyAK classification may provide complementary information beyond conventional outcome measures. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Collared cemented femoral stems are associated with lower periprosthetic femoral fracture rates: A systematic review and subgroup meta-analysis.
authors: Laboudie P, Blancatto M.
abstract: Purpose Periprosthetic femoral fracture (PFF) is a severe complication after hip arthroplasty. Cemented femoral stems have been used to reduce this risk, while collars have been associated with lower fracture rates in cementless stems. However, the role of a collar in cemented femoral stems remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared postoperative PFF rates between collared and collarless cemented femoral stems. Methods Nine comparative cohorts directly comparing collared and collarless cemented stems were included in the odds ratio (OR) meta-analysis. Eligible single-arm cohorts were additionally included in pooled incidence analyses. Random-effects models were used throughout. Predefined subgroup analyses were performed according to surgical indication and stem surface finish, including a polished-stem subgroup comparing polished collared with polished collarless designs. Results Collared stems were associated with a lower postoperative PFF rate (OR, 0.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.17-0.49; p I 2 = 71%). Pooled PFF incidence was 0.51% for collared stems and 2.27% for collarless stems. This association was observed in elective arthroplasty cohorts (OR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.15-0.63) and femoral neck fracture cohorts (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.20-0.38). In the polished-stem subgroup, analysis showed a lower odds of PFF with polished collared stems (OR, 0.17; 95% CI, 0.01-2.86; p = 0.22). Pooled incidence was 0.65% for polished collared stems and 2.34% for polished collarless stems. Conclusions Collared stems were associated with lower PFF rates. This association was observed in both elective arthroplasty and femoral neck fracture cohorts. Polished collared designs also showed lower PFF rates than polished collarless designs. Substantial heterogeneity and confounding by other stem characteristics limit interpretation. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Breastfeeding and maternal bone health 10 years postpartum: findings from the ROLO longitudinal cohort study.
authors: Kennedy S, Dunlop K, Callanan S, Crowley RK, McAuliffe FM.
abstract: Brief rationale: To investigate associations between breastfeeding behaviours and maternal bone health at 10-year follow-up. Main result Breastfeeding durations were not associated with DXA measurements. Significance of the paper: These findings add to the evidence that breastfeeding is not associated with adverse long-term maternal bone health. Purpose To investigate associations between breastfeeding behaviours and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) measurements of maternal bone health at 10-year follow-up. Associations with bone turnover markers (BTMs) were examined as exploratory secondary outcomes. Methods This was an analysis of 196 women from the ROLO (Randomised cOntrol trial of a LOw glycaemic index diet in pregnancy to prevent macrosomia) longitudinal cohort study at 10-year follow-up. Data on demographics, lifestyle and breastfeeding were collected by questionnaire. DXA measurements were available for 171 participants and BTM measurements for 60. Exclusive breastfeeding duration, any breastfeeding duration and three mutually exclusive cumulative breastfeeding groups (never breastfed, breastfed for Results The mean (SD) age of participants was 42.8 (3.87) years and 97.9% were premenopausal. Ever breastfeeding rates were 70.9% (n = 139/196) and 40.3% (n = 79/196) had a cumulative breastfeeding duration of ≥12 months. Breastfeeding durations were not associated with DXA measurements at 10-year follow-up. An unadjusted difference in β-CTX-I was observed between the ≥12-month and never-breastfed groups (p = 0.038) however, given the small group size an adjusted analysis was underpowered. Conclusion These findings reassure women that breastfeeding does not have a lasting negative impact on skeletal health. The exploratory BTM finding should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Automated laboratory detection of hypercalcemia: Diagnostic yield, clinical pathway and outcomes in a real-world cohort.
authors: Roig-Marín N, López-Garrigós M, Flores E, Seguí-Ripoll JM.
abstract: Background Automated laboratory detection of hypercalcemia may facilitate the recognition of previously unrecognized primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT), but its value in routine clinical practice remains poorly defined, particularly with regard to subsequent etiological evaluation, healthcare resource utilization, and biochemical follow-up. Methods This retrospective cohort study evaluated an automated laboratory case-finding strategy for hypercalcemia across a healthcare area serving more than 230,000 inhabitants. Consecutive laboratory alerts generated between 2012 and 2020 were reviewed. After duplicate alerts were removed, 685 unique patients constituted the laboratory-detected cohort, of whom 258 underwent sufficient etiological evaluation and constituted the fully evaluated cohort. Clinical, biochemical, imaging, therapeutic, and longitudinal follow-up data were collected. Results Among the 258 fully evaluated patients, definite PHPT was diagnosed in 229 (88.8%). Eight additional patients were retrospectively considered to have probable mild PHPT with concomitant vitamin D deficiency, while other etiologies included tertiary hyperparathyroidism associated with chronic kidney disease, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, medication-related hypercalcemia, familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, sarcoidosis, and vitamin D intoxication. Patients underwent a median of seven specialist consultations. Among patients with an available date of definitive etiological diagnosis, the median interval from the initial laboratory alert to diagnosis was 432 days (IQR 94.5-1219.5). During follow-up, 219/258 patients (84.9%) had at least one documented normocalcemic measurement after biochemical confirmation of persistent hypercalcemia, and 150/258 (58.1%) fulfilled the definition of sustained normocalcemia. In Kaplan-Meier analysis, the median time to first documented normocalcemia was 595 days (95% CI 505-780). Conclusions Automated laboratory case-finding can identify patients with previously unrecognized persistent hypercalcemia and provide an entry point for subsequent etiological evaluation. PHPT was the predominant diagnosis within the fully evaluated cohort, although post-detection selection must be considered when interpreting this proportion. The prolonged diagnostic pathway and substantial healthcare use observed after the initial laboratory alert highlight the need to link automated detection strategies to structured clinical follow-up.

title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Is Associated With Lower Rates of Adhesive Capsulitis, Bursitis, Shoulder Stiffness, and Revision Shoulder Arthroscopy After Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair.
authors: Zelenski KN, Sasaki J, Bedi N, Chelton A, MacFarlane AJ, Alben MG, Fuller SI.
abstract: Background Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (RCR) success is dependent on adherence to a structured postoperative rehabilitation protocol. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with worse outcomes after certain orthopaedic surgeries, but its impact on rehabilitation after RCR remains unclear. This study compared short-term outcomes after arthroscopic RCR in patients with and without ADHD. Hypothesis Patients with ADHD will experience higher rates of postoperative complications within the first 12 months after arthroscopic RCR. Study design Retrospective cohort study. Level of evidence Level 3. Methods Using the TriNetX Research Network, arthroscopic RCR cases from 113 healthcare organizations between January 2006 and January 2026 were identified and stratified by a preoperative ADHD diagnosis. Cohorts were propensity score-matched 1:1 for age, sex, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, mood disorders, anxiety and stress-related disorders, and nicotine dependence. Outcomes at 3 months included revision shoulder arthroscopy, adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, and shoulder stiffness; 1-year outcomes also included deep infection and wound disruption. A Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction was applied to address multiple comparisons. Results After propensity score matching, 4740 patients were included per cohort. At 3 months, patients with ADHD demonstrated lower odds of bursitis (odds ratio [OR], 0.733; 95% CI, 0.592-0.908; P = 0.004; BH-adjusted P = 0.009) and shoulder stiffness (OR, 0.729; 95% CI, 0.629-0.844; P P P = 0.03; BH-adjusted P = 0.04), adhesive capsulitis (OR, 0.676; 95% CI, 0.550-0.831; P P P P P P Conclusion ADHD was associated with lower 3-month rates of bursitis and shoulder stiffness, and lower 1-year rates of adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, shoulder stiffness, and revision shoulder arthroscopy after arthroscopic RCR. Clinical relevance In contrast to previous literature, ADHD was not associated with worse outcomes after arthroscopic RCR and was associated with lower rates of stiffness-related complications. These findings suggest further research is needed to inform patient counseling and surgical decision-making.

title: Association between cemented and uncemented cups and risk of revision in patients aged 65 years or older following primary total hip arthroplasty: a study of 310,515 patients from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association.
authors: Latifi R, Kornvig S, Mohaddes M, Ali M, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, Eskelinen A, Mäkelä K, Varnum C, Overgaard S.
abstract: Background and purpose Cemented stem fixation in total hip arthroplasty (THA) reduces early femoral fracture risk in elderly patients, but the optimal method of cup fixation remains controversial. We aimed to compare cup revision risk between cemented and uncemented acetabular cups in patients aged 65 years or older undergoing primary THA. Methods This registry-based cohort study used data from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association (NARA). We included patients aged 65 years or older who underwent primary THA for primary osteoarthritis or sequelae of childhood hip disorders between 1995 and 2018. The primary outcome was all-cause cup revision, with prespecified analyses stratified by age and sex. Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, femoral head size, time period, and nation was used. Follow-up was divided into 3 periods: 0-1, 1-6, and 6-26 years. Results Among 310,515 patients, cemented cups were associated with a lower risk of all-cause cup revision during the first year (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.47, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.41-0.53) and a higher risk at 6-26 years (aHR 1.91, CI 1.72-2.13). In patients aged 80 years or older, the sex-specific adjusted hazard ratios after the first year were close to 1, with wide confidence intervals. Conclusion Cemented cups were associated with a lower risk of cup revision during the first year across all age groups and a higher risk at 6-26 years in the overall cohort. Among patients aged 80 years or older, we found no evidence of an association between fixation method and cup revision after the first year.

title: Arthroscopic Suture-Only Intra-articular Soft-Tissue Long-Head Biceps Tenodesis to the Rotator Cuff.
authors: Prasetia R, Pravitha CA, Andri F.
abstract: Pathology of the long head of the biceps tendon (LHBT) is a prevalent source of shoulder pain and is often concomitant with rotator cuff diseases. Various treatment modalities exist for addressing this condition, including surgical approaches, anatomical sites for tenodesis fixation, and types of fixation devices employed. We describe an arthroscopic suture-only intra-articular soft-tissue long-head biceps tenodesis to the rotator cuff technique for managing LHBT pathology using a loop-and-tack configuration with suture shuttling to secure the LHBT to the anterior supraspinatus without anchors. This technique maintains the physiological length-tension relation, mitigates implant-related complications, and offers a cost-effective solution for treating LHBT pathology.

title: All-Inside Stabilization of Discoid Lateral Meniscus Popliteal Hiatus-Related Instability Using Anterior Cord Release With Meniscus Retention.
authors: Toyooka S, Miyazaki H, Osaki Y, Arai N, Kawano H, Nakagawa T.
abstract: Discoid lateral meniscus is a common cause of lateral knee pain, snapping, catching, and intermittent locking. Although saucerization combined with repair has been widely used, postoperative remodeling, reduced meniscal volume, extrusion, and degenerative changes on magnetic resonance imaging have raised concerns regarding meniscal resection. A meniscus-retention concept using anterior cord release with robust suturing has been described, particularly for large displaced longitudinal tears with frank mechanical locking. In daily practice, however, many symptomatic cases present with popliteal hiatus-related posterior peripheral disruption and popliteomeniscal fascicle insufficiency, resulting in peripheral rim instability and anterior translation of the discoid meniscus during knee motion. Here, we describe a simple and physiologic, meniscus-retaining technique that combines anterior cord release to reduce anterior horn tension and facilitate peripheral reduction and targeted all-inside vertical mattress fixation around the popliteus tendon. A pragmatic avoidance criterion is emphasized for extensive, notch-locked displaced tears that likely require more robust fixation, in which inside-out repair is preferred. This technique aims to control dynamic instability while preserving native meniscal tissue and minimizing intra-articular environmental change.

title: Advanced Analytics Show Domain-Specific Performance Changes After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in National Football League Players.
authors: Hayes E, Kerhoulas Z, Matache B, Pickell M.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate return to play, performance, and assess performance changes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction using advanced statistics in National Football League players. Methods National Football League players who underwent anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) between 2017 and 2024 were identified using publicly available databases and injury reports. Demographic and outcome data for 1 year preinjury to 2 years postinjury were obtained. Return to play was defined as being listed as active for a regular season game after injury. Return to performance was defined as returning to greater than 90% of preinjury performance. Our primary performance outcome was Sports Information Solutions points above replacement (PAR). Binary logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with return to play and return to performance. Preinjury and postinjury performance data at the first and second postinjury year were compared with paired t -tests. Results We included 237 players in return-to-play and 173 players in return-to-performance analyses. Of players, 75.5% returned to play; players with more preinjury games played, more index games played, starters, and players with greater preinjury PAR were more likely to return to play ( P = .03, P P P P = .004, P P = .002, P = .004), driven at both time points by significantly decreased rushing ( P = .02, P = .001) and pass coverage ( P = .003, P = .03) PAR. Conclusions After anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, National Football League players with more preinjury games played and higher preinjury performance are more likely to return to play; younger players with lower preinjury performance are more likely to return to performance; and there is a significant decrease in overall performance 1 and 2 years after injury, driven by decreased rushing and pass coverage performance. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective case series.

title: Access to Trauma Care for Patients With Proximal Femur Fractures in Resource-Limited Settings: A Prospective Cohort Study in Rural Tanzania.
authors: Eleveld AJ, Mtui GS, Hendriks TCC, Bellet FD, Botman M, Bloemers FW, van Embden D.
abstract: Background The standard of care for proximal femur fractures is internal fixation or arthroplasty within 48 hours after injury. In resource-limited settings, access to surgical services is limited. The aim of this study was to assess access to care for patients with proximal femur fractures in Tanzania by applying the Three Delays framework. Methods A prospective cohort study was conducted in a rural regional referral hospital in Tanzania. All patients with a proximal femur fractures admitted between August 2019 and August 2020 were included. Data were collected on patient demographics, pre- and in-hospital care, timelines and affordability. According to the Three Delays framework, delays and reasons for delays in seeking (first delay), reaching (second delay) and receiving care (third delay) were explored using a structured survey. Results Forty-seven patients were included. Twenty-four patients (51%) delayed in seeking care at a health care facility within 24 hours after injury with a median delay of 13 days (IQR 4-26 days). Ten patients (21%) were delayed in reaching a healthcare facility within 24 hours. Thirteen patients (28%) experienced a delay in receiving initial surgical care. None of the patients were treated according to the international standard. Thirty-eight patients experienced catastrophic expenditure as a result of their hospital admission. Conclusion The majority of patients with a proximal femur fracture experienced a considerable delay in access to care and none of the patients were treated according to international standards. This should be improved by identifying ways to increase the availability of affordable surgical treatment options.

title: A Decade in Periprosthetic Joint Infection Care: Growing Referrals and High Resource Demands at a High-Volume Center.
authors: Rainey JP, Blackburn BE, Noyd RC, Hammond J, Certain LK, Archibeck MJ, Anderson LA, Peters CL, Gililland JM, Pelt CE.
abstract: Background The management of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) requires a multidisciplinary approach that is not feasible in all healthcare settings. This study characterized the evolving burden of PJI referrals at an academic referral center over the past decade. Methods A retrospective review was conducted of all referred patients who underwent treatment for hip or knee PJI at a single referral center between 2014 and 2024. Demographic data, initial operative time, hospital length of stay (LOS), and number and duration of subsequent surgeries were recorded. Results In total, 523 referred patients were treated for PJI. The mean initial LOS was 7.0 days (standard deviation [SD] 5.7) and the mean operative time was 169.5 min (SD 75.9). Overall, 36% underwent irrigation and debridement with modular component exchange, single stage revision, or a spacer alone. Of the 335 who had at least 1 subsequent surgery, under half (N = 146, 43.5%), received stage two alone. On average, patients underwent 1.8 subsequent surgeries (SD 1.4), ranging from 1 to 14. The cumulative mean operative time for these subsequent surgeries was 306.4 min (SD 253.3). The number of PJIs nearly doubled from 2014-2017 (N = 112) to 2021-2024 (N = 221). There were no significant changes in LOS, number of subsequent surgeries, or cumulative operative time for reoperations during these intervals. Conclusions The volume of referred PJIs has increased substantially over the past decade at our referral center, underscoring the growing demand for PJI care and profound resource burden necessary to care for these patients.

title: Transfemoral bone-anchored limbs alter joint-load-line offset during walking.
authors: Gaffney BMM, Milius DW, Melton DH, Christiansen CL, Stoneback JW.
abstract: Individuals with transfemoral amputation are at a heightened risk of musculoskeletal overuse injuries and reduced stability, largely due to altered joint biomechanics. The position of the ground reaction force (GRF) relative to hip and knee joints directly influences both joint biomechanics and dynamic stability and is influenced both by both movement patterns and prosthetic alignment. However, it is unknown if it is influenced by prosthetic suspension type. Our objective was to determine how the position of the GRF relative to hip and knee joint centers during walking differs between individuals with transfemoral amputation using either a socket prosthesis or bone-anchored limb (BAL). Motion capture data was collected from a convenience sample of 17 participants with unilateral transfemoral amputation during overground walking at two timepoints: before and 12-months following BAL implantation. The distances between the GRF line of action and the hip and knee joints in the sagittal and frontal planes were calculated and compared across timepoints (α = 0.05). The distance between the GRF and hip joint center was less medial (p < 0.001) on the amputated limb and more lateral (p < 0.001) on the intact limb during stance period when using a BAL compared to a socket prosthesis. Closer positioning of the GRF relative to the hip joint may reduce frontal plane compensatory strategies required for hip stabilization, potentially reflecting a biomechanical stable gait pattern when using a BAL.

title: TikTok Videos on the Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Have Low Educational Quality and Reliability.
authors: Conteduca J, Brindisino F, Casto A, Valentino L, Scrimitore A, Bernetti A, Rollo G.
abstract: Purpose To assess the quality, reliability, and engagement of TikTok videos addressing the material about medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL). Methods Between November 2 and 24, 2024, a comprehensive search of the TikTok platform was performed using both keyword-based search ("MPFL," "medial patellofemoral ligament") and hashtag-based search (#MPFL) to maximize content capture. Videos were included if they addressed the MPFL with respect to anatomy, injury mechanism, clinical evaluation, surgical management, or rehabilitation. Each video was independently assessed using the DISCERN instrument, Journal of the American Medical Association benchmark criteria, Global Quality Scale, and Patient Education and Decision Support Score. Video characteristics, including duration, number of views, likes, shares, and shares, were recorded, and correlations between engagement metrics and quality scores were analyzed. Results Of 100 videos analyzed, 9% were posted by medical doctors, 3% by physiotherapists, and 88% by private users. Most videos focused on personal experience, representing 74% of the information type and 80% of the content type. The mean scores of DISCERN, Journal of the American Medical Association , Global Quality Scale, and Patient Education and Decision Support Score were 16.25 ± 4.07, 0.1 ± 0.4, 1.1 ± 0.5, and 0.6 ± 1.88, respectively. Videos uploaded by medical professionals achieved significantly higher quality scores across all metrics ( P P = .173). Engagement metrics (views, likes, shares) showed moderate positive correlations with DISCERN ( r = 0.31) and Patient Education and Decision Support Score ( r = 0.39), whereas video duration showed no correlation with any quality index. Conclusions TikTok videos related to the MPFL show low educational quality and limited reliability, with the most content produced by nonmedical users. Videos uploaded by health care professionals achieved significantly higher quality scores across all evaluated assessment tools. Clinical relevance Patients with MPFL pathology frequently seek medical information on social media platforms. Awareness of the limited educational quality and reliability of MPFL-related content on TikTok may help clinicians better counsel patients regarding online health information.

title: The Chimeric Osteomyocutaneous Anterolateral Thigh Flap: A Novel Method for Lower Extremity Long Bone Reconstruction.
authors: LoGiudice J, Mather T, Hsieh M, Law B, Neilson J, Wooldridge A, Schmeling G.

title: Surgical treatment of thoracic vertebral chondrosarcoma with total en bloc spondylectomy: a case report.
authors: Sakti YM, Lanodiyu ZA, Prasetyo TE, Nurfadhilah MI, Sari DAP, Ridha M, Santiko W, Darutama AA, Anggunio V, Pratama IA, Aji AS, Calisto KE, Adamina ZN, Rukmoyo T.
abstract: Spinal chondrosarcoma is a rare malignant cartilage-forming tumor that is largely resistant to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, making complete surgical resection the cornerstone of treatment. We report a 60-year-old man with recurrent thoracic chondrosarcoma involving the T4-T6 vertebrae following previous intralesional decompression, spinal stabilization, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Revision surgery was performed through a posterior approach with implant removal, wide tumor excision, total en bloc spondylectomy (TES), spinal reconstruction using an expandable cage, posterior instrumentation, and spinal fusion. Histopathological examination confirmed recurrent grade II conventional chondrosarcoma. The patient remained neurologically stable after surgery without major perioperative complications. The present case indicates the limitations of intralesional surgery and adjuvant therapy in conventional chondrosarcoma and supports TES as the treatment for complete tumor excision and optimal local control, despite its technical difficulty.

title: Sternal "Medusa's head" sign.
authors: Ogul H.

title: Sleep disorders in patients with systemic sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Bayala YLT, Ayouba Tinni I, Sougué C, Kaboré F, Zabsonré-Tiendrebeogo WJS, Ouédraogo DD.
abstract: Background Systemic sclerosis is a rare autoimmune disease associated with substantial morbidity and reduced quality of life. Sleep disturbance has been reported with variable frequency in patients with systemic sclerosis, though its prevalence remains incompletely characterised. Objective This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of sleep disorders in patients with systemic sclerosis. Methods Six databases were searched up to 15th February 2026 without language restriction. Studies reporting sleep outcomes in adults with systemic sclerosis were eligible. Prevalence estimates were pooled using a logit transformation with a random-effects model and Hartung-Knapp correction. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Publication bias was evaluated with Egger's test and the trim-and-fill method. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251152354). Results Twenty-three studies totalling 1487 patients were included across all analyses. Eleven studies (820 patients) contributed to the primary meta-analysis of poor sleep quality assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. The pooled prevalence of poor sleep quality was 76.49% (95% CI 66.62 to 84.13%), with moderate to substantial heterogeneity (I 2 =70.1%) and a 95% prediction interval of 49.66 to 91.47%, indicating that the true prevalence may range from approximately half to nearly all patients across different SSc populations. Five studies (346 patients) contributed to the obstructive sleep apnea meta-analysis, yielding a pooled prevalence of 40.30% (95% CI 25.56 to 57.04%, I 2 =71.8%) with a 95% prediction interval of 13.95 to 73.75%. Five additional studies were included in a qualitative synthesis only, and three randomised controlled trials addressed sleep interventions. Egger's test identified possible funnel plot asymmetry. After trim-and-fill adjustment, four studies were imputed and the corrected estimate was 69.62% (95% CI 57.33 to 79.63%), somewhat lower than the primary estimate, suggesting that the primary estimate may be modestly influenced by publication bias. The certainty of evidence was rated as low according to GRADE. Conclusion Available evidence suggests that sleep disorders may affect approximately three quarters of patients with systemic sclerosis when assessed by the PSQI, and obstructive sleep apnea may affect more than one third when evaluated by objective tools. These estimates carry low GRADE certainty and wide prediction intervals, and should not be interpreted as definitive prevalence figures. Larger prospective studies and well-powered randomised trials are needed to establish more precise estimates and to evaluate targeted sleep interventions in this population.

title: Simultaneous Oblique Lateral Interbody Fusion (OLIF) and posterior transpedicular screw fixation in treatment of lumbar pyogenic spondylodiscitis.
authors: Omran K, Abdel-Fattah AS, Hassan MY.
abstract: Background Anterior retroperitoneal spine surgery is advocated for the management of lumbar pyogenic spondylodiscitis (LPS) to target the anterior spondylodiscal pathology. The OLIF corridor provides access to the anterior infective lumbar lesion directly through the pre-psoas space with minimal complications and morbidity, successful debridement, and fusion rate, while respecting surgeon preference, accounting for equipment availability, and the learning curve. Purpose The aim of this study was to analyze the clinical, radiological, and functional outcomes after combined OLIF and posterior transpedicular screw fixation in the treatment of LPS. Study design This was a retrospective single-center clinical study. Methods Twenty-seven patients with complicated LPS were treated surgically by combined OLIF and posterior percutaneous transpedicular screw fixation from 2018 to 2021. Preoperatively and postoperatively, all patients were examined clinically for back or leg pain by applying the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), sensory or motor deficit, Arabic-validated Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and modified Prolo scores; radiologically (plain X-ray, multidetector computerized tomography (MDCT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)). Perioperative data and complications were recorded. All patients were regularly followed for 26 months regarding clinical outcomes, functional status, and radiological measures. Results Significant postoperative improvement in VAS for back and leg pain, ODI, and modified Prolo scores was reported, with statistically significant differences between preoperative, during, and at the final follow-up. The mean fusion time was 10.52 ± 1.24 months. Twenty-five patients (92.6%) showed definitive fusion (grade 5) according to Lee and Suh's criteria. Conclusion This combined surgery is an effective method for treating LPS with adequate canal decompression, radiological correction, and functional recovery.

title: Risk factors of high osteoporosis risk in subjects over 40 years in Mongolia.
authors: Jaalkhorol M, Ikeda Y, Narangerel E, Dashtseren A, Khulgar T, Munkhsonguuli U, Iimaa T, Sampil T, Enkhbayar N, Bruyere O.
abstract: In Mongolia, osteoporosis screening is difficult because advanced scans are scarce. In 356 adults aged 40 years or older, stronger handgrip strength was associated with a lower OSTA-defined osteoporosis risk category in both men and women, whereas lifestyle factors were not. Adding handgrip testing could improve low-cost screening strategies. Background Osteoporosis is a growing public health concern in Mongolia, where access to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is limited. The Osteoporosis Self-Assessment Test (OSTA) provides a simple, low-cost alternative for identifying individuals at risk. This study aimed to examine factors associated with OSTA-defined osteoporosis risk categories among adults aged 40 years and older in Mongolia. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 356 adults (200 men, 156 women) recruited from two urban health units. Sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, medical history, and handgrip strength were assessed through structured interviews and standardized measurements. OSTA scores were categorized into low, moderate, and high risk based on established sex-specific thresholds. Group differences in categorical variables were evaluated using chi-square tests. Logistic regression models were performed separately for men and women to identify factors independently associated with the combined moderate/high OSTA risk category. Results Age, sex, educational level, comorbidities, and BMI were significantly associated with OSTA categories. Higher dominant handgrip strength was associated with lower odds of the combined moderate/high OSTA risk category in both men (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.06-0.58) and women (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.02-0.51). In contrast, lifestyle factors such as smoking, alcohol consumption, diet, and sedentary time were not independently associated with OSTA scores. Conclusion Several demographic and clinical factors were associated with OSTA risk categories in this low-resource setting. The strong association with handgrip strength suggests potential added value in integrating functional assessments into screening strategies. These findings support the development of scalable, low-cost approaches for osteoporosis risk stratification in Mongolia.

title: Revisiting menopausal hormone therapy for bone health: evidence, controversies, and clinical positioning in India in 2026.
authors: Vaghasia N, Nagendra L, Kapoor N, Maldar A, Baro A, Bhandarkar A, Joshi A, Ghosh A, Monteiro AS, Joseph A, Mishra I, Agarwal K, Cherian KE, Tandon N, Kaur P, John R, Shetty S, Das S, Bhadada S, Kalra S, Bhattacharya S, Patra S, Sidana S, Mondal S, Paul TV, Sriram U, Mithal A.
abstract: Menopause is characterized by the rapid decline of estrogen exposure, resulting in accelerated bone loss superimposed on the gradual age-related decline in bone mass. This process is particularly relevant in India, where women experience menopause earlier than Western populations, thereby increasing lifetime fracture risk. Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) has been evaluated extensively over the years for skeletal health, with consistent evidence demonstrating preservation of bone mineral density and reduction in vertebral and hip fractures, especially when initiated early after menopause. Although multiple concerns arose following the Women's Health Initiative in terms of cardiovascular safety and breast cancer risk, leading to a decline in MHT use, subsequent analyses have supported a more favorable benefit-risk profile in appropriately selected younger postmenopausal women. Current evidence suggests that individualized MHT can also improve skeletal outcomes while benefiting menopausal symptoms and overall quality of life. This review revisits the evolving role of MHT in bone health in the Indian context.

title: Revision surgery for osteochondral lesions of the talus: Are there predictive factors for successful surgery?
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
authors: Biehl C, El Khassawna T, Fritzsche C, Walter N, Biehl L, Heiss C, Rupp M.
abstract: Purpose Osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT) are common injuries of the ankle associated with persistent pain and functional impairment. Revision procedures are frequent. Currently, objective criteria to guide revision decision-making remain limited. This retrospective study is designed to identify factors associated with patient-reported outcome after surgery pathways and to enhance selection of patients who may benefit from revision surgery in OLT. Methods Between 2015 and 2018, 64 patients underwent surgical treatment for OLT (97 procedures in total). A symptomatic subgroup of 21 patients required additional procedures (33 revision operations). Outcomes at a mean follow-up of 3 years were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, and the Foot and Ankle Outcome Score (FAOS). Primary outcome was a patient-level PROM-based classification (Success/ Partial relief/No relief) at follow-up. Analyses were performed per patient; procedure counts were reported descriptively. Results Of 64 patients, 43 (67%) achieved a successful outcome after a single procedure, whereas 21 (33%) required multiple procedures. In the multiple-surgery group, 9/21 (43%) were classified as Success at follow-up. PROM categories in follow up correlated significantly with AOFAS, VAS, and FAOS. A longer interval (> 24 months) between procedures might be associated with a higher likelihood of a habituation effect at follow-up. Conclusion PROM-based classification provides a patient-centered assessment of outcome after revision pathways for OLT. The FAOS score subdomains proved particularly valuable in identifying specific issues that could justify a revision. The waiting time between surgeries appears relevant and should be considered when planning revision surgery. Our data suggests that a longer interval between surgeries (exceeding 24 months) might be associated with habituation effects and adaptation processes, leading to a reduction in periarticular swelling and the continuation of physiotherapy. Despite moderate success rates, the treatment of OLT remains challenging, and preoperative factors such as age and activity level should be considered when evaluating the chances of success.

title: Removal of a large maxillary sinus mucocele via Le Fort I osteotomy during orthognathic surgery: a case report.
authors: Boylu D, Boylu ÖF.
abstract: Maxillary sinus mucoceles are uncommon expansile lesions resulting from impaired sinus drainage and mucus accumulation. We report a 19-year-old male with a large left maxillary sinus mucocele identified during planning for bimaxillary orthognathic surgery. Preoperative cone-beam computed tomography showed complete sinus occupation with extension into the nasal cavity and toward the nasopharynx. During the independently planned Le Fort I osteotomy, maxillary down-fracture provided direct access, allowing intact removal of the well-encapsulated lesion. Histopathological examination confirmed a mucocele. At 2-month follow-up, the patient had no nasal symptoms, and postoperative imaging demonstrated marked sinus re-aeration without radiographic evidence of residual or recurrent disease. When independently indicated, Le Fort I osteotomy may provide effective access for simultaneous management of selected extensive maxillary sinus mucoceles.

title: Predicting Return to Play After Achilles Tendon Injury in National Football League Players Using Machine Learning.
authors: Chen Z, Wang NM, Lei Z, Thomas GM, Pedowitz D, Parekh SG.
abstract: BackgroundNational Football League (NFL) players frequently experience Achilles tendon (AT) injuries. However, there is mixed evidence regarding factors influencing return to play (RTP) after AT injury. The objective of this study is to develop machine learning models to predict NFL players' likelihood of RTP within 1 year of an AT tear. Hypothesis Machine learning models can predict 1-year RTP status in NFL players following AT tear. Study design Retrospective Cohort.MethodsA retrospective review was conducted to identify NFL players who sustained unilateral AT injuries from 2004 to 2024. Player demographics and performance data were recorded. Return to play was defined as generating playing statistics. Five machine learning models were developed: logistic regression, random forest classifier, XGBoost, Gaussian naive Bayes, and K-nearest neighbors. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 were used to assess model performance.ResultsOne hundred seventy-six NFL players were identified with an AT injury. One hundred eight players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 63 players did not (class 0). In the full cohort, injury etiology was the most influential feature associated with 1-year RTP, followed by pre-injury performance. Among the 99 players with a confirmed AT tear, 48 players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 51 players did not (class 0). Within the confirmed-tear cohort, draft round and games started were the leading predictors of 1-year RTP, which was best predicted by random forest with a mean accuracy of 0.69, precision of 0.68, recall of 0.70, and an F1-score of 0.69 for class 0.ConclusionMachine learning models that combine clinical and performance metrics of NFL athletes demonstrated potential for predicting 1-year RTP after AT injury and identifying factors associated with RTP. Clinical relevance Machine learning could be integrated into clinical decision-making and prognosis to refine rehabilitation approaches in NFL players. Level of evidence Level 3.

title: Oxidative stress-driven cellular heterogeneity in Knee Osteoarthritis: scRNA-seq pinpoints SPP1 and CYBA for diagnostic development.
authors: Liu Y, Chi Y, Yin J, Yao J.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and subchondral bone remodeling. Oxidative stress plays a critical role in KOA pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with machine learning to uncover potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for KOA. ScRNA-seq data from KOA cartilage tissues were obtained from the GEO database to characterize cellular heterogeneity and identify disease-associated chondrocyte subsets. CellChat was used to analyze intercellular communication, and Monocle2 was applied to reconstruct cell differentiation trajectories. Oxidative stress activity at the single-cell level was evaluated using AUCell, while high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) was performed to identify oxidative stress-related gene modules. Candidate genes were screened using Venn analysis and further refined by LASSO regression, SVM-RFE, and XGBoost combined with SHAP analysis. Diagnostic performance was assessed, and biological relevance was explored through immune infiltration and pathway analyses. Experimental validation was conducted using qRT-PCR and western blot assays in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. InfC and ProFC were detected specifically in OA cartilage and exhibited high oxidative stress activity. InfC was enriched in inflammatory and immune-related pathways, whereas ProFC was associated with cell cycle regulation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Integrated hdWGCNA and machine-learning analyses consistently identified CYBA and SPP1 as candidate genes. The two-gene model achieved bootstrap-corrected AUCs of 0.937 and 0.825 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. qRT-PCR and western blot analyses further showed increased CYBA and SPP1 expression in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. Conclusion InfC and ProFC may represent OA-associated chondrocyte states characterized by enhanced oxidative stress, while CYBA and SPP1 may serve as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Given the small cohort sizes and preliminary in vitro validation, these findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts and functional studies.

title: OsteoNet-X: A deep residual learning framework for automated osteoporosis detection from knee X-ray images.
authors: Sangula SK, Ibrahim SPS.
abstract: Osteoporosis is a progressive skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mineral density and increased susceptibility to fractures, making early diagnosis essential for effective clinical intervention and long-term patient management. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have demonstrated significant potential for automated bone disease assessment using medical imaging modalities. In this study, a unified deep learning framework, termed OsteoNet-X, is proposed for automated osteoporosis detection and multi-class bone health classification using knee X-ray images. Unlike conventional image classification approaches, OsteoNet-X integrates YOLO-based Region of Interest (ROI) localization, DenseNet-based feature extraction, Feature-Aware Learning (FAL) optimization, and Grad-CAM-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enhance both classification performance and model interpretability. The ROI extraction stage automatically identifies anatomically relevant knee joint regions, reducing background interference and enabling more discriminative feature learning. Subsequently, DenseNet facilitates efficient feature propagation and hierarchical representation learning for distinguishing normal, osteopenia, and osteoporosis conditions. The incorporation of XAI further provides visual explanations of model decisions by highlighting clinically relevant regions within the knee joint. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that OsteoNet-X achieves a classification accuracy of 97.08%, a macro F1-score of 96.61%, and a weighted F1-score of 97.11%.

title: Not the Last Word: Are Orthopaedic Surgeons Working Class?
authors: Bernstein J.

title: Minimally Invasive Surgery for Adult Scoliosis: Recent Updates and Advancements.
authors: Khan F, Hoofnagle MD, Mummaneni PV, Chan AK, Chou D.
abstract: Purpose of review Circumferential minimally invasive surgery (cMIS) for adult scoliosis has evolved over the past five years. Here, we review how advances in patient selection, operative technique, and technology have transformed the capabilities of cMIS for deformity. Recent findings Early cMIS was constrained by a "corrective ceiling" that limited its use to flexible deformities. Patient selection has since grown more nuanced, incorporating surgical complexity, patient-specific factors, and the deformity itself rather than radiographic thresholds alone. Technique has changed in parallel, as correction is now distributed across multiple interbody levels with segmental release, performed through both anterior and lateral techniques. Workflow and technology have adapted as well: single-position prone transpsoas and lateral prepsoas approaches may reduce intraoperative repositioning, staging extends treatment to patients with greater deformity or frailty, and robotics and patient-specific implants improve the precision of planning and execution. These advances have been accompanied by data demonstrating improved patient-reported outcomes and spinopelvic alignment at lower morbidity in appropriately selected patients. With the safety and efficacy of cMIS established, the field continues to push its boundaries toward more challenging pathology, as illustrated by contemporary cases of severe multiplanar deformity and complex revision. The boundaries of cMIS have expanded considerably beyond the flexible, moderate deformities for which these techniques were initially developed. Careful patient selection remains essential, as not all deformities are amenable to minimally invasive correction. Nevertheless, advances in surgical technique, operative workflow, and patient-specific planning have enabled increasingly severe and complex deformities to be addressed while preserving the fundamental advantages of minimally invasive surgery.

title: Mesenchymal progenitor cell Zeb1 regulates bone homeostasis and PTH-dependent anabolic responses.
authors: Liu B, Yang J, Chen Z, Liu Y, Niu S, Higashi Y, Takagi T, Tang Y, Weiss SJ, Chen G, Zhu L.
abstract: The regulation of postnatal bone homeostasis by specific transcriptional programs in skeletal mesenchymal progenitor cells remains incompletely understood. While epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) transcription factors are critical drivers of cellular plasticity, their physiological roles in bone-forming lineages are largely unknown. Here, we identify the EMT transcription factor Zeb1 as a central regulator of osteogenic differentiation in vitro and in vivo. Conditional knockout of Zeb1 in bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) using Prrx1-Cre impairs bone formation, giving rise to a significant osteopenic phenotype. At the cellular level, Zeb1-deficient BMSCs display impaired osteogenic differentiation and self-renewal. Transcriptional profiling further defined a role for Zeb1 in regulating the expression of the parathyroid hormone type 1 receptor (PTH1R), a key mediator of skeletal anabolism. Consequently, Zeb1 loss attenuated PTH1R levels and blunted downstream PTH signaling, rendering mice refractory to the bone-anabolic effects of intermittent PTH treatment. Taken together, these studies identify Zeb1 as a key transcriptional regulator governing osteoblastogenesis, bridging skeletal mesenchymal progenitor cell fate regulation with PTH-mediated anabolic control of bone mass.

title: Introducing the rodent open science skeletal archive.
authors: Maye P, Kelleher B, Shostak W, Mark A, Sinder B, Che X, Choi JY, Huang CH, Salisbury J, Shin DG, Andersen TL, Rowe DW.
abstract: Musculoskeletal diseases affect more than half of the adult population, yet the mechanisms underlying skeletal pathology remain incompletely understood. Rodent animal models have been central to advancing this knowledge, generating decades of skeletal phenotyping data through well-established quantitative methods. Despite this, no dedicated repository exists to archive and share this data, leaving the vast majority of rodent skeletal phenotyping results accessible only through individual publications and unavailable for broader integration and reuse. Here we introduce the Rodent Open Science Skeletal Archive (ROSSA; rossa.uchc.edu), an NIH-funded, open-access web-based repository designed to store and share rodent skeletal phenotyping data. We describe the architecture of ROSSA and report on three core deliverables completed in this first phase of development: a data submission system, a core facility registry, and the underlying database infrastructure. The data submission system supports a wide range of experimental paradigms, including genetically modified animal models, pharmacological interventions, and gonadectomy procedures, and accepts quantitative phenotyping data generated by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), microcomputed tomography (μCT), bone histomorphometry, mechanical strength testing, and serum, plasma, and urine biomarker assays. Submitted data are preserved in original form to ensure authenticity and parsed into a relational database to support flexible search functionality and programmatic access. The core facility registry catalogs institutional resources available to the skeletal research community. Together, these components establish ROSSA as a foundational resource for the skeletal biology community and lay the groundwork for future cross-study data integration and meta-analysis.

title: Health-Related Performance Decrements Resulted in Substantial Financial Loss for Team USA Athletes at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.
authors: Oeding JF, Anderson T, Triplett AN, Donaldson A, Finnoff JT, Vincent HK, Post EG.
abstract: Purpose To estimate the financial impact of injury and illness among Team USA athletes who participated in the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a feasible illness prevention program. Methods All Team USA athlete-events at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games were analyzed. Precompetition betting markets were used to derive the expected performance. Counterfactual finish distributions were generated using a Markov ranking model. Injury- and illness-associated performance decrements were estimated relative to expected medal placement outcomes and translated into expected financial losses across 3 domains: Operation Gold performance incentives, athlete stipends, and estimated commercial value. Losses were summarized at the athlete-event, athlete, and Team USA levels. A cohort Markov cost-effectiveness model evaluated a potential illness prevention program using probabilistic sensitivity analysis. Results Across 808 Team USA athlete-events, 186 injuries and 108 illnesses were recorded. Total injury- and illness-attributable financial losses were estimated at $1,014,210 under conservative commercial value assumptions ( B = $10,000), including $462,409 attributable to injuries and $551,802 attributable to illnesses. Median athlete-event-level financial loss was $3000 (75th percentile: $5094; 90th percentile: $7758), whereas median athlete-level loss was $4710 (90th percentile: $15,617; maximum: $62,915), indicating substantial right skewness and concentration of losses. Illness events were associated with higher mean financial losses per event than injuries ($5109 vs $2486). An illness prevention program costing $200 per athlete and reducing illness risk by 40% was cost-saving, averting $220,721 in expected losses at a total cost of $117,000, yielding net savings of $103,721, and remaining cost-saving in 95.2% of probabilistic simulations. Conclusions Injury and illness at the Olympic Games are associated with substantial and highly concentrated financial losses, with illnesses accounting for a disproportionate share of the total impact on Team USA athletes. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective cohort study with counterfactual performance modeling.

title: Getting REAL balance: a simple and reproducible method for imageless robotic TKA.
authors: Rossi SMP, Sangaletti R, Muci C, Capitani P, Benazzo F, Andriollo L.
abstract: Background In imageless robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA), intraoperative assessment of ligament balance may be influenced by asymmetric cartilage wear, potentially misrepresenting true soft-tissue behavior. Functional alignment (FA) aims to restore constitutional alignment while respecting the native ligament envelope. Using the unworn compartment as the primary reference for intraoperative balancing may reduce the effect of asymmetric wear and improve mediolateral symmetry. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on 180 knees (176 patients) undergoing femur-first imageless RA-TKA with a functional alignment strategy at a single-volume center. All procedures were performed using the ROSA Knee System with a medial congruent implant. Intraoperative balancing prioritized the unworn or less affected compartment, targeting a 19-mm implant space with near-symmetric medial-lateral laxity in extension and flexion. Medial and lateral laxities were recorded robotically before implantation and after final component placement and classified using the Robotic Evaluation of Articular Laxity (REAL). Results Preoperatively, lateral laxity exceeded medial laxity in both extension and flexion. Following implantation, mediolateral symmetry was restored with a significant reduction in medial-lateral laxity differences (p Conclusions In femur-first imageless RA-TKA performed according to functional alignment principles, unworn-compartment-based balancing enables reliable restoration of mediolateral ligament symmetry with balanced REAL phenotypes and a limited need for soft-tissue releases, representing a refinement of robotic ligament assessment in knees with asymmetric osteoarthritis during contemporary robotic surgery.

title: Externally validated MRI radiomics machine learning models for differentiating between myxoid liposarcoma and myxoma.
authors: Chen YH, Bazanjani S, Wang Z, Bauer F, Sharp A, Hung YP, Ossiani T, Saraee M, Smith G, Viator M, Gonzalez M, Chen A, Kerimo E, Palmer W, Pianykh O, Lozano-Calderón SA.
abstract: Objective To develop and externally validate a radiomics-based machine learning model for differentiating myxoid liposarcoma (MLS) from myxoma on MRI and compare its diagnostic performance with that of experienced musculoskeletal radiologists. Methods In this retrospective study, T1-weighted and fluid-sensitive MRI sequences from 109 patients with histologically confirmed MLS or myxoma were used to train support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB) classifiers. Models were evaluated in an independent external cohort of 32 patients from a second institution using different scanner hardware and protocols. Diagnostic performance was compared with that of two fellowship-trained senior musculoskeletal radiologists. Secondary analysis assessed MLS grading. Results The T1-weighted SVM achieved the strongest external binary performance (accuracy, 0.84; AUC, 0.91), outperforming RF and XGB (p = 0.005 and p 0.05), although the study was not powered to establish equivalence. Fluid-sensitive SVM performance was limited (accuracy, 0.56; AUC, 0.60), indicating sequence-dependent generalizability. Models and radiologists demonstrated limited MLS grading accuracy, reflecting tumor heterogeneity. Conclusion Externally validated radiomics-based machine learning supported noninvasive differentiation of MLS from myxoma primarily on T1-weighted MRI. T1-weighted SVM performance was not significantly different from that of experienced radiologists, although equivalence was not established, whereas fluid-sensitive performance was substantially weaker. T1-weighted quantitative imaging biomarkers may complement soft tissue tumor characterization, but extrapolation to fluid-sensitive sequences requires caution.

title: Does greater orthoplastic integration reduce deep infection after open tibial fracture? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Choi B, Ghaie S, Shah A, Boriani F.
abstract: Objective Combined orthoplastic management of open tibial fractures is widely recommended, but existing evidence has not quantified whether the degree of care-pathway integration, beyond a binary orthoplastic-versus-orthopaedic distinction, is associated with a graded difference in outcome. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified deep infection and secondary outcome rates across four care-pathway models of increasing team continuity. Methods MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and grey literature were searched in collaboration with a specialist medical librarian. Studies were classified into four care-pathway groups: Group 1, single-setting simultaneous fixation and soft tissue coverage; Group 2, staged care with continuous orthoplastic team involvement; Group 3, discontinuous or delayed plastic surgical involvement; Group 4, purely orthopaedic management. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled deep infection, limb salvage, reoperation, and non-union rates per group. Comparative meta-analyses used genuine within-study comparator arms. Confounding was assessed via meta-regression and subgroup analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence was rated using GRADE. Results Fifty-eight studies (81 classified arms) were included. Pooled deep infection rates rose progressively with decreasing care-pathway integration: 8% (95% CI 5-12%) in Group 1, 16% (9-24%) in Group 2, 28% (11-49%) in Group 3, and 37% (25-50%) in Group 4. A similar gradient was observed for non-union (4-26% across groups). Limb salvage was near-universal (94-99%) and did not discriminate between pathways. Leave-one-out and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness for Groups 1, 2, and 4; Group 3's estimate was substantially influenced by a single Critical-risk-of-bias study, with deep infection rates attenuating from 28% to 23% on exclusion. No significant publication bias was detected. Certainty of evidence, per GRADE, was Very Low for majority of the pooled estimates, reflecting serious risk of bias and inconsistency, and Low where heterogeneity was minimal. Conclusion Progressive care-pathway integration is associated with a consistent, graded reduction in deep infection and non-union risk following open tibial fracture, independent of injury mechanism. These findings support continued investment in combined orthoplastic care, including partial integration models where single-setting surgery is not achievable.

title: Comparison of internal fixation outcomes in young femoral neck fractures: three cannulated compression screws versus the femoral neck system.
authors: Xiao B, Lu M, Chen X, Qiu D, He Y, Li X.
abstract: Background Femoral neck fractures in young patients typically result from traumatic injury, present significant treatment challenges, and are associated with a high risk of complications. The cannulated compression screw (CCS) is a common fixation device, whereas the femoral neck system (FNS) is a newer fixation device. Objective To compare the clinical efficacy of the FNS and CCS in the treatment of femoral neck fractures in young patients. Methods Between September 2021 and September 2023, 82 patients with femoral neck fracture aged 18-60 years were admitted to our hospital. According to the different fixation methods, the patients were divided into the FNS (38 cases) and CCS (44 cases) groups. The perioperative indicators, complications and follow-up function scores were compared between the two groups, and the follow-up time was ≥ 12 months. Results The FNS group had shorter operation time (53.71 ± 11.20 vs. 64.61 ± 11.27 min, p p p p p = 0.026) and a lower incidence of lateral thigh irritation (7.89% vs. 29.55%, p = 0.014), along with less severe femoral neck shortening (4.68 ± 2.04 vs. 7.14 ± 2.27 mm, p p p p p Conclusion Compared to CCS, FNS has better intraoperative efficiency, a lower internal fixation failure rate, and less severe femoral neck shortening in the treatment of femoral neck fractures in young adults. However, given the retrospective design, relatively small sample size, limited follow-up time, and differential follow-up duration between the groups, these conclusions should be interpreted with caution.

title: Axial spondyloarthropathy with peripheral joint involvement mimicking gout on ultrasound: A case of double contour sign pitfall.
authors: Lee YE, Park EH.
abstract: Axial spondyloarthropathy (axSpA) may present with peripheral joint involvement, which makes the diagnosis more challenging when axial symptoms are unrecognized. In this report, a 66-year-old man presented with chronic left knee pain and swelling as the initially recognized musculoskeletal manifestation of axSpA. A double contour sign (DCS)-like appearance near the fibular head and a DCS at the first metatarsophalangeal joint initially suggested gout. Subsequent evaluations, including dual-energy CT, sacroiliac joint CT and MRI, and HLA-B27 testing, led to a diagnosis of axSpA with peripheral joint involvement. This case highlights diagnostic pitfalls in musculoskeletal ultrasound, particularly the gout-specific DCS. It also emphasizes the importance of correlating imaging findings with clinical symptoms and pain distribution.

title: Associations between countermovement jump impulse and running kinetics following ACL reconstruction.
authors: Ghani S, Lucron EM, Chan LY, Paton B.
abstract: Persistent deficits in lower-limb loading are commonly observed following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and may influence running biomechanics. Countermovement jump (CMJ) impulse can provide a phase-specific measure of force-time characteristics to reflect limb loading capacity; however, its relationship with running kinetics remains unclear. This study aimed to quantify phase-specific CMJ impulse following ACLR and examine associations with vertical ground reaction force (vGRF) metrics during treadmill running at the return-to-running phase. Forty-two participants performed three unilateral and bilateral CMJs on dual force plates and ran at 8 km/hr on an instrumented treadmill. Concentric, eccentric braking, and landing impulses were calculated. Running variables included weight acceptance rate, weight acceptance peak force, and maximum applied force. Inter-limb differences were assessed using Wilcoxon/paired t-tests. Impulse-vGRF relationships were analysed using Pearson/Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression. The ACLR limb exhibited significant deficits across all unilateral and bilateral CMJ phases, except for unilateral landing impulse. Deficits were greatest for unilateral concentric impulse (Δ1.3Ns·kg -0.67 , d = 1.49, p 2 = 0.25, p 2 = 0.38, p 2 = 0.37, p < 0.001). No meaningful relationships were observed for eccentric impulses or weight acceptance rate metrics. These findings indicate that jump impulse testing may provide clinically relevant indicators of running kinetics.

title: Arthroscopic Technique for Anterior Calcaneal Process Avulsion Fractures and Bifurcate Ligament Injuries Using Suture Tape Augmentation.
authors: Díaz-Fernández R.
abstract: Avulsion fractures of the anterior process of the calcaneus are frequently associated with injury to the bifurcate ligament and may result in persistent lateral midfoot pain and instability. Although open fixation or fragment excision has traditionally been used, these approaches may fail to restore ligamentous function and joint stability. Arthroscopic techniques for combined management of bony and ligamentous pathology at the calcaneocuboid joint remain poorly described. We describe an arthroscopic technique for the management of anterior calcaneal process avulsion fractures associated with bifurcate ligament injury. The procedure combines endoscopic excision of symptomatic intra-articular fragments with internal brace augmentation of both limbs of the bifurcate ligament using suture tape fixation, preserving residual native fibers and restoring ligamentous stability. This arthroscopic technique allows minimally invasive management of combined osseous and ligamentous pathology of the calcaneocuboid joint, providing stable ligament augmentation while avoiding the morbidity of open surgery and rigid across-joint fixation. Arthroscopic bifurcate ligament internal brace augmentation may represent a valuable option for selected patients with symptomatic anterior calcaneal process avulsion fractures and associated midfoot instability.

title: Arthroscopic Repair of Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Tear: Transtibial Fixation With 2 Lasso-Loop Sutures and 1 Samsung Medical Center Sliding Knot for Tensioning Secured by a Tibial Button.
authors: Arican N, Guven S, Karaman Y, Atalay M, Bingol I.
abstract: Medial meniscus posterior root tears disrupt the circumferential load-transmission function of the meniscus and negatively affect knee biomechanics. This technical note describes a reliable and reproducible arthroscopic repair technique using 2 lasso-loop sutures and 1 Samsung Medical Center sliding knot through a single transtibial tunnel, secured with a tibial cortical button, emphasizing controlled anatomic reduction and balanced tensioning at the meniscus-suture interface. This method provides strong tissue capture and secure tibial fixation while allowing controlled footprint restoration and minimizing suture loosening or cut-through, thereby enabling anatomic reduction of the meniscal root.

title: Are Cannabis and Cannabinoids a Valid Treatment Option in Patients with Rheumatic Diseases? A narrative review.
authors: Perrot S.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate current evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of cannabis and cannabinoids in patients with rheumatic diseases. Methods A narrative review was conducted based on a search for studies published between 2000 and 2026 evaluating cannabinoid therapies in rheumatic diseases. Results We identified 17 preclinical studies on the mechanisms of action of cannabis and 43 clinical studies published between 2000 and 2026, including randomized trials, observational studies and systematic reviews. We identified two articles on rheumatoid arthritis, 10 on osteoarthritis (2 reviews and 8 clinical studies), 28 on fibromyalgia (9 reviews, 7 randomized control trials, 12 clinical studies), one on psoriatic arthritis, and one on systemic sclerosis. The evidence of an effect of cannabinoids was strongest for fibromyalgia and limited for rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis. Most studies reported improvements in pain and sleep quality. Globally, cannabinoids were well tolerated. Conclusion Some studies suggest short-term symptomatic benefits of cannabinoid-based therapies, particularly in fibromyalgia, but the findings are inconsistent and limited by small samples, heterogeneous formulations, and risk of bias. Current evidence is insufficient to support routine clinical use or recommendations in rheumatic diseases.
